Right-sided respiratory crackles

data.description: A 67-year-old man with advanced alcoholic cirrhosis presented with progressive dyspnea. Physical examination after thoracentesis revealed right lung crackles, and the patient developed coughing, tachypnea, and tachycardia. His oxygen saturation was 82% while breathing ambient air.
Acute noncardiogenic pulmonary edema that can occur after rapid drainage of a large pleural effusion or pneumothorax, typically affecting the re-expanded lung.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypoxemia with oxygen saturation of 82% on room air
Imaging consistent with unilateral right-lung air-space opacity after pleural fluid drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Advanced alcoholic cirrhosis is a predisposing condition for pleural effusion but is not itself a typical feature of re-expansion pulmonary edema

data.description: Infection or chemical lung injury caused by inhalation of gastric or oropharyngeal contents, often producing dependent unilateral infiltrates and hypoxemic respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided pulmonary infiltrate or consolidation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt symptom development immediately after thoracentesis
No fever reported
No purulent sputum reported
No aspiration event reported

data.description: Acute infectious inflammation of lung parenchyma that commonly causes cough, dyspnea, hypoxemia, crackles, and focal consolidation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No chills reported
No sputum production reported
Temporal association with thoracentesis is more suggestive of a procedure-related complication

data.description: Pulmonary fluid accumulation caused by elevated cardiac filling pressures, usually due to acute heart failure; it typically produces bilateral interstitial or alveolar edema.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary air-space opacity compatible with edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly unilateral right-lung involvement rather than typical bilateral edema
Onset directly after thoracentesis
No history of heart failure reported
No peripheral edema, elevated jugular venous pressure, or chest pain reported

data.description: 52-year-old woman with exertional right buttock and thigh pain that resolves within 2 minutes of rest. Exercise tolerance worsened over past year, now limited to several blocks. Previously able to run 5-6 miles per day. Recently diagnosed hypertension controlled with lisinopril (5 mg daily). No other cardiovascular risk factors. Physical exam shows blood pressure 124/76 mm Hg bilaterally, high-pitched systolic bruit over right subcostal region and umbilicus, normal peripheral pulses. Ankle brachial index (ABI) at rest borderline normal (0.91) on right and normal (1.03) on left. Remainder of examination normal.

A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder causing alternating stenosis and dilation ('string-of-beads' appearance), which can involve renal and iliac arteries. Iliac involvement can cause exertional claudication, while renal involvement can cause hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional right buttock and thigh pain
Pain reliably resolves within minutes of rest, consistent with vascular claudication
Relatively few conventional atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk factors
Normal peripheral pulses despite proximal iliac arterial disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are atypical; the presentation is highly compatible with iliac and possible renal artery fibromuscular dysplasia

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic fibrotic narrowing of the external iliac artery, classically occurring in endurance athletes and producing exercise-induced buttock, thigh, or leg claudication with near-normal resting vascular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive exercise-induced buttock and thigh pain
Rapid relief of pain with rest
Marked decline from prior running capacity
Borderline or normal resting ankle-brachial index can occur because obstruction becomes more significant during exercise
Lack of typical atherosclerotic risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypertension is not usually caused by isolated external iliac endofibrosis
Abdominal/right subcostal bruit is less typical unless there is additional arterial involvement

data.diagnosis: Aortoiliac peripheral artery disease causing vascular claudication
data.description: Narrowing of the aortoiliac arteries reduces blood flow during exertion, producing buttock, hip, or thigh claudication. It is most commonly due to atherosclerosis but may also result from nonatherosclerotic arterial disease.
symptoms_in_common: Buttock and thigh claudication with walking or exertion
Hypertension as a vascular risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: She has few other conventional atherosclerotic risk factors
Normal peripheral pulses are less typical in more advanced aortoiliac atherosclerotic disease
Prior ability to run long distances and relatively young age make typical atherosclerotic disease less likely
Possible beaded arterial morphology would favor fibromuscular dysplasia rather than atherosclerosis

data.diagnosis: Lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication
data.description: Degenerative narrowing of the lumbar spinal canal can cause exertional buttock and thigh discomfort, often worsened by standing or walking and relieved by sitting or spinal flexion.
symptoms_in_common: Buttock and thigh pain with walking
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain resolves within approximately 2 minutes of rest, which is more characteristic of vascular claudication
No report of relief specifically with sitting or leaning forward
No back pain, numbness, weakness, or neurologic findings
Abdominal systolic bruit is not explained by spinal stenosis
Borderline-low right ankle-brachial index suggests vascular disease
Hypertension and possible arterial imaging abnormalities are not explained by spinal stenosis

diagnoses.name: External iliac artery dissection
diagnoses.title: Aneurysm or dissection of iliac artery[External iliac artery]

data.description: A 66-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with episodes of palpitations, dizziness, and near fainting that had lasted for a few hours. Her medical history included removal of a left atrial myxoma 15 years ago, after which she experienced recurrent atrial tachycardia managed with modified release verapamil 240 mg once daily. She had recently started sotalol 120 mg twice daily in addition to verapamil and underwent direct current cardioversion for persistent atrial tachycardia one week prior to presentation. Initial workup showed normal urea and electrolytes including magnesium. An echocardiogram revealed normal left ventricular systolic function with no recurrence of left atrial myxoma.

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced acquired long QT syndrome with torsades de pointes
data.description: A potentially life-threatening polymorphic ventricular tachycardia caused by QT prolongation, commonly triggered by QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic drugs such as sotalol. Concomitant rate-slowing therapy and post-cardioversion bradycardia can increase risk.
symptoms_in_common: Acute episodic onset over several hours
ECG appearance consistent with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal magnesium and other electrolytes
Normal left ventricular systolic function

data.description: A rapid ventricular rhythm with beat-to-beat variation in QRS morphology. When associated with prolonged QT interval it is termed torsades de pointes; it can cause hypotension, syncope, or sudden cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: ECG showing a broad-complex tachycardia with changing QRS morphology
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented complete loss of consciousness
No reported chest pain
No reported cardiac arrest

data.description: An adverse antiarrhythmic effect in which sotalol prolongs ventricular repolarization and may provoke marked QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, bradyarrhythmia, or other ventricular arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms began after recently starting sotalol
Recent cardioversion, which may contribute to bradycardia and QT-related proarrhythmia
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal renal-related laboratory assessment as described
Normal electrolytes including magnesium

data.description: A supraventricular tachyarrhythmia arising from the atria, often causing palpitations, lightheadedness, and reduced exercise tolerance. Prior atrial surgery can predispose to recurrent atrial tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent persistent atrial tachycardia requiring cardioversion
symptoms_not_in_common: Near fainting is less typical unless the ventricular rate is very rapid or there is hemodynamic compromise
ECG appearance is more consistent with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia than atrial tachycardia
Recent sotalol use strongly raises concern for a drug-induced ventricular proarrhythmia

data.description: 18-year-old pregnant woman. Healthy with no history of smoking, drug abuse, or family history of chromosomal disease or encephalodysplasia. Experienced mild flu-like symptoms during first month of pregnancy that resolved after three days without medication.

30-year-old male with 6 weeks of low-grade fever, fatigue, and progressive polyarthritis involving large joints of the arms and legs, without small joint involvement or diurnal variation. No significant past medical history, tuberculosis contact, or high-risk sexual behavior. Examination showed fever (38.9°C), multiple tender dull red nodules on the forehead, left cheek, and sternum, a solitary 1×1 cm firm right cervical lymph node, active bilateral arthritis of the knees, hips, and elbows, and hepatomegaly with the liver palpable 4 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies showed normal blood counts, ESR 6 mm/h, CRP 131 mg/L, and negative ANA, RF, ANCA, ASO, anti-DNase B, blood cultures, gonococcal and syphilis tests; serum calcium and ACE were normal.

data.diagnosis: Systemic sarcoidosis with acute sarcoid arthritis (Lofgren-spectrum presentation)
data.description: A multisystem granulomatous inflammatory disease characterized by noncaseating granulomas, commonly involving intrathoracic lymph nodes, skin, joints, liver, and lymph nodes. Acute sarcoid arthritis can present with fever, erythematous nodules, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, and polyarthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph
Histology suggestive of noncaseating granulomatous inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Arthritis involving hips and elbows rather than the more typical ankle-predominant arthritis of classic Lofgren syndrome
Normal ESR despite markedly elevated CRP
Male sex, as acute Lofgren syndrome is more common in women

data.diagnosis: Tuberculosis with erythema nodosum and reactive polyarthritis
data.description: Tuberculosis can cause constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, granulomatous inflammation, erythema nodosum, and inflammatory arthritis. Tuberculous arthritis is usually chronic and commonly affects one joint, while reactive arthritis may be polyarticular.
symptoms_in_common: Tender erythematous nodules that could represent erythema nodosum
symptoms_not_in_common: No known tuberculosis contact
No pulmonary infiltrate, cavitation, or pleural effusion described
Symmetric active polyarthritis of several large joints is less typical than chronic monoarthritis in tuberculous arthritis
Normal ESR is atypical in active disseminated tuberculosis
Chest radiograph appearance of bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is more suggestive of sarcoidosis

data.description: An autoinflammatory systemic disorder causing fever, inflammatory polyarthritis, rash, lymphadenopathy, and hepatomegaly. It typically produces high spiking quotidian fever and a transient salmon-pink rash.
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is low-grade rather than typical high quotidian spiking fever
Skin lesions are tender dull red nodules rather than an evanescent salmon-pink maculopapular rash
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is not a typical feature
Granulomatous inflammation is not characteristic
Normal blood counts are less typical because neutrophilic leukocytosis is common

data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis occurring after gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection, usually affecting lower-limb joints asymmetrically and sometimes accompanied by mucocutaneous findings.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory arthritis affecting large lower-limb joints, especially knees and hips
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection reported
Arthritis includes upper-limb joints and is bilateral/polyarticular rather than typically asymmetric oligoarthritis
Tender facial and sternal nodules are not typical
Cervical lymphadenopathy and hepatomegaly are not typical
Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and granulomatous inflammation are not typical

data.diagnosis: Disseminated fungal infection with granulomatous disease (for example histoplasmosis)
data.description: Disseminated fungal infections can produce prolonged fever, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, pulmonary hilar lymph node enlargement, skin lesions, and granulomatous inflammation, particularly in immunocompromised individuals.
symptoms_not_in_common: No immunocompromising condition reported
Normal blood counts are less typical in disseminated fungal infection
Prominent inflammatory polyarthritis is less typical
No pulmonary respiratory symptoms reported
No fungal exposure history provided

data.description: 13-year-old girl with a multiply recurrent hypothalamic/chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases. Had never received steroids or bisphosphonates. After 16 courses of treatment, complained of wrist pain. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation of the left dorsal wrist with decreased range of motion.

Anti-VEGF therapy such as bevacizumab can disrupt endochondral bone formation in growing children, producing widened, irregular, or painful physes, often involving the distal radius or other rapidly growing bones.
symptoms_in_common: Wrist pain after multiple treatment courses
MRI abnormality centered near the distal radial physis
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiply recurrent hypothalamic-chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma
Ventricular metastases

data.description: A repetitive mechanical stress injury of the distal radial growth plate that can cause physeal widening, irregularity, local pain, and reduced wrist motion. It is classically seen in young athletes but may also occur in medically vulnerable children with altered bone health.
symptoms_in_common: Skeletal immaturity with an open distal radial physis
Imaging abnormality at the distal radial growth plate
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported repetitive athletic loading or trauma
Cancer treatment history is not a typical cause
Hypothalamic-chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases

data.diagnosis: Osteonecrosis (avascular necrosis) involving the distal radius/carpal region
data.description: Osteonecrosis is bone death caused by impaired blood supply. It can occur in children receiving cancer therapy, particularly with corticosteroid exposure, and may present with focal joint pain and restricted motion; MRI can detect early changes.
symptoms_not_in_common: She had never received steroids, a major common risk factor for treatment-associated osteonecrosis
The described MRI finding is centered at the growth plate rather than showing a classic subchondral osteonecrotic lesion
No reported joint collapse or chronic progressive joint dysfunction

data.description: 10-month-old male admitted with fever. Born at 38 weeks gestation after unremarkable pregnancy, birth weight 2,960g. History of cephalhematoma over parietooccipital region at birth, bilateral inguinal hernia repair at 2 months, recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection. Growth parameters below 3rd percentile (weight: 7,500g, length: 73.7cm). Physical exam showed pale skin, sparse/light/curly hair with pili torti on microscopy. Neurologic exam revealed diffuse hypotonia with poor head/trunk support, no visual fixing/following, hyperreflexic deep tendon reflexes bilaterally with ankle clonus, bilateral Babinski extension. Lab results: serum copper 27 μg/dL (normal 70-130), ceruloplasmin 9.07 μg/dL (normal 20-60).

An X-linked disorder of impaired intestinal copper transport causing severe systemic copper deficiency, neurodegeneration, connective-tissue abnormalities, characteristic sparse kinky hair, and tortuous cerebral vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with onset in the first year of life
Sparse, light, curly hair with pili torti on microscopy
Failure to thrive and growth below the 3rd percentile
Diffuse hypotonia and poor head/trunk control
Hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and bilateral Babinski signs
Recurrent infections including pneumonia and urinary tract infection
Bilateral inguinal hernias suggesting connective-tissue fragility
MRI findings compatible with cerebral ischemic injury and vascular tortuosity
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever at admission is not a defining manifestation, although infection-related fever can occur

data.diagnosis: Occipital horn syndrome (milder ATP7A-related copper transport disorder)
data.description: A milder allelic form of ATP7A-related copper transport disease characterized primarily by connective-tissue manifestations, vascular tortuosity, bladder diverticula, joint laxity, and occipital bone exostoses.
symptoms_in_common: Possible vascular tortuosity on brain vascular imaging
Hypotonia and developmental impairment may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe early infantile neurologic deterioration is more typical of classic Menkes disease than occipital horn syndrome
Marked pili torti and sparse kinky hair are more characteristic of classic Menkes disease
No occipital horns or occipital bone exostoses are described
No bladder diverticula, joint laxity, or skin hyperextensibility are described
Severe failure to thrive and recurrent infections are less characteristic

data.diagnosis: Acquired copper deficiency due to malnutrition or impaired intestinal absorption
data.description: Low copper levels can result from inadequate dietary intake, prolonged parenteral nutrition without adequate supplementation, malabsorption, or intestinal disease; it may cause anemia, neutropenia, poor growth, and neurologic dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and neurologic impairment can occur in severe deficiency
Recurrent infections can occur if associated neutropenia is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Pili torti and sparse light kinky hair are not typical of acquired nutritional copper deficiency
Cephalhematoma and inguinal hernias are not typical features
Severe early-onset spastic upper motor neuron signs are less typical
Cerebral arterial tortuosity is not typical
No dietary deficiency, parenteral nutrition history, malabsorption syndrome, or gastrointestinal disease is described

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial membrane protein-associated neurodegeneration / mitochondrial disorder with secondary copper abnormalities
data.description: Mitochondrial disorders may present in infancy with failure to thrive, hypotonia, developmental delay, recurrent illness, and neuroimaging abnormalities, although they do not usually cause the distinctive Menkes hair phenotype or profound copper transport defect.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse hypotonia and poor head control
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly low serum copper and ceruloplasmin are not typical primary findings
Pili torti with sparse light curly hair is not typical
Inguinal hernias and cephalhematoma are not typical hallmark features
Tortuous cerebral arteries are not a typical general mitochondrial finding
No lactic acidosis, metabolic acidosis, cardiomyopathy, hepatic dysfunction, or characteristic mitochondrial biochemical findings are provided

data.description: 47-year-old female with an incidentally found right adrenal mass noted 3 years ago, initially 2.2 × 3.1 cm and untreated, now enlarged on CT 10 days ago to 5.8 × 4.7 cm. She has remained asymptomatic throughout. Past history is negative for hypertension, diabetes, cardiac, pulmonary, and cerebrovascular disease; no smoking or alcohol use. Menstrual flow is reduced. Physical examination was unremarkable, with normal vital signs, normal cardiopulmonary exam, and a soft, non-tender abdomen without palpable masses or bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness.

A rare adrenal cortical tumor composed of oncocytic cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm. Most are nonfunctioning and incidentally discovered, although some can enlarge substantially and require surgical removal to exclude malignant potential.
symptoms_in_common: No diabetes or other signs of cortisol excess
Progressive enlargement of a nonfunctioning-appearing adrenal lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical feature of a nonfunctioning adrenocortical oncocytoma

data.description: A common benign tumor of the adrenal cortex. Many adenomas are nonfunctioning incidental findings, while some produce cortisol or aldosterone.
symptoms_in_common: No abdominal pain or palpable mass
No obvious clinical features of hormone excess
symptoms_not_in_common: Growth from 2.2 × 3.1 cm to 5.8 × 4.7 cm over 3 years is less typical for a benign adrenal adenoma
A lesion larger than 5 cm is less typical for a routine adrenal adenoma
Reduced menstrual flow is not typical

data.description: A rare malignant tumor of the adrenal cortex that may be hormonally functional or nonfunctional. It often presents as a large, enlarging adrenal mass and can be asymptomatic when nonfunctional.
symptoms_in_common: Documented increase in tumor size over time
Possible asymptomatic presentation when the tumor is nonfunctioning
No hypertension or overt endocrine syndrome does not exclude a nonfunctioning carcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal or flank pain
No palpable abdominal mass
No weight loss or systemic symptoms reported
No virilization, Cushingoid features, or other overt steroid-hormone excess
Reduced menstrual flow alone is not a classic presentation

data.description: A catecholamine-producing tumor of adrenal medullary chromaffin cells. Some pheochromocytomas are clinically silent, but most cause episodic or persistent catecholamine-related symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Can be asymptomatic in a minority of cases
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension
No episodic headache
No palpitations
No sweating episodes
No tremor, anxiety attacks, or tachycardia reported
Reduced menstrual flow is not typical

data.description: A rare benign vascular adrenal lesion that is often nonfunctioning and incidentally found. It can become large and may show heterogeneous imaging features due to hemorrhage, thrombosis, or calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Normal physical examination and vital signs
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive growth raises concern but is not specific for hemangioma
Reduced menstrual flow is not a typical feature

data.description: 34-year-old white male presented with an indurated plaque on the forehead that extended onto the scalp over approximately 1 year. Initial laboratory findings showed positive antinuclear antibodies (1:200) and slightly increased C3d complement; other laboratory tests were normal.
A localized scleroderma subtype causing a linear, indurated, sclerotic plaque on the forehead and scalp, often associated with scalp atrophy and scarring alopecia.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive indurated plaque over approximately 1 year
Linear lesion involving the forehead and extending onto the scalp
Pink to ivory-colored, sclerotic-appearing plaque with reduced hair density
Positive antinuclear antibodies can occur in localized scleroderma
Histology appears consistent with dermal sclerosis and inflammatory infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical systemic sclerosis features such as Raynaud phenomenon, sclerodactyly, dysphagia, or internal-organ involvement were reported

data.description: A deeper variant of localized scleroderma involving the deep dermis, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, or muscle, producing marked induration and tethering of skin.
symptoms_in_common: Histologic involvement of deep dermal and subcutaneous tissue with sclerosis
Associated inflammatory infiltrate around deeper structures
symptoms_not_in_common: The sharply linear forehead-to-scalp distribution is more characteristic of en coup de sabre linear morphea
No limb, trunk, joint-contracture, or deep-muscle involvement was reported

data.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus manifestation characterized by inflammation of subcutaneous fat, which can cause firm plaques, lipoatrophy, and scarring alopecia when affecting the scalp.
symptoms_in_common: Possible alopecia over the involved area
Deep inflammatory infiltrates involving subcutaneous tissue may be present histologically
symptoms_not_in_common: The linear forehead-to-scalp configuration is not typical
No photosensitivity, discoid plaques, dyspigmentation, systemic lupus symptoms, or other lupus laboratory abnormalities were reported
Prominent dermal sclerosis favors morphea rather than lupus panniculitis

data.description: An autoimmune connective-tissue disorder characterized by widespread skin thickening and fibrosis, vascular abnormalities, and potential internal-organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Complement abnormality may occur in autoimmune connective-tissue disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion is localized to the forehead and scalp rather than widespread
No Raynaud phenomenon, finger skin thickening, digital ulcers, telangiectasias, or internal-organ manifestations were reported
The focal linear plaque pattern is much more typical of localized scleroderma

data.description: A 14-year-old girl with no prior medical history presented to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain for 2 days, accompanied by non-bilious vomiting. Physical examination revealed pallor, diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding, and sluggish bowel sounds but no rigidity. Her recent history included two episodes of multiple oral ulcers that had resolved spontaneously. Laboratory findings showed hemoglobin 88 g/L, total leucocyte count 3.6 × 10⁹/L, platelets 96 × 10⁹/L, and ESR 54 mm/h. Urinalysis was normal, and blood and urine cultures were sterile. Initial ANA testing by indirect immunofluorescence with HEp-2 cell substrate was negative. Subsequent repeat ANA testing at a different laboratory remained negative, but dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies were strongly positive with low concentrations of C3 and C4. Echocardiography showed a mild pericardial effusion.

data.diagnosis: ANA-negative systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus enteritis (mesenteric vasculitis)
data.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus is a multisystem autoimmune disease. Rarely, ANA can be negative despite strongly positive anti-dsDNA/anti-Ro antibodies. Lupus enteritis, often due to immune-complex-mediated mesenteric vasculitis, causes acute abdominal pain, vomiting, bowel-wall edema, and possible ileus.
symptoms_in_common: Severe diffuse abdominal pain with guarding
Sluggish bowel sounds and radiographic features compatible with ileus or bowel edema
Low C3 and C4 complement concentrations
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeatedly negative ANA by HEp-2 indirect immunofluorescence
Normal urinalysis without evidence of lupus nephritis

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with lupus serositis and intestinal pseudo-obstruction
data.description: Lupus can cause inflammation of serosal surfaces, including pericarditis and peritonitis, and can occasionally produce intestinal pseudo-obstruction from intestinal smooth-muscle dysfunction, vasculitis, or associated bowel-wall edema.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal distension or obstructive bowel pattern on imaging
Pancytopenia pattern with anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported constipation or obstipation
No reported urinary tract dilatation or hydronephrosis, which can accompany lupus pseudo-obstruction
Repeated ANA negativity is unusual in SLE

data.description: Behçet disease is an inflammatory vasculitic disorder characterized by recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, eye inflammation, skin lesions, and sometimes gastrointestinal ulceration or vascular inflammation causing abdominal pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: No genital ulcers reported
No uveitis or other eye inflammation reported
No characteristic skin lesions reported
Anemia, leukopenia, and thrombocytopenia are not typical core features
Strong anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro positivity are not typical
Low C3 and C4 complement levels are not typical
Pericardial effusion is uncommon

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa or another medium-vessel systemic vasculitis with mesenteric involvement
data.description: Medium-vessel vasculitis can affect mesenteric arteries, producing severe abdominal pain, vomiting, intestinal ischemia, bowel-wall edema, and inflammatory marker elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Possible imaging evidence of bowel-wall edema or mesenteric inflammatory involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent oral ulcers are not characteristic
Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia are not typical
Strong anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibody positivity is not typical
Low complement levels are less typical
Mild pericardial effusion is less typical
No reported hypertension, renal impairment, neuropathy, skin nodules, purpura, or livedo reticularis

data.description: 41-year-old woman presented with chest pain. One year earlier, she had transient left chest and shoulder tightness. Five days before presentation, she developed acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders with dyspnea while packing for a flight; it lasted 1 hour and resolved spontaneously. The day before presentation, similar pain recurred after walking, accompanied by light-headedness and dyspnea. Past history included laparoscopy for an ovarian cyst and miscarriage 1 month earlier. Family history was notable for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in her mother, brother, and sister, and a maternal second cousin who died of a cerebral aneurysm at age 51. On examination, she was diaphoretic; vital signs were temperature 36.6°C, heart rate 68, blood pressure 143/87 mmHg bilaterally, respiratory rate 18, and oxygen saturation 100%, with no cardiac murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Troponin T was 0.03 ng/mL on presentation and 0.21 ng/mL 8 hours later.

A nonatherosclerotic tear or intramural hematoma in a coronary artery causing narrowing of the vessel lumen and acute myocardial ischemia; it is more common in younger women and may be associated with pregnancy-related hormonal changes and connective-tissue disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Rising troponin T consistent with myocardial injury
Young woman without described atherosclerotic risk factors
Family history of a heritable connective-tissue disorder
Coronary angiographic appearance suggestive of coronary dissection
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are clearly atypical; the prior transient chest and shoulder tightness may represent earlier ischemic episodes rather than typical abrupt SCAD presentation

data.diagnosis: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) secondary to SCAD
data.description: Acute myocardial infarction without persistent ST-segment elevation, caused here most plausibly by reduced coronary blood flow from spontaneous coronary artery dissection rather than plaque rupture.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged substernal chest pain lasting approximately 1 hour
Pain radiating to jaw and shoulders
Troponin T rise from 0.03 to 0.21 ng/mL
ECG changes compatible with myocardial ischemia without clear persistent ST-elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 41 and lack of documented conventional coronary atherosclerotic risk factors are less typical for plaque-related NSTEMI
Family history of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome suggests a nonatherosclerotic mechanism rather than typical plaque rupture

data.description: A heritable connective-tissue disorder, usually related to pathogenic COL3A1 variants, characterized by arterial fragility, arterial aneurysm or dissection, organ rupture, and pregnancy-related complications. Coronary and renal/visceral arterial involvement can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Coronary artery dissection/arterial fragility causing acute coronary syndrome
Family history of cerebral aneurysm in a relative
Recent miscarriage, which can occur more often in some heritable connective-tissue disorders
Imaging findings suggestive of abnormalities in additional medium-sized arteries, including renal/visceral arterial involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thin translucent skin, characteristic facial appearance, easy bruising, bowel rupture, uterine rupture, or prior major arterial rupture
The known family diagnosis is hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, which is distinct from vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arteriopathy of medium-sized arteries, particularly renal and carotid arteries, that can cause arterial stenosis, aneurysm, dissection, and tortuosity. It has a strong association with SCAD in women.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent renal/visceral arterial irregularity or beading on vascular imaging
Possible multi-arterial involvement without atherosclerotic risk factors
Mildly elevated blood pressure, which can occur with renal artery involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported resistant hypertension
No reported headaches, pulsatile tinnitus, carotid bruit, transient neurologic symptoms, or cervical artery dissection
The chest pain and troponin elevation are due to coronary ischemia rather than typical primary renal or carotid FMD symptoms

data.description: Patient is a 2 month-old male, full-term infant, with severe malnutrition and failure to thrive, admitted to the intensive care unit, with long term feeding difficulties. The study was performed initially to rule out malrotation.

data.diagnosis: Intestinal malrotation with intermittent midgut volvulus
data.description: Congenital abnormal positioning and fixation of the intestine that can predispose to twisting of the midgut around the mesenteric vessels. Upper GI contrast studies may show an abnormal duodenojejunal junction and a corkscrew configuration of the proximal small bowel.
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious vomiting is reported
No acute abdominal distension or shock is reported

data.description: Progressive thickening of the pyloric muscle causing gastric outlet obstruction, usually affecting young male infants between 2 and 8 weeks of age. It can lead to poor intake, dehydration, and poor weight gain.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent non-bilious projectile vomiting is reported
No dehydration or hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis is reported

data.diagnosis: Congenital duodenal web or partial duodenal obstruction
data.description: A congenital membrane within the duodenum that partially obstructs passage of feeds. Partial webs may present later than complete duodenal atresia with chronic feeding intolerance and poor growth.
symptoms_not_in_common: No bilious vomiting is reported
No abdominal distension is reported

data.diagnosis: Gastroesophageal reflux disease with feeding aversion
data.description: Reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus can cause feeding refusal, irritability, recurrent regurgitation, and inadequate caloric intake. Severe cases may lead to poor weight gain.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent regurgitation or vomiting is reported
No irritability, choking, cough, or aspiration symptoms are reported

data.description: 47-year-old man with hypertension presented with 3 days of left periorbital swelling, throat tightness, hoarseness, and dysphagia to solids with a sensation of food sticking. He denied pruritus, visual symptoms, pain, wheezing, shortness of breath, fever, or recent illness. Exam showed hoarse, muffled voice; edema around the left eye with faint erythema; mildly diffusely enlarged tongue; no ptosis, normal extraocular movements, reactive pupils, and no stridor. Two weeks later he developed worsening dysphonia, increased throat swelling sensation, nasal regurgitation of liquids, shoulder and hip pain, and difficulty jumping. Re-examination showed anterior and lateral neck tenderness, subcutaneous edema of both upper arms, normal arm strength, reduced hip strength, and difficulty rising from a seated position. Labs showed elevated ALT, AST, and creatine kinase, mildly elevated ESR and CRP, positive ANA (1:160), and negative myositis-specific antibodies. Muscle biopsy from the left deltoid showed mild fiber size variability, epimysial perivascular inflammatory infiltrates, and patchy MHC class I staining on nonnecrotic fibers.

A rare, severe variant of dermatomyositis characterized by inflammatory myopathy with prominent subcutaneous edema, often involving the face, limbs, and neck, with possible bulbar and respiratory muscle involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Periorbital edema with faint erythema suggestive of a heliotrope-type eruption
Progressive proximal muscle weakness involving the hips and difficulty rising from a seated position
Dysphagia, nasal regurgitation of liquids, throat tightness, and sensation of food sticking
Dysphonia, hoarseness, and muffled voice from pharyngeal/laryngeal muscle involvement
Tongue, facial, neck, and upper-arm subcutaneous edema
Elevated creatine kinase, AST, and ALT
Muscle biopsy with perivascular inflammatory infiltrates and MHC class I expression on nonnecrotic fibers
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly described Gottron papules
No clearly described shawl sign or V-sign rash
Initial unilateral periorbital swelling is less typical than bilateral facial edema
No pruritus

data.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory myopathy causing symmetric proximal muscle weakness and elevated muscle enzymes; dysphagia may occur due to pharyngeal muscle involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive hip weakness and difficulty rising from a seated position
Dysphagia and nasal regurgitation due to bulbar muscle weakness
Elevated creatine kinase, AST, and ALT
Inflammatory changes and MHC class I staining on muscle biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent periorbital, tongue, neck, and upper-arm subcutaneous edema is unusual
Faint erythema around the eye may suggest dermatomyositis rather than polymyositis
Very prominent early facial and oropharyngeal swelling is atypical
Biopsy lacks the classic endomysial CD8-positive invasion of nonnecrotic muscle fibers expected in polymyositis

data.description: A severe autoimmune myopathy that usually produces marked proximal weakness and substantial creatine kinase elevation, sometimes with dysphagia; biopsy typically shows prominent muscle necrosis with relatively little inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Difficulty rising from a seated position and difficulty jumping
symptoms_not_in_common: Periorbital and generalized subcutaneous edema are not typical
Tongue and pharyngeal soft-tissue edema are unusual
Muscle biopsy shows perivascular inflammation rather than prominent myofiber necrosis
No mention of anti-SRP or anti-HMGCR antibodies
Faint periorbital erythema is more suggestive of dermatomyositis

data.description: Acute localized swelling of the skin and mucosal tissues, often affecting the face, tongue, and upper airway; it may be histamine-mediated or bradykinin-mediated, including medication-associated angioedema.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of pruritus, which can occur in bradykinin-mediated angioedema
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive proximal hip weakness
Difficulty rising from a seated position and difficulty jumping
Shoulder and hip pain
Elevated creatine kinase
Inflammatory muscle biopsy findings
Persistent and progressive muscle-related symptoms over two weeks
Upper-arm subcutaneous edema associated with objective myopathy

data.description: 11-year-old boy who received his first black henna tattoo while on holiday in Portugal in August 2013. One week after getting the tattoo, the area became hot, red, raised and itchy. Physical exam showed bullae with clear yellow-orange discharge and golden crusting on a background of erythematous plaque.

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis to paraphenylenediamine (PPD) in black henna tattoo
data.description: A delayed type IV hypersensitivity reaction caused by PPD, a chemical commonly added to black henna to darken the color and shorten application time. It often produces a sharply localized eczematous or blistering eruption matching the tattoo design.
symptoms_in_common: Reaction began about one week after black henna tattoo application
Erythematous plaque localized to the tattooed area
symptoms_not_in_common: Clear yellow-orange discharge
Golden crusting, which suggests possible secondary bacterial infection

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis to black henna with secondary impetiginization
data.description: Severe PPD-induced allergic contact dermatitis that has become secondarily infected with bacteria, commonly Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes. This can cause weeping, yellow discharge, and honey-colored crusts over an eczematous tattoo-shaped rash.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed onset after exposure to black henna tattoo
Erythematous plaque in the tattoo distribution

data.description: A superficial bacterial skin infection, usually caused by toxin-producing Staphylococcus aureus, characterized by fragile blisters that rupture and leave erosions with yellow or golden crusting.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked itch is less characteristic than in allergic contact dermatitis
Precise localization in the shape of a recently applied tattoo
Delayed onset specifically following black henna exposure

data.diagnosis: Irritant contact dermatitis from tattoo dye or application chemicals
data.description: Inflammation caused by direct chemical injury to the skin from substances in tattoo dye, solvents, or additives. It can produce redness, burning, swelling, and occasionally blistering at the contact site.
symptoms_in_common: Red, raised, warm skin at the site of tattoo exposure
Localized eruption corresponding to the exposure area
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset one week after exposure is more typical of allergic than irritant dermatitis
Prominent itching favors allergic contact dermatitis
Golden crusting and yellow-orange discharge suggest secondary infection rather than uncomplicated irritant dermatitis

data.description: 59-year-old man with multiple nodules on his joints. Patient had history of gouty arthritis (confirmed by visualization of negative birefringent crystals in joint aspirate), hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Physical examination showed multiple gouty nodules in the auricle, knee, ankle, and toe joints, with severe loss of flexion and extension in hands. Laboratory findings showed elevated creatine (137 μmol/L; normal range 62–115 μmol/L) and uric acid (725 μmol/L; normal range 208–428 μmol/L).
Advanced gout caused by chronic deposition of monosodium urate crystals in joints and soft tissues, producing visible tophi, joint destruction, and loss of function.
symptoms_in_common: History of gouty arthritis confirmed by negatively birefringent crystals in joint aspirate
Multiple nodules involving the fingers and hand joints
Tophi in the auricle, knee, ankle, and toe joints
Severe loss of hand flexion and extension due to chronic joint and soft-tissue involvement
Male sex and comorbid hypertension and type 2 diabetes, which are associated with gout
symptoms_not_in_common: Mildly elevated creatinine is not a defining manifestation, although renal impairment can coexist with gout

data.diagnosis: Tophaceous gout with severe gouty arthropathy of the hands
data.description: A severe deforming form of chronic gout in which large urate tophi accumulate around the small joints, tendons, and soft tissues of the hands, causing deformity and major restriction of motion.
symptoms_in_common: Large nodular deposits around multiple hand joints
Severe hand deformity with loss of flexion and extension
Extensive deposits at typical gout sites, including auricles, toes, ankles, and knees
Very high serum uric acid concentration
symptoms_not_in_common: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is not a direct manifestation of gouty arthropathy
Hypertension is not a direct manifestation of gouty arthropathy
Mild creatinine elevation is not required for the diagnosis

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that commonly affects the small joints of the hands symmetrically and can cause deformity, nodules, and impaired hand function.
symptoms_in_common: Severe bilateral hand dysfunction with reduced flexion and extension
Subcutaneous nodules can occur near pressure points in rheumatoid arthritis
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative birefringent crystals in synovial fluid strongly support gout rather than rheumatoid arthritis
Marked hyperuricemia is not typical of rheumatoid arthritis
Tophi involving the auricle, toe, ankle, and knee are characteristic of gout rather than rheumatoid nodules
Large chalky-appearing nodular deposits around the fingers are more typical of tophaceous gout
No reported symmetric inflammatory small-joint pain, prolonged morning stiffness, rheumatoid factor, or anti-CCP antibody findings

data.description: A crystal deposition disorder caused by calcium pyrophosphate crystals, usually producing acute or chronic arthritis and occasionally mass-like periarticular deposits.
symptoms_in_common: Older adult with multiple joint involvement
Knee and wrist/hand-region involvement can occur
Nodular periarticular crystal deposits can rarely mimic tophi
symptoms_not_in_common: The aspirate demonstrated negatively birefringent crystals, whereas calcium pyrophosphate crystals are typically weakly positively birefringent
Very high uric acid supports gout rather than calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease
Auricular and toe tophi are much more characteristic of chronic gout
Extensive large hand tophi and severe deforming gouty arthropathy are not typical presentations of pseudogout

data.description: A 25-year-old man was referred to the oncology unit with a three-week history of a progressively enlarging neck lump and atypical lymphoid cells found on fine needle aspiration cytology. He reported mild exertional dyspnea and drenching night sweats, but denied weight loss, occupational exposure to harmful substances, recent travel, or high-risk sexual behavior. He had a smoking history since age 16. On physical examination, a palpable right supraclavicular lymph node measuring 3 cm in diameter was found. Chest radiography revealed a widened mediastinum but no lung lesions. Core biopsy of the lymph node showed partial effacement of nodal architecture by scattered large cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells with some collagen fibrosis. These large cells stained positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A B-cell-derived lymphoma characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background; nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin lymphoma commonly affects young adults and often presents with mediastinal and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging right supraclavicular lymph node
Widened mediastinum/mediastinal mass on chest imaging
Mild exertional dyspnea from mediastinal involvement
Large atypical lymphoid cells on cytology
Large cells positive for CD15 and CD30
Reactive background with lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells
Collagen fibrosis, supporting nodular sclerosis subtype
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss (weight loss may occur but is not required)
Smoking history (not a typical causative feature)

data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in the anterior mediastinum, usually in young adults, often causing a bulky mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Tumor cells positive for CD15 and CD30 with negative CD45, which is more characteristic of classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Prominent eosinophil-rich reactive background
Collagen fibrosis with scattered Reed-Sternberg-like cells
No reported expression of B-cell markers such as CD20, PAX5, or CD79a

data.description: A tumor derived from germ cells that can arise in the anterior mediastinum of young men and present as a mediastinal mass with respiratory symptoms and supraclavicular lymph node enlargement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Drenching night sweats are less typical
Lymph node biopsy showing atypical lymphoid cells rather than germ cell tumor morphology
CD15-positive and CD30-positive large cells with CD45 negativity in an inflammatory background
Reactive eosinophils, plasma cells, and collagen fibrosis suggest Hodgkin lymphoma rather than germ cell tumor

data.description: A 45-year-old man presented with dry cough and breathlessness. During the investigation, he was found to be infected with HIV. Physical examination and other baseline clinical details were not specifically described in this brief case report.

An opportunistic fungal pneumonia occurring most often in advanced HIV infection, typically causing diffuse bilateral interstitial or perihilar pulmonary infiltrates and progressive respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse/perihilar interstitial chest radiograph opacities

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the lungs, which is common in people with HIV and may have atypical radiographic appearances, including diffuse infiltrates or hilar involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry cough is less characteristic than a persistent productive cough
No fever, night sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, or prolonged constitutional symptoms were described

data.description: A lower respiratory infection caused by organisms such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, or respiratory viruses, often producing dry cough and diffuse or patchy interstitial infiltrates.
symptoms_not_in_common: HIV infection increases concern for opportunistic rather than routine atypical infection
No fever, sore throat, malaise, or other acute infectious symptoms were described

data.description: An opportunistic viral lung infection occurring primarily in severely immunocompromised individuals, including advanced HIV, and capable of causing diffuse interstitial lung infiltrates and hypoxemic breathlessness.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse bilateral interstitial chest radiograph abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic constitutional symptoms were described
CMV pneumonitis is less common than PJP as an isolated pulmonary presentation in HIV

data.description: A malignancy associated with human herpesvirus 8 in advanced HIV infection that can involve the lungs, producing cough, dyspnea, and bilateral perihilar or interstitial radiographic opacities.
symptoms_not_in_common: No skin or mucosal Kaposi lesions were described
No hemoptysis, pleural effusion, or known advanced AIDS features were described

data.description: A 65-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presented with a one-month history of worsening breathlessness and chest discomfort on walking. He came to hospital following a collapse that occurred after self-administering sublingual glyceryl trinitrate to relieve his symptoms. He reported no history of cough or coryza, had not lost weight, and experienced no haemoptysis. Laboratory testing revealed a raised serum D-dimer level.

Diffuse infiltration of pulmonary lymphatic vessels by metastatic carcinoma, often from lung, breast, stomach, pancreas, or prostate cancer. It commonly produces interlobular septal thickening and progressive breathlessness.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening breathlessness over one month
Heavy smoking history, increasing risk of underlying bronchogenic malignancy
CT appearance of prominent interlobular septal and peribronchovascular thickening in the right lung
Raised D-dimer, which can occur with malignancy-associated hypercoagulability
symptoms_not_in_common: Collapse immediately after sublingual glyceryl trinitrate is not a typical direct manifestation

data.description: A rare cancer-related condition in which microscopic tumor emboli obstruct small pulmonary arteries and trigger vascular remodeling, causing rapidly progressive dyspnea, pulmonary hypertension, and elevated coagulation markers.
symptoms_in_common: CT interstitial and vascular-appearing abnormalities that may include septal thickening and small branching centrilobular opacities
Possible occult malignancy despite no weight loss or haemoptysis
symptoms_not_in_common: The predominantly unilateral right-lung radiographic abnormality is less typical, as the process is often bilateral

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus, usually originating from deep veins, producing acute or subacute dyspnea, pleuritic or nonspecific chest pain, and occasionally syncope.
symptoms_not_in_common: One-month gradually progressive course rather than a clearly acute onset
Marked unilateral interlobular septal thickening/reticulonodular opacity is not a typical primary chest imaging finding of uncomplicated pulmonary embolism

data.diagnosis: Primary bronchogenic carcinoma with lymphangitic spread
data.description: Lung cancer, particularly adenocarcinoma in a smoker, may spread through pulmonary lymphatics before a dominant lung mass is apparent, causing progressive dyspnea and unilateral interstitial lung changes.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided diffuse interstitial abnormality on chest radiograph
Raised D-dimer, which may reflect cancer-associated thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No haemoptysis
No cough

data.description: Fluid accumulation in the lung interstitium and alveoli due to elevated cardiac filling pressures, commonly from left ventricular dysfunction or acute ischemic heart disease.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional chest discomfort that could reflect myocardial ischemia
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate, which can cause hypotension
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly unilateral right-sided interstitial abnormality is atypical for standard cardiogenic pulmonary edema
No reported orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea
Raised D-dimer is not a typical defining feature

data.description: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of shortness of breath and sore throat. Her medical history included smoking, obesity, type 2 diabetes On examination, her oxygen saturation was 81% on room air, dropping to 71% with exertion. She was afebrile with a normal white blood cell count. Chest examination revealed soft heart sounds, decreased air entry, wheeze, and aegophony at the lung bases bilaterally. Abdominal examination was normal except for obesity.

Loss of right phrenic nerve function causes elevation and reduced movement of the right hemidiaphragm, leading to compression of the right lung base and hypoxemic breathlessness. It may occur after viral illness or from other phrenic nerve injury.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased air entry at the lung bases
Elevated right hemidiaphragm with basal lung compression on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheeze
Aegophony at both lung bases

data.description: Diaphragmatic eventration is abnormal permanent elevation of part or all of a hemidiaphragm due to thinning or weakness of diaphragmatic muscle. It can reduce lung volume and cause dyspnea, particularly in obesity.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated right hemidiaphragm on chest radiograph and CT
Obesity, which can worsen restrictive respiratory impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute 1-week onset
Sore throat
Wheeze
Bilateral basal aegophony

data.diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
data.description: COPD exacerbation is an acute worsening of airflow limitation, often triggered by viral respiratory infection. Smoking is a major risk factor and patients may have wheeze, dyspnea, and hypoxemia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sore throat suggesting a viral respiratory trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with lung compression on imaging
Aegophony at both lung bases
No stated chronic cough or sputum production
No known prior COPD diagnosis

data.description: Pulmonary embolism is obstruction of pulmonary arterial blood flow, usually by thrombus, and may cause acute dyspnea and severe hypoxemia with relatively few chest examination findings.
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat preceding symptoms
Wheeze
Aegophony at both lung bases
Elevated right hemidiaphragm and apparent basal compressive change on imaging
No reported pleuritic chest pain, hemoptysis, tachycardia, or unilateral leg symptoms

data.description: Community-acquired pneumonia is infection of the lung parenchyma and can produce dyspnea, hypoxemia, focal reduced air entry, and aegophony. Viral infection can occur without fever or leukocytosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile presentation
Normal white blood cell count
No clear focal lobar consolidation reported on imaging
Prominent elevation of the right hemidiaphragm better suggests diaphragmatic dysfunction or eventration

data.description: 67-year-old female patient presented with chief complaint of swelling in right cheek. History of unhealed tooth extraction sockets from right upper posterior tooth extraction performed approximately one month previously. Past medical history significant for colorectal cancer treatment. Intraoral examination revealed localized, well-defined swelling measuring 4 cm × 5 cm obliterating buccal and palatal vestibules in region of unhealed extraction sockets of teeth 14, 15, and 16. Laboratory examination showed abnormal GTP level and slightly elevated serum CRP level.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL-NOS) of the maxilla/oral cavity
data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that may present as a rapidly enlarging extranodal mass in the oral cavity or jaw. The histology and BCL6/MUM1-positive, CD10-negative immunophenotype are compatible with an activated B-cell phenotype of DLBCL.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly apparent localized right cheek and maxillary swelling
Large, well-defined 4 cm × 5 cm intraoral mass
Obliteration of buccal and palatal vestibules
Possible bone/soft-tissue involvement around the posterior maxilla on CT
History of malignancy, which may raise concern for an underlying neoplastic process
Mildly elevated CRP can occur with aggressive lymphoma or tissue necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The swelling appeared after a recent tooth extraction, which can initially mimic a dental complication rather than lymphoma
Abnormal GTP level is not a typical defining feature of DLBCL

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma of the oral cavity
data.description: A lymphoma arising primarily in oral soft tissues, gingiva, palate, maxilla, or jaw rather than initially presenting in lymph nodes. DLBCL is the most common histologic subtype in the oral cavity.
symptoms_in_common: Gingival or vestibular mass involving an extraction-site region
Possible maxillary bone destruction or infiltrative lesion on imaging
Lack of a described acute odontogenic pain syndrome despite a large lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No cervical lymphadenopathy or constitutional B symptoms were reported
Abnormal GTP level is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the maxilla/oral cavity
data.description: Colorectal carcinoma can rarely metastasize to the jaws or oral soft tissues, producing swelling, bone destruction, tooth mobility, and nonhealing extraction wounds. A prior history of colorectal cancer makes this an important alternative diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Past history of colorectal cancer treatment
Possible destructive maxillary lesion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: The reported histologic appearance and B-cell-marker pattern favor lymphoma rather than adenocarcinoma
No gastrointestinal symptoms, weight loss, or evidence of recurrent systemic colorectal cancer was reported
Mild CRP elevation is nonspecific and does not specifically support metastatic colorectal cancer

data.description: A bacterial infection of the maxilla and adjacent soft tissues, often following dental extraction, that can cause swelling, delayed socket healing, local inflammation, and bone destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Recent extraction of right upper posterior teeth
Unhealed extraction sockets one month after extraction
Localized swelling in the posterior maxilla
Possible local bony changes around extraction sites
symptoms_not_in_common: The large well-circumscribed 4 cm × 5 cm mass is more suggestive of neoplasia than routine infection
No fever, severe pain, purulent drainage, foul taste, or marked systemic inflammatory response was described
Pathologic findings favor a lymphoid neoplasm rather than an infectious inflammatory process

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary gingiva/alveolus
data.description: An oral cavity malignancy arising from squamous epithelium that can present as an ulcerative or exophytic gingival mass, persistent extraction-site nonhealing, local bone invasion, and cheek swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Large intraoral mass involving the posterior maxillary alveolus
Possible local bony invasion or destruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No ulceration, leukoplakia, erythroplakia, bleeding, or pain was reported
The described cytology/histology and B-cell immunostaining pattern are not typical of squamous cell carcinoma
No smoking, alcohol exposure, or other classic oral squamous cell carcinoma risk factors were provided

diagnoses.name: Primary oral diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas

data.description: 24-year-old man presents with severely itchy rash that spread over two months. Had previously used an over-the-counter cream containing clobetasol, ofloxacin, terbinafine, and ornidazole which helped initially.
A dermatophyte fungal infection whose typical ring-like appearance has been altered, masked, and allowed to spread by use of potent topical corticosteroids such as clobetasol.
symptoms_in_common: Large annular and polycyclic erythematous plaques on the thighs and groin
Peripheral scaling and relatively less active central areas
Involvement of the groin and adjacent thighs
Initial improvement with a cream containing terbinafine and clobetasol, followed by persistence/spread

data.description: A superficial dermatophyte infection of glabrous skin and the groin, producing itchy, expanding scaly annular plaques with an active raised border and central clearing.
symptoms_in_common: Partial central clearing in several lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Very large confluent and atypically shaped plaques, which may reflect steroid modification rather than untreated ordinary tinea
Initial apparent improvement from potent topical clobetasol, which can suppress inflammation but usually worsens fungal spread over time

data.description: A chronic inflammatory eczema characterized by itchy coin-shaped scaly plaques, often on the extremities; lesions may become extensive or secondarily irritated.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous scaly plaques on the thighs
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent annular/polycyclic lesions with raised active borders and central clearing
Groin-predominant spread
Partial response to terbinafine
Progressive centrifugal enlargement of multiple ring-shaped lesions

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease causing well-demarcated erythematous plaques with scale; inverse psoriasis can affect the groin with less scale.
symptoms_in_common: Temporary improvement with potent topical corticosteroid use
symptoms_not_in_common: Annular lesions with central clearing and an advancing peripheral border
Rapid spread over two months in a dermatophyte-like pattern
Partial improvement with terbinafine
No described classic thick symmetric silvery plaques on extensor surfaces, scalp, or nails

data.description: 72-year-old man with a history of GERD well controlled on omeprazole until 11 months before admission, when heartburn recurred despite treatment. He developed postprandial nausea and early satiety, with gradual progression over 9 months causing stepwise dietary changes from solid food to soft solids, then blended food, then mostly liquids over 2 weeks, and inability to tolerate liquids by presentation. Two months before admission, EGD at another hospital was limited by large retained food in the stomach; no intraluminal mass was seen. On admission, he was thin, had a nasogastric tube in place, and had mild epigastric tenderness; vital signs showed mild tachycardia and low-grade fever.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma (linitis plastica, often signet-ring cell carcinoma)
data.description: An infiltrative gastric cancer that spreads diffusely through the stomach wall, causing marked wall thickening, poor distensibility, and gastric outlet obstruction; mucosal endoscopy may initially fail to show a discrete intraluminal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive intolerance of solids followed by liquids
Severe gastric retention and marked gastric dilatation
No obvious intraluminal mass on prior endoscopy despite obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding GERD is not a typical primary feature
Low-grade fever is not a common presenting symptom
Heartburn recurrence is nonspecific and may be due to gastric stasis rather than the cancer itself

data.description: A rare, usually benign mesenchymal tumor arising predominantly in the gastric antrum or pylorus. It can infiltrate the gastric wall and produce gastric outlet obstruction, often without a prominent mucosal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Inability to tolerate solid food and eventually liquids
Retained food in the stomach on endoscopy
Lack of a clear intraluminal mass on prior endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Older age is less typical because this tumor often occurs in younger or middle-aged adults
Progressive cachectic appearance may be less pronounced with a benign tumor
Low-grade fever is not typical
Recurrent heartburn is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy involving the stomach that can cause diffuse gastric-wall thickening, enlarged folds, submucosal infiltration, and occasionally gastric outlet obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse gastric-wall abnormality that may not appear as a discrete intraluminal mass
Low-grade fever can occur with lymphoma
Gastric outlet obstruction with retained gastric contents
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe progressive obstruction to liquids is less common than in infiltrative adenocarcinoma or a pyloric mass
No reported lymphadenopathy or systemic B symptoms such as drenching night sweats
Heartburn recurrence is not typical

data.description: A mesenchymal tumor arising from the muscularis propria of the stomach. An antral or pyloric GIST may compress or obstruct the gastric outlet, although many GISTs form a localized exophytic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Retained food and marked gastric dilatation
Submucosal origin can make a lesion difficult to identify on routine endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: No distinct focal gastric mass was identified on the initial endoscopy
Diffuse nodular or infiltrative gastric-wall involvement is less typical than a localized mass
No gastrointestinal bleeding, anemia, or ulceration was reported
Low-grade fever and recurrent heartburn are not typical

data.description: A male full-term neonate was admitted to the hospital 4 hours after birth for ecchymosis and petechiae. The infant was delivered by cesarean section at 40+5 weeks gestation due to failed induction, with birth weight 4000g and Apgar scores of 10. Physical examination revealed stable vital signs, weight 3850g, length 52cm, head circumference 35cm. The infant was alert and responsive with no special facial features. Skin examination showed large areas of ecchymosis on the chest, back, and upper limbs, with ecchymosis at the hepatitis B vaccine and vitamin K1 injection sites, and scattered pinpoint hemorrhages on the buttocks and lower limbs. The umbilical cord ligation site showed no bleeding, and cardiac, pulmonary, abdominal, and neurological examinations were normal.
A condition in which maternal antibodies cross the placenta and destroy fetal platelets, causing severe thrombocytopenia and bleeding manifestations in an otherwise well newborn.
symptoms_in_common: Bleeding/bruising at vitamin K1 and hepatitis B injection sites
Otherwise alert, stable, and clinically well-appearing neonate
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported cephalohematoma or other birth-trauma-associated bleeding
No reported intracranial hemorrhage

data.diagnosis: Congenital thrombocytopenia due to inherited platelet-production disorder
data.description: A group of genetic disorders causing reduced platelet number or abnormal platelet production, which may present at birth with petechiae, purpura, and excessive bruising.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of systemic illness or abnormal cardiopulmonary examination
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported skeletal abnormalities
No reported congenital limb defects
No reported hepatosplenomegaly
No reported dysmorphic facial features

data.description: An inherited platelet function disorder caused by defective or absent platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptors, resulting in impaired platelet aggregation despite a potentially normal platelet count.
symptoms_in_common: Normal general physical examination apart from skin bleeding
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported mucosal bleeding such as epistaxis or oral bleeding
No reported gastrointestinal bleeding
No reported prolonged umbilical stump bleeding

data.description: A rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder in which clots are unstable because factor XIII cannot adequately cross-link fibrin. It can cause neonatal bruising, bleeding after procedures, and later severe hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Petechiae or superficial hemorrhagic skin lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No bleeding from the umbilical cord ligation site
No reported delayed wound bleeding
No reported intracranial hemorrhage

data.description: X-linked deficiencies of factor VIII or factor IX that primarily affect male infants and can cause excessive bleeding after trauma, injections, or invasive procedures.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising at vitamin K1 and hepatitis B injection sites
symptoms_not_in_common: Petechiae are less typical than deep tissue bleeding
No reported cephalohematoma
No reported prolonged bleeding from the umbilical stump
No reported joint, muscle, or deep soft-tissue bleeding

data.description: 50-year-old man presented with 2-week history of constant worsening headache affecting the whole head. No history of head trauma, but reported headbanging at a Motörhead concert 4 weeks prior to presentation. Medical history was unremarkable and patient denied substance misuse. Neurological examination and laboratory studies, including coagulation screening, were normal.

A collection of blood products between the dura and arachnoid membranes, often developing gradually over days to weeks after minor or repetitive head trauma. It may cause progressive headache and mass effect despite a normal neurological examination initially.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed presentation several weeks after repetitive minor head acceleration/deceleration from headbanging
Normal coagulation screening, which can occur in traumatic chronic subdural hematoma
Normal neurological examination can be present early
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal neurological deficit
No confusion, drowsiness, personality change, or gait disturbance reported
No nausea, vomiting, or seizures reported

data.description: A chronic subdural collection with newer bleeding into it, potentially following repeated minor trauma. It can produce an increasingly severe headache and radiological evidence of mixed-age blood products.
symptoms_in_common: Symptoms developing over weeks after the precipitating event
Normal laboratory coagulation studies do not exclude the condition
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported sudden severe deterioration
No altered consciousness
No focal weakness, speech disturbance, or seizures reported

data.diagnosis: Traumatic cerebral contusion with associated subdural hematoma
data.description: A cerebral contusion is bruising and bleeding within brain tissue after acceleration-deceleration injury; temporal and frontal regions are common sites. It may coexist with a subdural hematoma after repetitive head movements.
symptoms_in_common: Worsening symptoms after possible minor traumatic injury
Normal neurological examination may occur with a small contusion
symptoms_not_in_common: No loss of consciousness reported
No vomiting
No seizure
No focal neurological signs
No documented direct impact to the head

data.description: A 35-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with a clinically incarcerated umbilical hernia. Fourteen days after the initial hernia repair surgery, she developed strong pain in the right lower abdomen and complained of umbilical secretion. Physical examination revealed the patient was afebrile. Blood analysis showed a slight elevation in leukocyte count at 11.05 × 10^9/L, while other parameters were unexceptional. Ultrasound of the abdominal wall detected a semisolid infraumbilical mass with a diameter of 5.5 cm. Initial histologic examination of the resected omental fat from the hernia repair revealed malignant cells with neuroendocrine differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis was positive for synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5. Fluorescent in situ hybridization revealed a rearrangement of the EWSR1 gene.

data.diagnosis: Extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma / peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor (pPNET)
data.description: A malignant small round cell sarcoma arising in soft tissue rather than bone. It commonly has EWSR1 rearrangement, often involving an EWSR1-FLI1 fusion, and may show neural or neuroendocrine differentiation.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly symptomatic abdominal wall or omental soft-tissue mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Umbilical secretion shortly after hernia repair is not a typical primary presentation and may reflect local postoperative involvement
Presentation as an incarcerated umbilical hernia is unusual

data.description: An aggressive small round cell sarcoma that usually develops in the abdominal or pelvic peritoneum of young people. It is characterized by an EWSR1-WT1 fusion and often presents with peritoneal masses.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable or imaging-detected abdominal wall mass
Malignant small round cell tumor morphology may overlap
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex is less typical because DSRCT has a strong male predominance
Synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5 positivity are not the classic dominant immunophenotype
No reported desmoplastic stromal reaction
No reported WT1 positivity or EWSR1-WT1 fusion confirmation
Solitary localized lesion is less typical than multifocal peritoneal disease
Umbilical secretion is not typical

data.diagnosis: Clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue
data.description: A rare malignant soft-tissue sarcoma, sometimes called melanoma of soft parts, most often arising in tendons or aponeuroses of the extremities. It may harbor EWSR1-ATF1 or EWSR1-CREB1 rearrangements.
symptoms_not_in_common: Omental and abdominal wall location is highly unusual
Neuroendocrine differentiation is not typical
Synaptophysin positivity is not typical
Protein gene product 9.5 positivity is nonspecific and not characteristic
No reported melanocytic marker positivity such as S100, SOX10, HMB45, or Melan-A
Umbilical secretion is not typical

data.description: A high-grade epithelial malignancy composed of neuroendocrine cells, often arising in the gastrointestinal tract, pancreas, lung, or gynecologic organs and commonly expressing synaptophysin.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 35 is younger than typical for most poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinomas
EWSR1 gene rearrangement is not typical
No identified epithelial primary tumor
No reported epithelial marker expression such as cytokeratin or EMA
Presentation through an umbilical hernia is unusual
Umbilical secretion is not a typical manifestation

data.description: 60-year-old Japanese woman presented with a black nodule on the right postauricular area. Initial staging after radical resection and sentinel node biopsy was pT3aN0M0 stage IIA. At 19 months post-surgery, imaging detected right jugular lymph node and lung metastases. Seven courses of pembrolizumab treatment later, evaluation showed further lung metastasis and new liver metastasis. Tumor harbored BRAF V600E mutation. Thirteen days after starting dabrafenib/trametinib, patient developed fever and hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory findings showed pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, increased liver enzyme levels, and coagulation abnormalities.

A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled activation of macrophages and T cells, resulting in cytokine excess, hemophagocytosis, cytopenias, liver dysfunction, and coagulopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Bone marrow findings consistent with hemophagocytosis in the provided image
symptoms_not_in_common: Black postauricular melanoma nodule
BRAF V600E mutation
Pulmonary and liver metastases

data.description: Secondary HLH triggered by BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy. Dabrafenib plus trametinib can rarely provoke severe systemic inflammatory reactions, including HLH, often shortly after treatment initiation.
symptoms_in_common: Possible drug-related skin eruption on the arm
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding metastatic melanoma predating treatment
Initial localized black postauricular tumor

data.description: HLH can rarely occur as a severe immune-related adverse event of PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors such as pembrolizumab, due to excessive immune activation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms began shortly after dabrafenib/trametinib initiation rather than during the documented pembrolizumab courses
Progressive melanoma metastases despite pembrolizumab

data.description: Secondary HLH may be triggered by advanced malignancy, including metastatic solid tumors, although it is more commonly associated with hematologic cancers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset 13 days after starting targeted therapy suggests a medication-associated trigger
Primary melanoma initially had no nodal or distant metastasis

data.description: 14-year-old boy presented to trauma unit with gunshot wound to left eye. Alert and hemodynamically stable, blind in left eye, no CSF rhinorrhea. Pubertal status: Tanner stage S3, height: 1.7m (75th percentile). Laboratory findings: 8am serum cortisol 28 nmol/L (normal 171-536), thyroid-stimulating hormone 0.63 mIU/L (normal 0.27-4.20), free thyroxine 13.5 pmol/L (normal 13.6-23.2), luteinising hormone 0.7 IU/L (normal 1.3-9.8), insulin-like growth factor 1 19.4 nmol/L (normal 28.8-127.3), prolactin 13.04 pmol/L (normal 174-660.9), testosterone undetectable <0.1 nmol/L (normal 1-38.5).

data.diagnosis: Traumatic panhypopituitarism due to hypothalamic-pituitary injury
data.description: Deficiency of multiple anterior pituitary hormones caused by trauma to the hypothalamus, pituitary stalk, or pituitary gland. The transorbital gunshot trajectory and retained metallic foreign body near the skull base may have injured these structures.
