symptoms_in_common: Low-normal thyroid-stimulating hormone despite low free thyroxine, consistent with central hypothyroidism
Delayed/incomplete pubertal development for age (Tanner stage S3 at age 14)
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute blindness in the left eye is more directly explained by ocular/orbital gunshot injury
No cerebrospinal-fluid rhinorrhea
Hemodynamic stability and alert mental status despite severe biochemical cortisol deficiency

data.description: Adrenocorticotropic hormone deficiency from hypothalamic or pituitary injury causes inadequate cortisol production. This can be life-threatening, particularly during acute trauma or infection.
symptoms_in_common: Recent severe head/orbital trauma that could disrupt pituitary-adrenal signaling
Potentially limited physiologic stress response despite major trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: Low free thyroxine with inappropriately low-normal thyroid-stimulating hormone
Low luteinising hormone and undetectable testosterone
Low insulin-like growth factor 1
Very low prolactin
Blindness in the left eye

data.description: Deficient hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone or pituitary gonadotropin secretion results in low luteinising hormone and low testosterone, causing delayed or arrested puberty.
symptoms_in_common: Pubertal development only at Tanner stage S3 at age 14
Possible hypothalamic-pituitary injury from penetrating cranial trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: Severely low morning cortisol
Low free thyroxine with low-normal thyroid-stimulating hormone
Low insulin-like growth factor 1
Very low prolactin
Acute left-eye blindness due to gunshot injury

data.diagnosis: Central hypothyroidism due to traumatic hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction
data.description: Central hypothyroidism occurs when pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion is inadequate for the circulating thyroid hormone level, usually because of pituitary or hypothalamic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Thyroid-stimulating hormone that is not appropriately elevated for the low free thyroxine concentration
Penetrating cranial trauma with potential hypothalamic-pituitary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Very low morning cortisol
Low luteinising hormone and undetectable testosterone
Low insulin-like growth factor 1
Very low prolactin
Left-eye blindness from gunshot trauma

data.description: 14-month-old girl with a 3-month history of recurrent episodic vomiting beginning at 11 months, with four 3–5 day episodes associated with lethargy, decreased oral intake, and intermittent diarrhea. Over the same period, she had developmental regression, stopping attempts to walk and crawling unsteadily with occasional falls. Parents reported brief morning episodes of symmetric shaking movements without loss of consciousness. Born full-term without complications. On examination, she was alert and interactive but had frontal bossing, a full fontanelle with visible pulsations when supine, and head circumference 51.5 cm. Neurologic exam showed decreased tone in the legs with brisk patellar reflexes and flexor plantar responses; eye movements and pupils were normal, with no nystagmus.

data.diagnosis: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to congenital aqueductal stenosis
data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct causes impaired cerebrospinal-fluid flow, progressive enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, and raised intracranial pressure.
symptoms_in_common: Lower-extremity hypotonia with brisk patellar reflexes
MRI appearance of marked ventriculomegaly consistent with obstructive hydrocephalus
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric shaking episodes without loss of consciousness

data.diagnosis: Hydrocephalus secondary to a tectal plate glioma
data.description: A low-grade tumor of the tectal region can compress the cerebral aqueduct and produce obstructive hydrocephalus, often presenting with vomiting, macrocephaly, and developmental decline in young children.
symptoms_in_common: Motor decline with unsteady crawling and falls
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal eye movements and absence of nystagmus, as tectal lesions may cause vertical gaze abnormalities
Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric shaking without impaired consciousness

data.diagnosis: Dandy-Walker malformation or other posterior fossa cerebrospinal-fluid outflow abnormality
data.description: Congenital posterior fossa malformations can disrupt cerebrospinal-fluid circulation and lead to hydrocephalus, macrocephaly, developmental delay, and impaired motor development.
symptoms_in_common: Macrocephaly with rapidly increasing head circumference
Poor motor function, unsteady crawling, and falls
symptoms_not_in_common: MRI does not primarily describe a posterior fossa cyst or vermian malformation
Brisk patellar reflexes are less characteristic than generalized hypotonia
Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric shaking episodes

data.diagnosis: Intracranial mass causing raised intracranial pressure
data.description: Brain tumors or other intracranial masses can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid pathways or increase intracranial pressure, causing vomiting, lethargy, developmental loss, and enlarged head size in infants with open sutures.
symptoms_in_common: Upper-motor-neuron-type findings suggested by brisk patellar reflexes
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal cranial nerve deficit or abnormal eye movements
No clearly described discrete mass lesion on the provided MRI
Intermittent diarrhea
Brief symmetric shaking without loss of consciousness

data.description: Cyclic vomiting syndrome causes recurrent stereotyped episodes of severe vomiting separated by periods of relative wellness, often associated with lethargy and poor intake.
symptoms_not_in_common: Developmental regression
Stopping attempts to walk
Unsteady crawling and falls
Macrocephaly with accelerated head growth
Frontal bossing
Full pulsatile fontanelle
Lower-extremity hypotonia with brisk patellar reflexes
Marked ventriculomegaly on MRI

diagnoses.name: Aqueductal stenosis
diagnoses.title: Stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius

data.description: 31-year-old man with sleep apnea and newly diagnosed hypertension, with repeated blood pressures up to 173/110 mm Hg. He reported 6 months of lethargy and intermittent headaches. Past history included a 20 pack-year smoking history. On examination, heart rate was 106 bpm and BMI 34; no cushingoid features, hyperpigmentation, renal or carotid bruits, or tremor were noted. Full blood count, urea, electrolytes, and renal artery Doppler were normal. Biochemical testing showed aldosterone 278 pmol/L, direct renin concentration 1.8 mU/L, aldosterone-to-renin ratio 157, normal urinary metanephrines and normetanephrines, elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol at 227 nmol/24 h, suppressed post-dexamethasone cortisol of 30 nmol/L, and ACTH <10 ng/L.
A cause of secondary hypertension due to autonomous aldosterone production, leading to suppressed renin and an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio. Potassium may be normal.
symptoms_in_common: New-onset significant hypertension with readings up to 173/110 mm Hg
Intermittent headaches, which can occur with severe hypertension
Normal renal artery Doppler, making renovascular hypertension less likely
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol
Lethargy is nonspecific and not a classic manifestation
No reported hypokalemia
Tachycardia is not a typical direct feature

data.description: Obstructive sleep apnea can cause resistant or newly recognized hypertension through recurrent nocturnal hypoxia and sympathetic nervous system activation. It is commonly associated with obesity.
symptoms_in_common: Headaches, which may occur with sleep apnea
Tachycardia, potentially related to sympathetic activation
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppressed renin concentration
Markedly elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio
Elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol

data.description: The most common form of hypertension, caused by a combination of genetic predisposition and environmental factors such as obesity, smoking, and sleep apnea.
symptoms_in_common: Headaches associated with elevated blood pressure
Sleep apnea, a major contributing cardiovascular risk factor
Normal renal function and normal renal artery Doppler
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppressed renin with a markedly elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio suggests a secondary endocrine cause rather than uncomplicated essential hypertension
Elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol
Lethargy is nonspecific

data.description: A disorder of chronic excess cortisol production that can cause hypertension, central obesity, fatigue, glucose intolerance, skin changes, and muscle weakness.
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppressed cortisol after dexamethasone, which argues against autonomous Cushing syndrome
No cushingoid physical features
No hyperpigmentation
ACTH is not clearly elevated
Markedly elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio is not typical

data.diagnosis: Pseudo-Cushing state related to obesity and obstructive sleep apnea
data.description: Obesity, chronic stress, and untreated obstructive sleep apnea may cause mild elevation of cortisol testing without true autonomous cortisol excess; dexamethasone suppression is usually preserved.
symptoms_not_in_common: Suppressed renin and high aldosterone-to-renin ratio are not explained by pseudo-Cushing physiology alone
Severe hypertension may require an additional cause such as primary aldosteronism

data.description: 46-year-old woman who experienced chest pain before having an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Pre-arrest rhythm strip showed sinus tachycardia. Initial troponin I was 5.9 μg/L (normal: 0-0.04 μg/L). Medical history included similar chest pain episode one year prior after taking sumatriptan for migraine, with transient inferior and lateral ST elevation on ECG but negative troponin at that time. Previous coronary angiography showed normal left coronary system and dominant right coronary artery with minor ostial spasm and slow flow. Negative bubble study for right to left shunting. Current medications: oral diltiazem, nicorandil, lansoprazole, and beclometasone inhaler. Patient was a former smoker.

data.diagnosis: Vasospastic angina (Prinzmetal angina) causing coronary vasospasm and myocardial infarction
data.description: Transient epicardial coronary artery spasm can cause severe ischemia, ST-segment elevation, myocardial infarction, and malignant ventricular arrhythmias despite otherwise normal or minimally diseased coronary arteries. Triptans such as sumatriptan can precipitate vasospasm.
symptoms_in_common: Transient inferior and lateral ST-segment elevation during a prior chest-pain episode
Current marked troponin I elevation indicating myocardial injury
Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, which can occur from ischemia-related ventricular arrhythmia
Previously normal coronary angiography with minor ostial spasm and slow coronary flow
Prior chest pain occurring after sumatriptan use
Use of diltiazem and nicorandil, medications commonly used for coronary vasospasm
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly atypical symptoms are described; the presentation is highly compatible with severe coronary vasospasm

data.description: An acute myocardial infarction caused by abrupt coronary occlusion produces chest pain, ST-segment elevation, elevated cardiac troponin, and may lead to ventricular arrhythmia and cardiac arrest. The ECG pattern shown is consistent with prominent anterior precordial ST-segment elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Acute chest pain before cardiac arrest
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous coronary angiography showed no significant obstructive coronary artery disease
Prior transient ST elevation resolved with a negative troponin, which is more suggestive of transient vasospasm than fixed thrombotic occlusion
Prior episode was temporally associated with sumatriptan exposure

data.description: Sumatriptan is a serotonin receptor agonist used for migraine that can rarely cause coronary vasoconstriction or vasospasm, resulting in chest pain, transient ST elevation, myocardial infarction, and potentially life-threatening arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Chest pain after taking sumatriptan during the prior episode
Transient inferior and lateral ST-segment elevation after sumatriptan exposure
Normal coronary anatomy apart from minor spasm and slow flow
Evidence of coronary vasoreactivity suggested by treatment with diltiazem and nicorandil
symptoms_not_in_common: The current arrest episode is not stated to have followed recent sumatriptan use
Marked troponin elevation and cardiac arrest are severe complications rather than typical uncomplicated triptan-associated chest symptoms

data.description: A 44-year-old woman with cerebral palsy and multiple sclerosis (diagnosed at age 16) presented to the emergency department with four days of acute constipation and vomiting. She had a history of chronic constipation due to neurogenic bowel dysfunction secondary to her underlying conditions, initially managed with laxatives. Her constipation had become severe enough to warrant insertion of a sacral anterior root stimulator in the last year. On examination, her abdomen was markedly distended, diffusely tender, with absent bowel sounds. There was no guarding, rigidity, or previous incisions, and all hernia orifices were intact. Vital signs showed tachycardia (140 beats/min), tachypnea, normal blood pressure (130/60 mmHg), and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Laboratory findings revealed normal pH of 7.36, hypocapnea (PCO2 29mmHg), hyperlactataemia (20 mg/dL), normal PO2 (), white blood cell count of 10,500 cells/mm3 (73% neutrophils), and elevated C-reactive protein of 3.25 mg/dL.

data.diagnosis: Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome) with impending or actual colonic perforation
data.description: Acute massive dilatation of the colon without a mechanical blockage, often occurring in patients with severe neurologic disease, immobility, metabolic illness, or medications affecting bowel motility. Marked dilatation can cause ischemia and perforation.
symptoms_in_common: Underlying neurologic disease with neurogenic bowel dysfunction
Radiographic marked colonic dilatation with air-fluid levels
symptoms_not_in_common: Long-standing severe constipation requiring a sacral anterior root stimulator is a predisposing condition rather than a typical acute symptom
No major atypical symptoms are described

data.diagnosis: Stercoral colitis with stercoral colonic perforation
data.description: Inflammation, ischemic pressure injury, ulceration, and possible perforation of the colon caused by impacted stool (fecaloma). It occurs most often in patients with chronic constipation, immobility, or neurologic impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Neurogenic bowel dysfunction from cerebral palsy and multiple sclerosis
Imaging appearance of substantial fecal loading with colonic dilatation
CT appearance concerning for perforation/free intraperitoneal air
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of guarding or rigidity despite possible perforation
Normal blood pressure and near-normal blood pH despite severe abdominal pathology

data.diagnosis: Mechanical large-bowel obstruction due to fecal impaction
data.description: A distal fecal impaction can function as a mechanical obstruction, producing proximal colonic dilatation, abdominal distension, vomiting, and potentially ischemia or perforation if untreated.
symptoms_in_common: Air-fluid levels and markedly dilated bowel on abdominal radiographs
Neurologic disorders that predispose to impaired colonic transit
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior abdominal surgery, which is a common historical clue for some mechanical bowel obstructions
No hernia detected on examination
No localized colicky pain is described

data.description: Twisting of the sigmoid colon around its mesenteric attachment causes closed-loop large-bowel obstruction. It is associated with chronic constipation, neurologic disease, reduced mobility, and a redundant sigmoid colon; ischemia and perforation may occur.
symptoms_in_common: Neurologic impairment and likely reduced bowel motility
Raised lactate, which may indicate bowel ischemia
Markedly dilated large-bowel loop on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No classic sudden onset of crampy lower abdominal pain is reported
No definite whirl sign or characteristic transition point is provided in the case description
Diffuse tenderness rather than predominantly lower abdominal pain

data.description: 64-year-old man with 5 months of cough with thin yellow sputum, exertional dyspnea, chest tightness, and wheezing, followed 10 days before presentation by lethargy, myalgias, chills, headaches, anorexia, and night sweats. He presented with dyspnea, wheezing, headache, cough, and neck stiffness/photophobia. On exam he was febrile and tachycardic, mildly ill-appearing, with neck stiffness, inspiratory crackles bilaterally, and mild synovial thickening of the hands consistent with chronic arthritic changes. Labs showed leukocytosis (21,130/mm³) with neutrophilia and elevated ESR (34 mm/hr). Past history included fibromyalgia, L5 radiculopathy with foot drop, carpal tunnel syndrome, osteoarthritis, cervical spondylosis, sleep apnea, and peptic ulcer disease. He worked in a healthcare facility and had recent travel to Florida and Europe/Caribbean. Family history included sister with systemic lupus erythematosus, scleroderma, and Hashimoto thyroiditis.

Infection with Cryptococcus neoformans or Cryptococcus gattii that can involve the lungs and disseminate to the central nervous system, causing subacute meningitis. Pulmonary disease may produce nodules, cough, dyspnea, and constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple pulmonary nodular abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked neutrophilic leukocytosis is less typical than in acute bacterial infection
Thin yellow sputum is not a classic feature
A 5-month wheezing-predominant respiratory illness is less typical

data.diagnosis: Histoplasmosis with pulmonary and central nervous system involvement
data.description: Histoplasma capsulatum is a dimorphic fungus that can cause chronic pulmonary disease, diffuse or nodular lung infiltrates, constitutional symptoms, and, less commonly, chronic meningitis.
symptoms_in_common: Neck stiffness and photophobia suggesting meningitis
Recent travel in regions where fungal exposure may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent wheezing is not typical
Acute neutrophilic leukocytosis is less characteristic than in bacterial pneumonia
Meningitis is an uncommon manifestation in an otherwise apparently immunocompetent patient

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can cause a chronic respiratory illness with constitutional symptoms and may spread hematogenously to the meninges, producing subacute meningitis with headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary nodules or diffuse pulmonary infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked neutrophilic leukocytosis is not classic for tuberculosis
Wheezing and chest tightness are less typical
The relatively abrupt 10-day systemic deterioration is less typical for uncomplicated tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Nocardiosis with pulmonary and central nervous system dissemination
data.description: Nocardia species are aerobic filamentous bacteria that can cause subacute pulmonary infection with nodules or consolidation and can disseminate to the brain or meninges, particularly in immunocompromised patients but occasionally in immunocompetent hosts.
symptoms_not_in_common: Meningitis is less common than focal brain abscess in nocardiosis
No known major immunosuppressive condition is described
Wheezing is not a characteristic feature

data.description: Legionella pneumophila causes an atypical pneumonia associated with fever, cough, myalgias, headache, and systemic symptoms. Neurologic manifestations can occur, although true meningitis is uncommon.
symptoms_not_in_common: Five months of preceding cough and dyspnea is not typical for acute Legionella infection
Neck stiffness and photophobia suggesting true meningitis are uncommon
Night sweats and chronic pulmonary nodules are less typical
Wheezing is not a prominent classic feature

data.description: 47-year-old woman admitted with left lumbar pain and macroscopic hematuria. Past medical history was unremarkable. Physical examination showed pale skin, no peripheral edema, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, and diuresis of 1000 mL/day. She had moderate normocytic anemia. Autoimmune serologies, antiphospholipid antibodies, ANCA, anti-GBM antibodies, cryoglobulins, rheumatoid factor, hepatitis B/C, HIV tests, and serum protein electrophoresis were negative.

A microvascular renal injury characterized by endothelial damage, arteriolar or glomerular thrombosis, and ischemic vascular changes. It may occur without the full systemic features of hemolytic anemia or thrombocytopenia.
symptoms_in_common: Renal biopsy appearance suggestive of vascular thrombotic and chronic onion-skin-type arteriolar changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal blood pressure
No peripheral edema

data.description: A complement-driven thrombotic microangiopathy that predominantly affects the kidneys and can present in adulthood, sometimes without a clear infectious trigger or prominent gastrointestinal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Renal vascular thrombotic microangiopathy-type histologic findings
symptoms_not_in_common: Left lumbar/flank pain is not a classic presenting feature
No reported thrombocytopenia
No reported acute kidney injury
No reported hypertension
No diarrhea or preceding gastrointestinal illness

data.description: A systemic thrombotic microangiopathy usually caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, leading to platelet-rich microvascular thrombi, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and possible neurologic or renal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Microangiopathic vascular lesions can be seen in the kidney
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported thrombocytopenia
No reported neurologic symptoms
No fever

Gross hematuria is less characteristic than systemic hemolysis and thrombocytopenia

data.description: Renal vascular injury caused by antiphospholipid-associated thrombosis, often producing thrombotic microangiopathy, fibrous intimal hyperplasia, and chronic ischemic renal changes.
symptoms_in_common: Normocytic anemia may occur with renal injury or thrombosis
Flank pain may occur with renal ischemia or infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: Antiphospholipid antibodies were negative
No history of arterial or venous thrombosis
No pregnancy morbidity history was reported
Normal blood pressure
No peripheral edema

data.description: Severe hypertension can cause endothelial injury, arteriolar fibrinoid damage, hyperplastic arteriolosclerosis, and secondary thrombotic microangiopathy in the kidney.
symptoms_in_common: Renal arteriolar injury with onion-skin-type vascular changes
Possible flank discomfort from renal ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Blood pressure of approximately 130/80 mmHg is not consistent with malignant hypertension
No reported severe headache, visual disturbance, heart failure, or hypertensive emergency symptoms
No peripheral edema

data.description: A 31-year-old female, G3P2, came in with 5-day history of severe menorrhagia. She was treated medically and discharged. She was readmitted 2 days later with menorrhagia and anaemia (haemoglobin of 77). The patient had suffered a spontaneous miscarriage a few months earlier.

An abnormal high-flow connection between uterine arteries and veins, often acquired after pregnancy-related uterine trauma, miscarriage, curettage, or other uterine procedures. It can cause sudden, recurrent, life-threatening uterine bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid recurrence of bleeding after medical treatment
Severe anaemia with haemoglobin of 77 g/L
Recent spontaneous miscarriage, a potential preceding pregnancy-related event
symptoms_not_in_common: No pelvic pain, uterine bruit, or haemodynamic instability was reported

data.description: Persistence of placental or fetal tissue in the uterus after miscarriage or pregnancy termination, causing ongoing or delayed vaginal bleeding and sometimes infection.
symptoms_in_common: History of spontaneous miscarriage a few months earlier
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding occurred months after the miscarriage rather than immediately afterward
No fever, foul-smelling discharge, uterine tenderness, or pelvic pain was reported

data.description: A spectrum of abnormal trophoblastic proliferation after pregnancy, including molar pregnancy and gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, which may present with abnormal uterine bleeding after a pregnancy loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: No persistently elevated beta-hCG result was provided
No enlarged uterus, pelvic mass, hyperemesis, or symptoms of hyperthyroidism were reported

data.description: A benign smooth-muscle tumour of the uterus; fibroids that project into the uterine cavity commonly cause heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding and iron-deficiency anaemia.
symptoms_in_common: Anaemia due to heavy menstrual blood loss
Age within the common reproductive-age range for fibroids
symptoms_not_in_common: The abrupt onset following a recent miscarriage is less characteristic
No history of chronic heavy periods, pelvic pressure, enlarged uterus, or palpable mass was reported

data.description: 28-year-old man with abdominal pain and 10–12 watery stools per day after completing azithromycin for pneumonia. He improved and returned to baseline bowel habits, then 6 weeks later developed 3 weeks of abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements with increased stool frequency to 4–5 formed stools per day. At the second presentation, vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable.

A functional bowel disorder that can develop after an episode of infectious or antibiotic-associated diarrhea, causing recurrent abdominal discomfort and altered bowel habits without systemic illness.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements
Symptoms occurring after a prior diarrheal illness
Normal vital signs and unremarkable physical examination
Formed stools at the second presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial severe watery diarrhea of 10–12 stools per day after azithromycin

data.description: Recurrent C. difficile infection is return of antibiotic-associated diarrhea after apparent improvement, usually causing frequent unformed stools and abdominal cramping.
symptoms_in_common: Prior episode of frequent watery diarrhea
Recurrence of increased bowel frequency after initial improvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Stools are formed rather than watery at the second presentation
Only 4–5 stools per day at the second presentation
Abdominal discomfort is relieved by bowel movements
No fever, abnormal vital signs, or abnormal examination findings

data.description: Diarrhea caused by disruption of normal intestinal microbiota during or shortly after antibiotic treatment, often mild and self-limited.
symptoms_in_common: Watery stools beginning after completing azithromycin
High stool frequency during the initial episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms recurred 6 weeks after returning to baseline bowel habits
Second episode consists of formed stools rather than diarrhea
Abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements suggests a functional bowel pattern

data.description: Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis are chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract that may cause abdominal pain and increased stool frequency.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptoms began in close association with antibiotic-associated watery diarrhea
Stools are formed at the second presentation
No blood in stool reported
No fever, weight loss, fatigue, or abnormal physical examination findings
Abdominal discomfort is relieved by bowel movements

data.description: 29-year-old man with 6 weeks of unintentional 10 kg weight loss, severe epigastric/upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat and worsened by eating, followed 3 weeks later by nausea, intermittent vomiting, decreased oral intake, one episode of hematemesis, sore throat, and fever. Past history includes a respiratory illness 2 years earlier and 10 years of macular hyperpigmentation on the feet and legs. On examination he was cachectic, febrile to 38.3°C, tachycardic, with low blood pressure, weight 47.6 kg (BMI 18.6), coarse breath sounds with scattered fine rales at both lung bases, white exudate on the underside of the tongue, and multiple 1–2 cm nontender mobile submandibular, submental, and cervical lymph nodes; abdomen was initially soft and nontender, later firm without distention. Labs showed anemia, leukopenia with marked lymphopenia, hyponatremia, low bicarbonate, hypoalbuminemia, elevated globulins, and low CD4 count with positive HIV-1 testing and detectable HIV-1 RNA.
Systemic infection with Histoplasma capsulatum, often occurring in advanced HIV infection and involving lungs, lymph nodes, gastrointestinal tract, bone marrow, liver, spleen, and adrenal glands.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV infection with low CD4 count and lymphopenia
Marked unintentional weight loss and cachexia
Diffuse pulmonary micronodular/interstitial infiltrates with rales
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, poor oral intake, and possible gastrointestinal bleeding
Hypotension and hyponatremia, which may suggest adrenal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten-year history of macular hyperpigmentation limited to the feet and legs
White oral exudate, which is more suggestive of oral candidiasis as a concurrent opportunistic infection

data.diagnosis: Disseminated or miliary tuberculosis with abdominal tuberculosis
data.description: Hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis causing diffuse pulmonary micronodules and possible involvement of lymph nodes, peritoneum, intestines, and other organs; risk is increased in advanced HIV infection.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and later abdominal firmness
Nausea, vomiting, reduced oral intake, and hypoalbuminemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported chronic cough, sputum production, night sweats, or hemoptysis
Prominent pain radiating to the throat and hematemesis are less typical as primary manifestations
White oral exudate is more consistent with candidiasis than tuberculosis

data.description: Opportunistic disseminated infection caused by nontuberculous mycobacteria, usually in patients with very low CD4 counts; it commonly causes fever, wasting, anemia, lymphadenopathy, and gastrointestinal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection with low CD4 count
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and decreased oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute severe epigastric pain radiating to the throat is not a classic presentation
Hematemesis is uncommon
Diffuse lung micronodules are less characteristic than systemic and gastrointestinal manifestations
Ten-year localized macular hyperpigmentation is not typical

data.description: A disseminated fungal opportunistic infection in advanced HIV, particularly in endemic regions of Southeast and East Asia, causing fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, pulmonary disease, cytopenias, and gastrointestinal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV infection with marked CD4 lymphopenia
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and poor intake
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported typical widespread papular skin lesions with central necrosis or umbilication
The long-standing macular hyperpigmentation on the feet and legs is not the usual acute skin manifestation
Hematemesis is less typical

data.diagnosis: AIDS with opportunistic esophagitis, most likely Candida esophagitis
data.description: Candida infection of the oral cavity and esophagus is common in advanced HIV and can cause painful swallowing, retrosternal or epigastric pain, nausea, poor intake, and occasionally bleeding from severe mucosal inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Positive HIV-1 testing with low CD4 count
White exudate on the underside of the tongue consistent with oral candidiasis
Upper abdominal/retrosternal pain radiating toward the throat
Nausea, intermittent vomiting, and reduced oral intake
Possible hematemesis from severe esophageal mucosal injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever, diffuse lymphadenopathy, severe cytopenias, and pulmonary micronodules are not explained by isolated Candida esophagitis
Fine bibasilar rales are not typical
Hyponatremia and hypotension are not typical direct manifestations
Ten-year macular hyperpigmentation is unrelated

data.description: 52-year-old man with a 2-week history of exertional central chest fullness and dyspnea, occurring only with activity and not at rest, without light-headedness or syncope. Past history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, and family history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; prior screening echocardiogram 3 years earlier showed mild left ventricular hypertrophy with otherwise normal cardiac structure and function. On examination he was afebrile with BP 146/70 mmHg, HR 70/min, RR 14/min, BMI 36.2; JVP was normal, heart rhythm regular without murmurs/rubs/gallops, lungs and abdomen were normal, and there was no leg edema. Initial labs showed mild leukocytosis, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), potassium 5.4 mmol/L, and normal INR, BUN, sodium, thyrotropin, and troponin I.

A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized by myocardial inflammation, myocyte injury, and multinucleated giant cells. It commonly presents with ventricular arrhythmias, heart failure, or rapidly worsening cardiac function.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute 2-week onset of exertional chest fullness
Histology showing multinucleated giant cells with myocardial inflammation
Normal initial troponin does not exclude myocarditis
No prior major structural heart disease on previous echocardiogram
symptoms_not_in_common: No resting dyspnea
No clinical signs of heart failure such as edema, elevated JVP, or pulmonary crackles
No syncope or presyncope
No fever or viral prodrome reported

data.description: Inflammatory granulomatous involvement of the heart due to sarcoidosis, which can cause conduction disease, ventricular tachycardia, cardiomyopathy, and sudden cardiac death. Histology typically shows noncaseating granulomas, sometimes with giant cells.
symptoms_in_common: Myocardial inflammatory infiltrate with giant cells on biopsy
Possible progression from previously mild ventricular hypertrophy to electrical instability
symptoms_not_in_common: No known pulmonary sarcoidosis
No reported hilar adenopathy, cough, skin lesions, eye symptoms, or systemic sarcoid manifestations
No reported atrioventricular block or other conduction-system disease
No fever, weight loss, or constitutional symptoms

data.description: A genetic myocardial disorder characterized by unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy, often with myocyte disarray and fibrosis. It can cause exertional chest symptoms, dyspnea, and ventricular arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Previously documented mild left ventricular hypertrophy
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior echocardiogram reportedly showed otherwise normal cardiac structure and function
No murmur suggestive of dynamic left ventricular outflow obstruction
No syncope or presyncope
Myocardial giant-cell inflammatory histology is not typical of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

data.diagnosis: Coronary artery disease with exertional angina
data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of coronary arteries causing myocardial ischemia during exertion. Diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and obesity substantially increase risk.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal troponin I
No reported ischemic ST-segment changes on the initial ECG
Sustained ventricular tachyarrhythmia is less typical without acute infarction or substantial scar
Giant-cell myocardial inflammation on histology is not explained by coronary artery disease

data.description: 32-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 0, with prior CIN II treated by loop excision 2 years earlier and bilateral breast reduction 13 years earlier with delayed but spontaneous wound healing. During pregnancy, she developed chronic hypertension at 18 weeks. At 31 weeks 4 days, she presented with 2 weeks of flu-like symptoms, then lower abdominal pain and fever. Exam showed temperature 38.3°C, uterine contractions, fundal height of 29 weeks, cervix 1 cm dilated and fully effaced with intact membranes. Ultrasound showed fetal growth at the 5th percentile and oligohydramnios; cardiotocography showed fetal heart rate 160 bpm with late decelerations. Labs revealed leukocytosis with neutrophilia and markedly elevated CRP. She underwent cesarean section for suspected fetal distress and then developed persistent postoperative fever, rising inflammatory markers, and a non-healing surgical wound despite standard wound care and antibiotics.
A rare neutrophilic dermatosis causing rapidly progressive painful ulceration and wound breakdown after trauma or surgery (pathergy), often mistaken for infection; debridement may worsen the lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Non-healing cesarean surgical wound despite antibiotics and standard wound care
Ulcerative postoperative wound with undermined violaceous-appearing borders and purulent-appearing base
Persistent postoperative fever and elevated inflammatory markers
History of delayed wound healing after prior breast reduction surgery
symptoms_not_in_common: Two-week flu-like illness before presentation
Preterm uterine contractions and cervical dilation
Fetal growth restriction
Oligohydramnios
Fetal tachycardia with late decelerations
Chronic hypertension during pregnancy

data.diagnosis: Post-cesarean surgical-site infection with wound dehiscence
data.description: A bacterial infection involving the cesarean incision that can cause fever, leukocytosis, purulent drainage, tissue separation, and delayed healing.
symptoms_in_common: Rising CRP and leukocytosis with neutrophilia
Open, inflamed cesarean wound with exudative material
Delayed wound healing and wound dehiscence
symptoms_not_in_common: Failure to improve despite appropriate antibiotics and routine wound care
Prior history of unusually delayed postoperative wound healing
Violaceous undermined ulcer-like wound margins suggestive of a neutrophilic dermatosis
Antepartum fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Chronic hypertension

data.diagnosis: Necrotizing fasciitis of the cesarean wound
data.description: A rapidly progressive, life-threatening soft-tissue infection involving fascia, usually producing severe pain, systemic toxicity, tissue necrosis, and worsening postoperative wound destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Marked inflammatory response with neutrophilic leukocytosis and high CRP
Wound breakdown with devitalized or purulent-appearing tissue
Persistent illness despite initial antibiotic treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pain out of proportion to examination
No reported crepitus, skin anesthesia, bullae, or rapidly spreading necrosis
No reported shock or severe hemodynamic instability
History of delayed wound healing after a remote surgery
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are not typical manifestations

data.description: Infection and inflammation of the amniotic fluid, placenta, and fetal membranes, typically associated with maternal fever, uterine tenderness, maternal leukocytosis, fetal tachycardia, and preterm labor.
symptoms_in_common: Uterine contractions and preterm cervical dilation
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent non-healing cesarean wound after delivery
Ulcerative wound dehiscence despite antibiotics
History of delayed healing after breast reduction surgery
Chronic hypertension
Fetal growth restriction is not a defining acute feature

data.diagnosis: Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis), including postoperative pathergy
data.description: An inflammatory neutrophilic skin disorder characterized by fever, neutrophilia, elevated inflammatory markers, and painful inflammatory skin lesions that can occasionally arise at sites of trauma or surgery.
symptoms_in_common: Possible pathergic response after surgical trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: Large destructive ulcer with wound dehiscence is more characteristic of pyoderma gangrenosum
No reported tender erythematous papules or plaques elsewhere on the body
Preterm labor and fetal distress are not typical manifestations
Oligohydramnios and fetal growth restriction are not typical manifestations
Prior delayed surgical wound healing is more suggestive of recurrent postoperative pyoderma gangrenosum

data.description: An 87-year-old man presented with a one-year history of difficulty swallowing, with episodes of choking and aspiration that progressively increased in frequency. Laryngeal examination revealed extraluminal obstruction from behind. The patient had multiple comorbidities as mentioned in the case.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) with large anterior cervical osteophytes
data.description: A noninflammatory disorder characterized by flowing calcification and ossification along spinal ligaments, often producing large anterior cervical osteophytes that can compress the pharynx or esophagus.
symptoms_in_common: Extraluminal obstruction from behind on laryngeal examination
Imaging appearance of prominent anterior cervical bony overgrowth

data.diagnosis: Cervical spondylosis with anterior cervical osteophyte formation
data.description: Degenerative disease of the cervical spine in which osteophytes form at vertebral margins; very large anterior osteophytes can mechanically compress the hypopharynx or esophagus and cause swallowing difficulty.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior extraluminal compression of the laryngeal/pharyngeal region
Cervical bony degenerative changes visible on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No neck pain, stiffness, or radicular arm symptoms were reported

data.diagnosis: Ossification of the anterior longitudinal ligament
data.description: Abnormal calcification or ossification of the anterior longitudinal spinal ligament, often associated with DISH, which may create a bulky anterior cervical mass effect on the pharynx and esophagus.
symptoms_in_common: Extraluminal obstruction from the posterior pharyngeal/laryngeal side
Radiographic suggestion of extensive anterior cervical ligamentous ossification
symptoms_not_in_common: No cervical pain or limitation of neck movement was described

data.diagnosis: Hypopharyngeal or cervical esophageal malignancy causing extrinsic compression
data.description: Tumors involving the hypopharynx, cervical esophagus, or nearby structures can produce progressive dysphagia and aspiration, although they more often cause an intrinsic mucosal lesion rather than a bony posterior compression.
symptoms_not_in_common: The obstruction was described as extraluminal from behind rather than an intrinsic mucosal mass
Imaging suggests cervical bony overgrowth rather than a soft-tissue tumor
No weight loss, odynophagia, hoarseness, neck mass, or bleeding was reported

data.description: A 22-year-old African American/Asian college-age woman presented with a 3-month history of mild exertional dyspnea that progressively worsened despite treatment with inhalers for suspected reactive airway disease. She reported shortness of breath with mild exertion, nonproductive cough for several weeks, and a 5-lb weight loss. She denied fever, chills, headaches, syncope, dizziness, bone pain, nausea, or vomiting. Physical examination was unremarkable except for decreased breath sounds and slight dullness to percussion on the left. Routine laboratory work-up was unremarkable. Initially, chest x-ray showed mediastinal widening, which led to further imaging and biopsy. An open mediastinal biopsy was performed after CT-guided biopsy failed, revealing a poorly differentiated carcinoma initially thought to be thymic carcinoma. Flow cytometry from tissue showed T cells and polyclonal B cells with no immunophenotypic evidence of malignancy.
An aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma arising in the anterior mediastinum, classically affecting young women and often presenting as a bulky mediastinal mass causing respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased left-sided breath sounds and dullness to percussion
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills
No marked constitutional B symptoms
Flow cytometry showing polyclonal B cells without clear immunophenotypic malignancy

data.description: A rare malignant epithelial tumor of the thymus that usually presents as an anterior mediastinal mass and may invade or compress nearby thoracic structures.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior mediastinal mass with mediastinal widening
Biopsy initially interpreted as poorly differentiated carcinoma suspicious for thymic carcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Very young age, as thymic carcinoma is more common in middle-aged adults
No chest pain
No superior vena cava syndrome symptoms
No evidence of metastatic disease or systemic illness described

data.description: A rare, highly aggressive poorly differentiated carcinoma driven by NUTM1 rearrangement, often arising in midline thoracic structures and commonly mistaken for thymic carcinoma or other undifferentiated cancers.
symptoms_in_common: Poorly differentiated carcinoma on mediastinal biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively mild and slowly progressive symptoms over 3 months
No fever or severe systemic symptoms
No reported pleural, bone, or distant metastatic symptoms

data.description: A lymphoma frequently affecting young adults and commonly presenting with mediastinal lymphadenopathy; the nodular sclerosis subtype is especially common in young women.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive exertional dyspnea from mediastinal compression
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats reported
No palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy described
Biopsy described as poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than classic Reed-Sternberg-cell lymphoma

data.description: A germ cell tumor arising in the anterior mediastinum, including teratoma, seminoma, or nonseminomatous germ cell tumor; large tumors can cause cough and dyspnea by compressing lung and mediastinal structures.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased breath sounds and dullness on the left, potentially due to mass effect or pleural fluid
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex, since mediastinal seminoma and nonseminomatous germ cell tumors are much more common in males
No reported elevated tumor markers
Pathology reported poorly differentiated carcinoma rather than germ cell tumor

data.description: 71-year-old woman with hematuria and a long history of easy bruising, which worsened at age 66. Past history includes nephrolithiasis at age 41 and osteoporosis (T-score -2.6 at the left femoral neck). Physical examination showed bruising on the lower extremities. Serial testing showed late-night serum cortisol of 70 ng/mL and a Dex-CRH test with cortisol levels of 1.8 µg/dL at 0 minutes and 2 µg/dL at 15 minutes.

data.diagnosis: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia (PBMAH) causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome
data.description: A rare cause of endogenous cortisol excess in which both adrenal glands develop multiple nodules and autonomously produce cortisol, often presenting gradually in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Easy bruising with worsening over time
Elevated late-night serum cortisol suggesting loss of normal circadian cortisol suppression
Abnormal dexamethasone-CRH testing consistent with hypercortisolism
Bilateral adrenal abnormalities suggested by the CT image
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria

data.description: A clinical state of chronic cortisol excess that can result from adrenal, pituitary, or ectopic ACTH-dependent causes. Cortisol excess causes skin fragility, bruising, bone loss, and increased risk of kidney stones.
symptoms_in_common: Failure of cortisol to adequately suppress on dexamethasone-CRH testing
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria
No reported central weight gain
No reported proximal muscle weakness
No reported diabetes or hypertension
No reported facial plethora or purple striae

data.diagnosis: Adrenal Cushing syndrome due to bilateral cortisol-secreting adrenal adenomas
data.description: Autonomous cortisol production from adrenal adenomas can produce ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome. Bilateral adrenal nodules are less common than a single adrenal adenoma but may cause mild or overt cortisol excess.
symptoms_in_common: Adrenal lesions suggested on CT imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria
No reported unilateral adrenal mass
No reported hypokalemia
No reported classic metabolic manifestations such as obesity, hypertension, or hyperglycemia

data.description: 40-year-old black woman with 10 months of progressive lower-extremity edema and abdominal distention/pain. Symptoms began as episodic pain and swelling in the feet and ankles after prolonged standing, then progressed to the lower legs and thighs. Five months before evaluation, she developed left back and flank pain. History includes hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis with previously negative chest radiograph, hysterectomy for fibroid uterus, appendectomy, two vaginal deliveries, and prior ectopic pregnancy. On examination: 2+ edema of the lower and upper legs, jugular venous pressure 8 cm H2O, and a distended, mildly tender abdomen.

A fibroinflammatory disorder causing plaque-like retroperitoneal soft-tissue thickening that can encase the ureters, inferior vena cava, and iliac vessels, producing venous obstruction and flank or abdominal pain.
symptoms_in_common: Edema extending from the ankles to the thighs
Abdominal distention and mild abdominal tenderness
Possible venous obstruction with mildly elevated jugular venous pressure
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial episodic foot and ankle swelling specifically after prolonged standing

data.diagnosis: Inferior vena cava and iliac venous obstruction (inferior vena cava syndrome)
data.description: Obstruction or compression of the inferior vena cava or iliac veins, often from thrombosis, retroperitoneal fibrosis, or a mass, causes impaired venous return from the legs and abdominal wall.
symptoms_in_common: Edema involving the upper legs and thighs
symptoms_not_in_common: None of the reported symptoms are strongly atypical

data.diagnosis: Retroperitoneal malignancy causing venous compression (such as lymphoma)
data.description: Lymphoma or another retroperitoneal tumor can form infiltrative soft tissue around major abdominal vessels and lymphatic channels, resulting in inferior vena cava or iliac venous compression, edema, and abdominal or back pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No reported drenching night sweats
No reported unintentional weight loss
Initial episodic swelling after prolonged standing

data.diagnosis: Abdominopelvic tuberculosis with retroperitoneal lymphadenitis or fibrosis
data.description: Tuberculosis can involve abdominal lymph nodes and the retroperitoneum, occasionally causing fibrotic tissue, vascular compression, abdominal pain, and edema. A history of latent tuberculosis increases consideration of this cause.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive lower-extremity edema if pelvic or retroperitoneal veins are compressed
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No weight loss
No pulmonary symptoms
Previously negative chest radiograph

data.diagnosis: Bilateral lower-extremity lymphedema due to pelvic or retroperitoneal lymphatic obstruction
data.description: Obstruction of pelvic or retroperitoneal lymphatic drainage by fibrosis, malignancy, inflammation, or prior pelvic surgery can cause chronic progressive swelling of both legs and sometimes abdominal wall edema.
symptoms_in_common: Edema progressing from the feet and ankles to the thighs
History of prior pelvic surgery including hysterectomy
symptoms_not_in_common: Jugular venous pressure elevation
Left flank and back pain are less typical in uncomplicated lymphedema
Mild abdominal tenderness is less typical in uncomplicated lymphedema

data.description: A 22 year old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain, jaundice, itching, and fever. His urine was dark and stools pale. Physical examination revealed temperature of 38.7°C, icterus, abdominal tenderness worst in the right upper quadrant with negative Murphy's sign, impalpable gall bladder, inflamed oropharynx with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests showed liver function abnormalities with alkaline phosphatase 327, aspartate aminotransferase 358, and bilirubin 109 suggesting cholestasis. White cell count was elevated at 20.8, C reactive protein was raised at 17, and platelets were low at 168. Monospot test was positive for Epstein Barr virus, confirmed by positive Epstein Barr virus serology. Hepatitis A, B, and C serology were negative.

data.diagnosis: Epstein-Barr virus infectious mononucleosis with cholestatic hepatitis
data.description: Primary Epstein-Barr virus infection causing infectious mononucleosis, with hepatic involvement producing cholestasis, jaundice, and elevated liver enzymes.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated alkaline phosphatase, AST, and bilirubin
Negative hepatitis A, B, and C serology
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked right-upper-quadrant tenderness
Prominent cholestatic jaundice is an uncommon presentation of infectious mononucleosis

data.description: Inflammation of the gallbladder without gallstones, occasionally occurring during Epstein-Barr virus infection and associated with gallbladder wall edema and right-upper-quadrant pain.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance suggestive of gallbladder inflammation without reported gallstones
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Dark urine and pale stools may reflect associated hepatitis rather than isolated cholecystitis

data.description: Bacterial infection of the biliary tract, usually caused by obstruction of the common bile duct; classically presents with fever, jaundice, and right-upper-quadrant pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot test and Epstein-Barr virus serology
No stated bile-duct stone, ductal dilatation, or other obstructing lesion
Young age without reported biliary disease

data.description: Acute inflammation of the gallbladder, usually caused by cystic-duct obstruction from gallstones.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Jaundice with pale stools and dark urine is not typical unless there is additional bile-duct obstruction
Pruritus
Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Epstein-Barr virus testing
No reported gallstones

data.description: Acute liver inflammation caused by hepatotropic viruses or systemic viral infections, which may cause jaundice, abdominal discomfort, dark urine, pale stools, and elevated aminotransferases.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked right-upper-quadrant tenderness suggestive of gallbladder involvement
Leukocytosis is less typical than a normal or low white-cell count
Elevated C-reactive protein
Hepatitis A, B, and C serology were negative
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy is more characteristic of Epstein-Barr virus infectious mononucleosis

data.description:
41-year-old man presented with sudden, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right groin and flank, slightly improved when lying down, with nausea and one episode of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting. Two weeks earlier, he had a similar but milder episode in the left lower quadrant radiating to the left flank that resolved spontaneously. He also reported several months of fatigue, but denied fever, weight loss, chest pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. He had no known medical problems or medications, smoked one pack per day for 26 years, and drank alcohol socially. 

On exam, he was uncomfortable, afebrile, hypertensive, with diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding and bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness, worse on the right. Labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia, mild anemia, elevated creatinine, elevated LDH, elevated ESR and CRP, and bland urinalysis. Serologic and hypercoagulability testing was negative/normal.

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa (PAN) with renal artery involvement
data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause renal arterial stenoses, microaneurysms, thrombosis, and renal infarctions. Angiography often shows multiple small aneurysms and irregular vessel narrowing.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe flank and abdominal pain
Elevated LDH consistent with tissue infarction
Renal imaging compatible with bilateral renal infarctions and arterial abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No weight loss
No skin manifestations such as livedo reticularis, nodules, or purpura
No peripheral neuropathy
No gastrointestinal ischemic symptoms such as postprandial pain or bloody stool

data.description: Acute interruption of renal arterial blood flow causing ischemic necrosis of renal tissue. It may result from vasculitis, arterial dissection, embolism, thrombosis, or severe atherosclerotic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe flank and abdominal pain
Imaging showing bilateral renal perfusion defects/infarcts
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue is nonspecific
No hematuria, which can occur with renal infarction
No fever, although low-grade fever may occur

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory disorder of medium-sized arteries that produces alternating stenosis and dilation, often described as a 'string-of-beads' appearance. Renal involvement can cause hypertension, dissection, thrombosis, or renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Flank and abdominal pain if renal artery dissection or infarction occurs
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP are not typical because fibromuscular dysplasia is not inflammatory
Leukocytosis is not typical
Markedly elevated LDH is only expected if complicated by renal infarction
The patient is a middle-aged man, whereas renal fibromuscular dysplasia is more common in women

data.description: Renal infarction can occur when an embolus from the heart or a proximal artery obstructs a renal artery branch. Common causes include atrial fibrillation, endocarditis, ventricular thrombus, or hypercoagulable states.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe flank and abdominal pain
Bland or minimally abnormal urinalysis can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No known atrial fibrillation or structural heart disease
No chest pain or symptoms of embolic heart disease
Hypercoagulability testing was negative

data.description: A 13-month-old male infant presented to the Department of Dermatology with a single asymptomatic plaque on the lower back that was first noticed by parents at approximately 4 months of age. During observation, the lesion gradually became larger and firmer, and intermittent sweating on the surface was noticed.

A rare benign childhood soft-tissue hamartoma, usually presenting before age 2 years as a painless, firm, slowly enlarging subcutaneous mass or plaque on the trunk, axilla, shoulder, or upper arm. It is composed of fibrous tissue, primitive mesenchyme, and fat.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent sweating over the lesion is not a classic feature, although it may occur when cutaneous adnexexal structures are involved

data.description: A benign congenital proliferation of dermal smooth muscle, commonly involving the lumbosacral region. It usually appears as a skin-colored or hyperpigmented plaque and may become more prominent with growth; hypertrichosis is common.
symptoms_in_common: Gradual increase in size and firmness
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent sweating over the plaque is not typical
No hypertrichosis or pseudo-Darier sign was described

data.description: A benign hamartoma containing eccrine sweat glands and vascular structures. It often presents in childhood as a solitary nodule or plaque and may be associated with focal hyperhidrosis, hypertrichosis, discoloration, or pain.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent focal sweating on the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-back location is less common than distal extremity involvement
No pain or tenderness was reported
No blue, red, or violaceous vascular discoloration was described

data.description: A localized benign hamartoma characterized by an increased number or size of eccrine sweat glands. It generally presents as a localized plaque with focal hyperhidrosis, often beginning in childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent excessive sweating confined to the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive firmness and a deep subcutaneous component are less typical
Lower-back location is less characteristic than extremity involvement

data.description: A 15-year-old boy presented with recent onset of breathlessness, weight loss, and tiredness for two months and a crusting erythematous scalp rash for six months. The investigations revealed neutrophilia, raised C-reactive protein (CRP), and Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). The blood urea and electrolytes, thyroid function tests, anti-nuclear antibodies, and clotting studies were normal

data.diagnosis: Multisystem Langerhans cell histiocytosis with pulmonary involvement
data.description: A clonal inflammatory disorder characterized by infiltration of tissues by Langerhans cells. In children it can involve skin, bone, lungs, liver, and other organs. Pulmonary disease may produce nodules and cystic or cavitary changes, while scalp lesions can resemble seborrheic dermatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Raised ALT, suggesting possible hepatic involvement
Diffuse bilateral cystic/nodular pulmonary abnormalities on imaging
Possible bony sternal lesion on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal clotting studies despite raised ALT
No reported bone pain, diabetes insipidus, lymphadenopathy, or hepatosplenomegaly

data.description: An inherited disorder of impaired mucociliary clearance that causes recurrent respiratory infections, chronic sinus disease, and progressive bronchiectasis. Some affected patients have situs inversus, known as Kartagener syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse bilateral bronchiectatic/cystic-appearing lung changes on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash
Weight loss without a reported history of recurrent chest infections or chronic sinus symptoms
Raised ALT
Possible sternal bone lesion
No situs inversus reported

data.description: A primary immunodeficiency, often caused by STAT3 pathway abnormalities, characterized by eczema-like dermatitis, recurrent bacterial lung infections, lung cysts or pneumatoceles, and bronchiectasis.
symptoms_in_common: Weight loss and fatigue associated with chronic infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of recurrent severe skin or respiratory infections
No reported eosinophilia or markedly elevated IgE
No reported characteristic skeletal, dental, or facial features
Raised ALT is not a typical core feature

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis with post-infectious bronchiectatic or cavitary disease
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause constitutional symptoms, chronic pulmonary inflammation, upper-lobe cavitation, and bronchiectasis. Cutaneous tuberculosis or a coincidental scalp infection may cause skin lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral upper-lung-predominant cystic/cavitary or bronchiectatic changes on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash is not typical of pulmonary tuberculosis
No reported fever, night sweats, cough, sputum production, hemoptysis, or tuberculosis exposure
Raised ALT is nonspecific
Possible sternal lesion would require separate confirmation

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Adult pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis

diagnoses.name: Skeletal involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Langerhans cell histiocytosis

data.description: A 40-year-old woman presented with a palpable lump in her left superior breast. Mammography and US and biopsy performed, confirming invasive carcinoma NST Grade 2. MRI performed pre-operatively due to occult on mammography. Subsequent left breast mastectomy and reconstruction with right breast mastopexy.

data.diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (NST), grade 2
data.description: The most common form of invasive breast cancer, previously termed invasive ductal carcinoma. Grade 2 indicates intermediate histologic differentiation.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable lump in the left superior breast
Suspicious breast lesion detected on ultrasound
Biopsy confirmation of invasive carcinoma NST, grade 2
Enhancing left breast mass on preoperative MRI
Mammographically occult tumor in dense breast tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: No breast pain was reported
No nipple discharge was reported
No skin dimpling, erythema, or nipple retraction was reported

data.diagnosis: Multifocal or multicentric invasive breast carcinoma
data.description: Breast cancer involving more than one malignant focus in the same breast; MRI is often used to assess the full extent of disease when mammography is limited by dense tissue or occult lesions.
symptoms_in_common: MRI performed for preoperative evaluation because the lesion was occult on mammography
MRI demonstrates an extensive enhancing abnormality in the left breast
Treatment with mastectomy is consistent with disease that may be extensive or have multiple foci
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple separate biopsy-proven breast lesions were not explicitly described
No nipple or skin involvement was reported
No contralateral breast malignancy was described

data.diagnosis: Breast carcinoma with possible internal mammary lymph node metastasis
data.description: Invasive breast cancer can spread to regional lymph nodes, including axillary and internal mammary nodes. MRI may identify suspicious enhancing internal mammary-chain nodes during staging.
symptoms_in_common: MRI findings suggest a possible enhancing lesion/node along the internal mammary region
Mastectomy was performed for the primary left breast cancer
symptoms_not_in_common: No pathologic confirmation of nodal metastasis was provided
No enlarged axillary lymph nodes were reported
No systemic symptoms or distant metastatic symptoms were reported

data.description: A 68-year-old woman with a longstanding history of non-specific inflammatory arthritis presented with a three-month history of flashing lights and blurred vision. She had been taking 400 mg hydroxychloroquine daily for 15 years, along with meloxicam, omeprazole, and amitriptyline. She was of normal body weight. Ophthalmological assessment revealed reduced visual acuity at 6/18 in the right eye and 6/12 in the left eye, with mild depression in color vision on Ishihara plate testing. Early cataracts were present.

A toxic maculopathy caused by long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure, producing parafoveal retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor damage. Risk rises substantially with prolonged treatment and high cumulative dose.
symptoms_in_common: Long-term hydroxychloroquine use at 400 mg daily for 15 years
Reduced visual acuity in both eyes
Bilateral central/paracentral visual-field defects consistent with a ring scotoma
Retinal imaging appearance suggestive of bilateral parafoveal macular damage
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are less typical than blurred vision, reading difficulty, paracentral scotomas, and color-vision changes
Early cataracts are not caused by hydroxychloroquine retinopathy

data.diagnosis: Autoimmune retinopathy associated with inflammatory arthritis
data.description: An immune-mediated retinal degeneration that may occur with systemic autoimmune disease and can cause photoreceptor dysfunction, visual-field loss, reduced color vision, photopsias, and progressive visual impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Very prolonged hydroxychloroquine exposure strongly favors drug-induced retinopathy instead
The characteristic parafoveal/ring-scotoma pattern is more typical of hydroxychloroquine toxicity
Early cataracts do not specifically support autoimmune retinopathy

data.diagnosis: Retinitis pigmentosa or a related inherited retinal dystrophy
data.description: A group of inherited retinal degenerations characterized by progressive photoreceptor loss, often beginning with night blindness and peripheral field constriction, with possible later central visual and color-vision impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Age of onset at 68 years is atypical for most inherited retinal dystrophies
No reported night blindness
No reported longstanding peripheral field constriction
No reported family history of retinal disease
Long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure provides a more likely explanation
The described parafoveal pattern is not the classic peripheral bone-spicule pattern of retinitis pigmentosa

data.description: 50-year-old woman, current smoker with a 35 pack-year history, presented with right nasal congestion and right parotid swelling unresponsive to antibiotics and steroids. Exam and nasal endoscopy showed right-predominant adenoid pad swelling. CT revealed a 4.1 cm nasopharyngeal soft tissue mass. Initial biopsy showed atypical lymphoid hyperplasia with scattered large atypical CD30-positive cells; flow cytometry showed no clonal B cells. After adenoidectomy, MRI at 3 months showed recurrence. Repeat endoscopic excision showed a nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes. PET-CT showed FDG uptake confined to the nasopharynx without lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow biopsy was negative; stage IEA disease was established.

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal classical Hodgkin lymphoma of the nasopharynx, likely lymphocyte-rich subtype
data.description: A rare localized form of classical Hodgkin lymphoma arising in nasopharyngeal lymphoid tissue. It is characterized by rare Reed-Sternberg cells in an inflammatory background; the malignant cells typically express CD30 and CD15.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells expressing CD30 and CD15
No clonal B-cell population on flow cytometry
symptoms_not_in_common: Right parotid swelling is not a classic direct manifestation, although it may reflect adjacent inflammatory or lymphatic involvement
Absence of lymphadenopathy is unusual for Hodgkin lymphoma but compatible with rare stage I extranodal disease
No reported B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.description: An indolent Hodgkin lymphoma composed of neoplastic lymphocyte-predominant cells in a background of small B lymphocytes. It usually involves peripheral lymph nodes and typically expresses CD20 and B-cell markers rather than CD15/CD30.
symptoms_in_common: Predominance of small lymphocytes in the recurrent specimen
Localized stage I disease without bone marrow involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Atypical large cells positive for CD30
Atypical large cells positive for CD15
Nasopharyngeal presentation is uncommon
Absence of a clonal B-cell population does not support a B-cell-derived lymphocyte-predominant lymphoma

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma composed of large pleomorphic anaplastic lymphoid cells. It may arise in lymph nodes or extranodal tissues and can mimic classical Hodgkin lymphoma histologically.
symptoms_in_common: No clonal B-cell population on flow cytometry
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity favors classical Hodgkin lymphoma over anaplastic large cell lymphoma
Predominant small-lymphocyte background with rare Reed-Sternberg-like cells is less typical
No reported T-cell immunophenotype or ALK status
No lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms

data.description: A localized Epstein-Barr virus-associated B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder that usually occurs in immunosuppressed or elderly patients and produces sharply circumscribed mucosal ulcers containing Hodgkin-like CD30-positive atypical cells.
symptoms_in_common: Can contain cells resembling Reed-Sternberg cells
Localized disease without bone marrow involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is described as a bulky recurrent nasopharyngeal mass rather than a mucosal ulcer
No reported immunosuppression
No reported EBV positivity
CD15 positivity and the overall staging pattern more strongly support classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: An epithelial malignancy arising from the nasopharyngeal mucosa, often associated with EBV in endemic populations. It commonly presents with nasal obstruction, neck lymphadenopathy, otologic symptoms, or cranial neuropathies.
symptoms_in_common: Smoking history increases risk for head and neck malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy demonstrated a lymphoid infiltrate rather than malignant epithelial cells
CD30-positive and CD15-positive large atypical lymphoid cells are not typical of nasopharyngeal carcinoma
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Recurrent small-lymphocyte-rich nodular infiltrate is not characteristic of carcinoma

data.description: 83-year-old woman with hypertension and biopsy-proven vaginal melanoma diagnosed 4 months earlier, with invasive locoregional disease and a 3-mm left upper lobe lung nodule on PET-CT. She received four cycles of ipilimumab, last dose 3 weeks before admission, and developed pruritus, lethargy, malaise after the third dose and diarrhea after the fourth. For 2 weeks before admission, she had worsening substernal chest pain and progressive dyspnea. On admission, ECG showed sinus tachycardia with 1 mm ST elevations in leads I, V2, and V3; troponin-I was elevated at 0.98 ng/mL and ESR was 65 mm/hr. Echocardiography showed EF 50% with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, peak gradient 100 mmHg, and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Cardiac catheterization showed isolated 30% proximal LAD stenosis without thrombus.

Inflammatory myocardial injury caused by immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy; it can present with chest pain, troponin elevation, ECG changes, heart failure symptoms, and nonobstructive coronary arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Recent ipilimumab treatment, with last dose 3 weeks before presentation
ST-segment elevations in leads I, V2, and V3
Only mild nonobstructive LAD disease on cardiac catheterization
Mildly reduced left ventricular ejection fraction
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction with a 100 mmHg gradient
Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
Diarrhea and pruritus, which are more suggestive of additional immune-related adverse events

data.diagnosis: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated cardiac sarcoid-like granulomatous inflammation
data.description: A sarcoid-like immune reaction induced by checkpoint blockade can cause granulomatous inflammation involving the myocardium, producing inflammatory cardiac uptake on PET imaging, myocardial injury, and conduction or functional abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Nonobstructive coronary angiography despite myocardial injury
Cardiac PET-CT appearance suggestive of focal myocardial inflammatory activity
Systemic immune-related symptoms including pruritus, malaise, and diarrhea
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hilar lymphadenopathy, pulmonary infiltrates, uveitis, or other classic systemic sarcoidosis manifestations
Severe LV outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior mitral motion is not a typical primary presentation
No reported ventricular arrhythmia or atrioventricular conduction block

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome with myocardial infarction and nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: Myocardial infarction can occur despite the absence of obstructive epicardial coronary disease, including from coronary vasospasm, microvascular dysfunction, embolism, or transient plaque disruption.
symptoms_in_common: Nonobstructive coronary angiography with only 30% proximal LAD stenosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent ipilimumab exposure with preceding immune-related symptoms strongly favors immune-mediated inflammation
Elevated ESR is less specific for typical ischemic infarction
Two-week progressive course is less typical for an acute plaque-rupture infarction
Dynamic LV outflow tract obstruction and systolic anterior mitral motion are not typical consequences of MINOCA

data.diagnosis: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy or dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
data.description: Dynamic obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract occurs when systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve narrows the outflow tract; it may be due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or be provoked by hypercontractility, dehydration, or systemic illness.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Peak LV outflow tract gradient of 100 mmHg
Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
Preserved to mildly reduced ejection fraction
symptoms_not_in_common: ST-segment elevations and elevated troponin are not typical unless there is secondary demand ischemia
Recent ipilimumab treatment and immune-related pruritus, malaise, and diarrhea are not explained
Elevated ESR is not typical
No reported asymmetric septal hypertrophy or prior history of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

data.description: 33-year-old bisexual Brazilian man with 4 months of painful bowel movements and bright red rectal bleeding on toilet paper, occurring with one daily bowel movement. He denied abdominal pain and weight loss. History included a sexual encounter with a man about 6 weeks before presentation. Initial exam showed a tender external hemorrhoid and normal vital signs. Follow-up exam 10 weeks later showed bleeding hemorrhoids around the anus. Surgical clinic exam found large superficial anal fissures at the anterior and posterior midline anal verge with small-to-moderate sentinel skin tags; digital rectal exam showed moderate tenderness. Anoscopy showed fissures and small internal hemorrhoids. Flexible sigmoidoscopy revealed mild-to-moderate distal rectal mucosal inflammation over the distal 10 cm with edema and patchy erythema. HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C tests were negative.

Sexually transmitted Treponema pallidum infection involving the rectum, which can cause inflammatory proctitis, rectal bleeding, pain, fissures, and ulcerative lesions. The histology and spirochete immunostaining are strongly supportive.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual encounter with a male partner
Distal rectal inflammation with edema and patchy erythema
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding external and internal hemorrhoids

data.diagnosis: Chlamydia trachomatis proctitis, including lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV)
data.description: Sexually acquired rectal infection, particularly common after receptive anal exposure, that may cause proctitis with rectal pain, bleeding, discharge, mucosal inflammation, and occasionally ulceration or fissuring. LGV serovars can cause more severe inflammatory disease.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual exposure with a male partner
symptoms_not_in_common: Large superficial anterior and posterior midline anal fissures are less typical
Sentinel skin tags are not a usual primary feature
Hemorrhoids are not caused by chlamydial proctitis

data.description: Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection of the rectum acquired through sexual contact. It commonly causes anorectal discomfort, tenesmus, rectal discharge, mucosal erythema, and sometimes bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Recent sexual exposure with a male partner
Distal rectal mucosal erythema and inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No rectal purulent or mucopurulent discharge was reported
