Large chronic-appearing anal fissures with sentinel tags are not typical
Hemorrhoids are not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: HSV infection of the anorectum, usually sexually acquired, can cause severe anorectal pain, painful defecation, bleeding, ulcerations, and inflammatory proctitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No painful perianal vesicles or discrete ulcerations were described
Four months of persistent symptoms is less typical of untreated primary HSV proctitis
Sentinel tags and midline fissures are not classic HSV findings
Hemorrhoids are not typical

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory bowel disease, especially ulcerative proctitis or Crohn disease involving the anus
data.description: Inflammatory bowel disease can involve the rectum and anus. Ulcerative proctitis typically causes rectal bleeding and mucosal inflammation, while Crohn disease can produce anal fissures and skin tags.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent sexual exposure suggests an infectious sexually transmitted cause
No abdominal pain was reported
No weight loss was reported
Only one bowel movement daily, without reported diarrhea, urgency, or tenesmus

data.description: 65-year-old man with a history of hypertension and prior laminectomy, evaluated with a normal PSA and normal digital rectal examination. Urine dipstick was largely normal, with trace blood only.
The presence of a small amount of blood in urine detected on dipstick testing without urinary symptoms; it may be benign or require evaluation for urinary tract, kidney, or prostate causes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal PSA
Normal digital rectal examination

data.description: Noncancerous enlargement of the prostate that commonly affects older men and can cause lower urinary tract symptoms or occasionally hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: Trace blood on urine dipstick can occasionally occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported urinary frequency, urgency, weak stream, hesitancy, or nocturia
Normal digital rectal examination
Normal PSA

data.diagnosis: Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder or urinary tract
data.description: A cancer arising from the lining of the bladder or upper urinary tract, often presenting with painless microscopic or visible hematuria, particularly in older adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Only trace rather than persistent or gross hematuria is reported
No urinary irritative symptoms such as urgency, frequency, or dysuria
No reported weight loss or pelvic pain

data.description: Kidney or ureteral stones can cause blood in the urine, often with sudden flank pain, nausea, or urinary discomfort.
symptoms_not_in_common: No flank or abdominal pain
No nausea or vomiting
No dysuria or urinary urgency
No reported history of kidney stones

data.description: An infection of the bladder, urethra, or kidneys that may cause dysuria, urinary frequency, urgency, fever, and occasionally microscopic hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: Trace blood on urine dipstick can occur with urinary tract infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Urine dipstick was otherwise largely normal
No dysuria
No urinary frequency or urgency
No fever or systemic symptoms
No flank pain

data.description: 20-year-old male with a history of neonatal bleeding tendency and a family history of easy bruising in his father. He was evaluated preoperatively for chronic maxillary sinusitis surgery. He also had conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis. Initial coagulation tests showed prolonged PT and aPTT with normal bleeding time; mixing studies suggested factor deficiency. Fibrinogen activity was markedly low by Clauss method with normal fibrinogen antigen level. Blood counts and serum chemistry were normal. Parents had normal coagulation tests and fibrinogen activity.

An inherited qualitative fibrinogen disorder in which fibrinogen antigen concentration is normal or near normal, but the fibrinogen molecule has impaired function, causing reduced functional fibrinogen activity and variable bleeding or thrombosis risk.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing studies consistent with a factor deficiency rather than an inhibitor
Markedly low fibrinogen activity by Clauss assay
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic maxillary sinusitis
Conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis

data.description: An inherited fibrinogen disorder characterized by both reduced fibrinogen quantity and impaired fibrinogen function. It may cause bleeding, thrombosis, or be discovered during preoperative coagulation screening.
symptoms_in_common: Very low functional fibrinogen activity by Clauss method
Normal blood counts and serum chemistry
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen level, which favors pure dysfibrinogenemia over hypodysfibrinogenemia
Chronic maxillary sinusitis
Conductive hearing loss after meningitis

data.description: An inherited quantitative fibrinogen deficiency caused by absent or reduced production of fibrinogen, typically producing low fibrinogen antigen and activity with bleeding beginning early in life.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen level, which is not typical because antigen is usually decreased or absent
Family history limited to easy bruising with normal parental coagulation tests
Chronic maxillary sinusitis
Conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis

data.diagnosis: Acquired dysfibrinogenemia due to liver disease or systemic illness
data.description: A secondary qualitative fibrinogen abnormality that can occur with liver disease, malignancy, autoimmune disease, or other systemic disorders and may lead to discordance between fibrinogen activity and antigen levels.
symptoms_in_common: Low fibrinogen activity with relatively preserved fibrinogen antigen
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding tendency present since the neonatal period
Family history of easy bruising
Normal serum chemistry
Normal blood counts
Young age without evidence of liver disease, malignancy, or autoimmune disease
Chronic maxillary sinusitis
Conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis

data.description: 60-year-old man with 1 year of progressive exertional dyspnea, worse over the preceding 4 months, accompanied by persistent nonproductive cough. He developed a 5-day history of sore throat, orthopnea, and swelling of the neck and both arms, with facial flushing/redness. He was transferred for evaluation of new dyspnea, cough, neck swelling, and a lung mass. At the outside hospital, he was afebrile with normal oxygen saturation; examination showed flushed face, swollen neck, and absent breath sounds in the right lung fields. History notable for heavy tobacco use (2 packs/day for 40 years), occasional marijuana use, regular alcohol intake, and maternal pancreatic cancer.

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary pleomorphic carcinoma (giant cell carcinoma of the lung)
data.description: A rare, aggressive non-small-cell lung carcinoma composed of poorly differentiated spindle and/or giant tumor cells, strongly associated with heavy smoking and often presenting as a large central lung mass.
symptoms_in_common: Absent breath sounds over the right lung fields
Facial flushing and neck/bilateral arm swelling from tumor-related superior vena cava obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute sore throat
Normal oxygen saturation despite substantial symptoms
Afebrile status

data.description: An aggressive neuroendocrine lung cancer strongly linked to smoking. It commonly arises centrally, grows rapidly, causes bulky mediastinal adenopathy, and may compress or invade the superior vena cava.
symptoms_in_common: Findings compatible with superior vena cava syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: One year of relatively gradual symptoms before rapid worsening is less characteristic of the usually rapidly progressive course
Sore throat is not a typical presenting symptom
No reported systemic paraneoplastic manifestations

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung
data.description: A non-small-cell lung cancer strongly associated with tobacco use that often develops as a central bronchial mass and can obstruct an airway or invade mediastinal structures.
symptoms_in_common: Absent right-sided breath sounds suggesting airway obstruction or lung collapse
Mediastinal compression causing neck and arm swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Nonproductive rather than bloody cough
No reported chest pain
No reported weight loss or anorexia
Sore throat is not typical

data.description: The most common non-small-cell lung cancer, usually peripheral but sometimes central; advanced disease can involve mediastinal lymph nodes and produce superior vena cava obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Neck and bilateral arm swelling due to superior vena cava obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: A large central obstructing mass is less typical than for squamous or small-cell carcinoma
Absent breath sounds on the right are less typical unless there is major airway obstruction or effusion
Sore throat is not typical

data.diagnosis: Superior vena cava syndrome secondary to an intrathoracic malignancy
data.description: A clinical syndrome caused by obstruction of the superior vena cava, most often from lung cancer or mediastinal malignancy, resulting in impaired venous drainage from the head, neck, and upper extremities.
symptoms_in_common: Thoracic/lung mass likely causing venous obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat is not a classic feature
Absent breath sounds in the right lung is not caused directly by superior vena cava obstruction
The year-long progressive cough and dyspnea suggest the underlying lung disease rather than the venous syndrome itself

diagnoses.name: Poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the lung
diagnoses.title: lung adenocarcinoma

data.description: Male infant born at term to healthy nonconsanguineous parents, with no family history of immune deficiency, presented at 20 days of age with profound T-cell lymphopenia detected on newborn screening (absent TRECs). Physical findings included neonatal teeth, hypotonia, umbilical hernia, and erythematous psoriaform dermatitis. Imaging showed wormian skull bones, mild pulmonary artery stenosis, and agenesis of the corpus callosum. No maternal engraftment was found.

data.diagnosis: BCL11B-related disorder with severe T-cell immunodeficiency
data.description: A de novo BCL11B-related developmental and immune disorder that can cause severe T-cell lymphopenia or SCID, neurodevelopmental abnormalities, craniofacial/skeletal findings, and skin disease.
symptoms_in_common: Craniofacial or skeletal abnormalities, including wormian skull bones
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Umbilical hernia
Mild pulmonary artery stenosis

data.diagnosis: Complete DiGeorge syndrome / congenital athymia due to 22q11.2 deletion or related thymic-development defect
data.description: A disorder of thymic development causing profound T-cell deficiency, often detected by absent TRECs. It may occur with congenital heart defects and developmental abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital cardiac abnormality, including pulmonary artery stenosis
Central nervous system malformation such as agenesis of the corpus callosum
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Psoriaform dermatitis
Umbilical hernia

data.diagnosis: PAX1 deficiency / otofaciocervical syndrome type 2 with severe combined immunodeficiency
data.description: A rare disorder caused by biallelic PAX1 variants that impairs thymic development and can produce profound T-cell immunodeficiency together with craniofacial, skeletal, and congenital structural abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Psoriaform dermatitis
Agenesis of the corpus callosum
Umbilical hernia

data.diagnosis: CHARGE syndrome with thymic hypoplasia or athymia
data.description: A CHD7-related multisystem developmental syndrome that can include impaired thymic development with T-cell lymphopenia, congenital heart disease, hypotonia, and brain abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: T-cell lymphopenia with abnormal newborn TREC screening
Agenesis of the corpus callosum or other brain malformations
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Psoriaform dermatitis
Umbilical hernia
Absence of typical reported CHARGE features such as coloboma, choanal atresia, ear anomalies, or genital anomalies

data.description: A thymic epithelial-cell developmental disorder causing severe T-cell immunodeficiency, classically associated with congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy.
symptoms_in_common: No evidence of maternal T-cell engraftment
symptoms_not_in_common: Thick scalp hair rather than congenital alopecia
Psoriaform dermatitis rather than the classic hair and nail phenotype
Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Umbilical hernia
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Agenesis of the corpus callosum

data.description: 47-year-old male with tenesmus and mucoid stool, admitted from a local clinic. He had a 20-year smoking history (1 pack/day) and no alcohol use. Past history included pulmonary tuberculosis 20 years earlier, treated for 9 months. On admission he was in good general condition, without weight loss, fever, or night sweats. Physical examination was unremarkable except for a depressed anterior chest wall; no lymphadenopathy, lungs clear, and heart sounds normal. Labs were largely normal. Chest radiograph showed a residual right upper lung field scar consistent with prior tuberculosis. Upper endoscopy showed a healed duodenal bulb ulcer with negative rapid urease test. Abdominal CT showed no lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow aspiration/biopsy was unremarkable.

data.diagnosis: Primary colorectal extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue. In the colon or rectum it may present as localized mucosal nodules, polyps, ulcerated lesions, or a mass, with histology showing small lymphoid-cell infiltration and lymphoepithelial lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Localized colorectal lesion on endoscopic imaging
No fever, night sweats, or weight loss, which is common in localized indolent MALT lymphoma
No lymphadenopathy on examination or abdominal CT
Unremarkable bone marrow biopsy, supporting localized extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Depressed anterior chest wall
Remote treated pulmonary tuberculosis
Healed duodenal bulb ulcer

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the colon or rectum
data.description: An aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can involve the gastrointestinal tract and cause a colorectal mass, altered bowel habits, bleeding, abdominal pain, or obstructive symptoms. It may arise de novo or by transformation of an indolent lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Possible colorectal mass or mucosal lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Good general condition
No weight loss
No fever or night sweats
No lymphadenopathy
Normal laboratory studies
Unremarkable bone marrow biopsy
Depressed anterior chest wall
Remote treated pulmonary tuberculosis

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the colon or rectum. Rectal tumors commonly cause tenesmus, mucus discharge, bleeding, altered stool caliber, and bowel-habit changes.
symptoms_in_common: Age compatible with possible colorectal malignancy
Smoking history as a modest colorectal cancer risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No anemia or notable laboratory abnormalities
No reported rectal bleeding
Histologic appearance of dense lymphoid infiltration rather than malignant gland formation
No lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Remote pulmonary tuberculosis
Depressed anterior chest wall

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease causing continuous mucosal inflammation beginning in the rectum. Proctitis can produce urgency, tenesmus, mucus discharge, diarrhea, and rectal bleeding.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported diarrhea
No rectal bleeding
No abdominal pain
No systemic inflammatory symptoms
Normal laboratory studies
Localized mass-like lesion rather than typical diffuse continuous colitis
Histology suggestive of a lymphoid neoplasm rather than chronic active colitis
Remote pulmonary tuberculosis
Depressed anterior chest wall

data.description: 24-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented with 2 days of left leg pain, swelling, erythema, and warmth extending from the thigh to the calf, with crampy pain radiating to the left lower abdomen and buttock and exertional dyspnea. She denied fever, chest pain, dyspnea at rest, or trauma. Vital signs were notable for tachycardia (pulse 102 bpm). History included oral contraceptive use since age 15, prior smoking (3 cigarettes/day, quit 2 years earlier), and a family history of DVT in her father after knee surgery. Labs showed mild leukocytosis (WBC 12,000/mm³) with otherwise normal blood counts and coagulation studies.

data.diagnosis: Acute extensive left iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
data.description: A blood clot in the deep veins of the left leg and pelvis, often causing unilateral swelling, pain, erythema, and warmth. In this case, risk factors include estrogen-containing oral contraceptives and possible inherited predisposition.
symptoms_in_common: Pain extending from thigh to calf
Crampy pain radiating toward the lower abdomen and buttock
symptoms_not_in_common: Exertional dyspnea

data.description: Pulmonary embolism is obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus, most commonly originating from a lower-extremity DVT. The chest CT image is consistent with emboli in pulmonary arterial branches.
symptoms_in_common: Acute lower-extremity symptoms suggestive of a source DVT
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain
No dyspnea at rest
Marked unilateral leg erythema and warmth
Crampy left lower abdominal and buttock pain

data.diagnosis: May-Thurner syndrome (left iliac vein compression syndrome) with iliofemoral DVT
data.description: May-Thurner syndrome is compression of the left common iliac vein by the overlying right common iliac artery, predisposing young women to extensive left-sided pelvic and leg DVT. The pelvic CT finding is compatible with left iliac venous thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Left lower abdominal and buttock pain suggesting pelvic venous involvement
Oral contraceptive use as an additional thrombosis risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior history of chronic left leg swelling or venous insufficiency symptoms
No reported recurrent prior DVT

data.diagnosis: Cellulitis of the left lower extremity
data.description: Cellulitis is a bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue that can cause localized warmth, redness, swelling, tenderness, and leukocytosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Symptoms extending from thigh to calf with pelvic/buttock pain
Exertional dyspnea
Tachycardia in the setting of suspected thromboembolism
Oral contraceptive use and family history favoring venous thrombosis

data.description: Superficial thrombophlebitis is inflammation and thrombosis of a superficial vein, producing localized pain, redness, warmth, and sometimes a palpable tender cord.
symptoms_in_common: Estrogen-containing oral contraceptive use as a thrombotic risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive swelling involving the thigh through calf
Lower abdominal and buttock pain suggesting iliac or pelvic vein involvement
Exertional dyspnea suggesting pulmonary embolism
No reported palpable superficial venous cord
Tachycardia

data.description: 3-year-old boy, born at 41 weeks gestation without perinatal problems, birth weight 3.4kg. Parents were not consanguineous and had no medical history. History of 3 prior hospitalizations for viral pneumonia at 12, 18, and 27 months. Presented with recurrent and persistent pneumonia. Current symptoms included cough, sputum and fever. Physical exam showed: temperature 39.5°C, pulse 129/min, respiration 28/min, BP 95/55 mmHg. Weight 15.3kg (50-75th percentile), height 96.5cm (50-75th percentile). Two 3mm ulcers in uvula, fine crackles in both lung fields, palpable liver 1 finger-breadth below right costal margin, palpable spleen tip.

data.diagnosis: X-linked chronic granulomatous disease (CGD; CYBB/gp91phox deficiency)
data.description: A primary immunodeficiency caused by impaired NADPH oxidase function in phagocytes, resulting in defective oxidative burst and susceptibility to recurrent severe bacterial and fungal infections. The absent oxidative-burst pattern and possible carrier pattern in a female relative strongly support X-linked CGD.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging consistent with significant pulmonary infection or consolidation
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior infections described specifically as viral pneumonia, whereas CGD classically predisposes to bacterial and fungal infections
Normal growth parameters despite recurrent severe infections

data.diagnosis: Autosomal recessive chronic granulomatous disease (NCF1, NCF2, NCF4, or CYBA deficiency)
data.description: A form of CGD caused by defects in other components of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex, also producing an absent or markedly reduced neutrophil oxidative burst and recurrent severe infections.
symptoms_in_common: Repeated severe lower respiratory tract infections
Findings suggestive of defective oxidative burst on flow-cytometric testing
symptoms_not_in_common: No known consanguinity, although autosomal recessive CGD can occur without consanguinity
A carrier-type oxidative-burst pattern in a mother would be more characteristic of X-linked than autosomal recessive CGD

data.description: A primary immunodeficiency caused by defective leukocyte adhesion and migration, leading to recurrent severe bacterial infections, poor wound healing, impaired pus formation, and delayed separation of the umbilical cord.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly can occur with recurrent infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of delayed umbilical cord separation
No poor wound healing or recurrent skin infections described
No absent pus formation described
Oral ulcers are less characteristic
Abnormal oxidative-burst testing would favor CGD rather than leukocyte adhesion deficiency

data.description: A 34-year-old woman presented with acute abdominal and back pain 3 years before evaluation at the oncology clinic. She had been well until this onset. Her medical history was notable for migraines. She did not smoke cigarettes, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. She worked full time as a social worker and lived in New Jersey with her husband and child. Family history included breast cancer in maternal grandmother (70s), uterine cancer in paternal aunt (40s), and colon cancer in two paternal cousins (30s and 50s). On physical examination: temperature 36.5°C, blood pressure 108/78 mm Hg, heart rate 78 beats per minute, body-mass index 27.7. The abdomen had well-healed surgical scars; remainder of physical examination was normal. Laboratory results showed elevated tumor marker CA 19-9 at 110 IU per milliliter (reference <35), while alpha-fetoprotein and carcinoembryonic antigen levels were normal.
A primary adenocarcinoma arising from bile ducts within the liver, often associated with elevated CA 19-9 and a desmoplastic, gland-forming histologic pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Histology showing infiltrative gland-forming adenocarcinoma in fibrotic/desmoplastic stroma
Normal alpha-fetoprotein, which argues against hepatocellular carcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 34 years, since cholangiocarcinoma is more common in older adults
No reported jaundice, pruritus, fever, or weight loss
No known history of primary sclerosing cholangitis, biliary disease, liver fluke exposure, or chronic liver disease

data.diagnosis: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma to the liver
data.description: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is a gland-forming malignancy that commonly elevates CA 19-9 and frequently spreads to the liver.
symptoms_in_common: Liver lesions compatible with metastatic disease
Adenocarcinoma with desmoplastic stromal reaction on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pancreatic mass
No jaundice or biliary obstruction
No unexplained weight loss or anorexia
Age 34 years is substantially younger than typical for pancreatic adenocarcinoma
No reported diabetes mellitus or pancreatitis

data.diagnosis: Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma to the liver
data.description: Colorectal cancer commonly metastasizes to the liver and can show gland-forming adenocarcinoma on biopsy; hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes may cause disease at young ages.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of colon cancer in paternal cousins, including one at a young age
Family history of uterine cancer, which can be associated with Lynch syndrome
symptoms_not_in_common: Carcinoembryonic antigen is normal
CA 19-9 elevation is less characteristic than for pancreaticobiliary tumors
No reported rectal bleeding, altered bowel habits, iron-deficiency anemia, or colon mass
No reported weight loss

data.diagnosis: Gallbladder or extrahepatic biliary tract adenocarcinoma with liver involvement
data.description: Adenocarcinoma arising from the gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts may invade or metastasize to the liver and is often associated with increased CA 19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Adenocarcinoma with biliary-type gland formation and desmoplastic stroma
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported gallbladder mass or biliary-duct primary lesion
No jaundice, dark urine, pale stools, or pruritus
No known gallstones or chronic biliary inflammation
Young age is atypical for gallbladder and extrahepatic biliary tract cancers

data.description: A 37-year-old woman presented with a 4-month history of right facial pain and a 3-month history of progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear lobe. Physical examination revealed a soft swelling in the anteroinferior auricular area that was smooth, elastic, mobile and painful on pressure, but not fluctuant. The facial nerve function was normal and the cervical lymph node was not palpable. There were no systemic symptoms. The patient was screened for metastases, and no lung or abdomen lesions were detected.

A benign smooth-muscle tumor arising from vascular smooth muscle, often presenting as a slow-growing, painful, well-circumscribed mass. Histology typically shows interlacing bundles of bland spindle cells around vascular channels, with smooth-muscle-marker positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive swelling beneath the ear lobe
Soft, smooth, elastic, mobile, nonfluctuant lesion
Possible small calcified focus/phlebolith on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Parotid-region location is uncommon because angioleiomyomas more often occur in the extremities
The lesion is described as soft rather than the more commonly firm consistency

data.diagnosis: Pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland
data.description: The most common benign salivary-gland tumor, usually a slowly enlarging, well-circumscribed and mobile parotid mass. It is generally painless and contains epithelial and myoepithelial elements in a variable stromal background.
symptoms_in_common: Gradually enlarging mass in the parotid/infra-auricular region
symptoms_not_in_common: Painful swelling
Facial pain preceding the swelling
Predominantly spindle-cell smooth-muscle-like histology rather than a mixed epithelial-myoepithelial tumor

data.diagnosis: Schwannoma of the facial nerve or great auricular nerve
data.description: A benign peripheral-nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells. It can produce a slowly growing, mobile mass and pain or paresthesia from nerve involvement; histology may show spindle cells in Antoni A and Antoni B areas.
symptoms_in_common: Normal facial nerve function can occur when the tumor arises from a non-facial sensory nerve or does not significantly impair the facial nerve
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported paresthesia, numbness, or sensory deficit
No facial weakness despite the parotid-region location
Histology lacks the typical reported Antoni A/Antoni B architecture and Verocay bodies

data.description: A rare benign tumor of smooth-muscle differentiation arising in or near the parotid gland, potentially from vascular smooth muscle. It usually forms a circumscribed spindle-cell mass and may be painful when vascular in origin.
symptoms_in_common: No cervical lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Primary leiomyoma in the parotid gland is very rare
Facial pain is not present in every nonvascular leiomyoma

data.diagnosis: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the parotid gland
data.description: A malignant salivary-gland tumor composed of mucous, intermediate, and epidermoid cells. Low-grade tumors may be slow growing, whereas higher-grade tumors may cause pain, fixation, facial nerve dysfunction, or nodal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Pain can occur in malignant salivary-gland tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is mobile, smooth, and elastic rather than infiltrative or fixed
No facial nerve weakness
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No systemic symptoms or distant metastases
Histology is spindle-cell rather than mucous, epidermoid, and intermediate-cell morphology

data.description: At the age of 30 months, the patient began presenting an evolving framework of severe cognitive and neurological impairment, with tetraparesis and mixed spastic-dystonic features, language delay and deafness. Moreover, she has coarse facial features, presenting a high forehead and hypertelorism; her tongue is protruding due to macroglossia.
A rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency, leading to progressive neurodegeneration, coarse facial appearance, dysostosis, and variable hearing loss.
symptoms_in_common: Onset of progressive neurological impairment in early childhood
Tetraparesis with spastic and dystonic motor features
Possible white-matter abnormalities and cerebral atrophy on MRI

data.description: A lysosomal storage disorder caused by impaired degradation of heparan sulfate. It is characterized predominantly by progressive cognitive decline and neurological deterioration, often with mild coarse facial features and hearing impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Early-childhood onset of progressive cognitive and neurological decline
White-matter changes and cerebral volume loss may occur on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked tetraparesis with mixed spastic-dystonic features is less characteristic early in the disease course

data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency. It can cause coarse facies, macroglossia, hearing loss, developmental delay, and progressive neurological disease in severe forms.
symptoms_in_common: Severe cognitive impairment in neuronopathic disease
White-matter abnormalities may be present on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Female sex is atypical because Hunter syndrome is usually X-linked and affects males
Tetraparesis with prominent dystonia is not a classic presenting feature

data.description: A beta-galactosidase deficiency causing accumulation of GM1 ganglioside, with infantile or late-infantile developmental regression, progressive motor impairment, coarse facial features, and skeletal or brain abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Possible cerebral atrophy and white-matter signal abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Deafness is less typical than in several mucopolysaccharidoses or fucosidosis
Hypertelorism is not a defining feature

data.description: A lysosomal storage disorder due to alpha-mannosidase deficiency, characterized by intellectual disability, hearing loss, coarse facial features, speech impairment, skeletal disease, and progressive motor dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe tetraparesis beginning at approximately 30 months is more severe and earlier than is typical
Marked mixed spastic-dystonic phenotype is not the usual dominant presentation

data.description: A male neonate, born at 36+1 weeks gestation via cesarean section due to scarred uterus and fetal heart rate deceleration, weighing 2700g with Apgar scores of 2-8-9. The infant experienced severe asphyxia at birth requiring intubation and chest compressions. After resuscitation, he presented with respiratory distress and difficulty breathing. Following extubation from mechanical ventilation on day 6, the patient developed recurrent inspiratory dyspnea and stridor. The infant had no relevant family history and no history of laryngeal or thoracic surgery.

Impaired movement of both vocal folds, typically leaving them near the midline and causing marked upper-airway obstruction in neonates. It may be congenital or associated with neurologic injury such as hypoxic-ischemic injury after severe asphyxia.
symptoms_in_common: Severe upper-airway obstruction suggested by the very narrow glottic opening on endoscopy
History of severe perinatal asphyxia, which can be associated with neurologic injury affecting vocal-fold mobility
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial respiratory distress immediately after birth may also reflect pulmonary disease from asphyxia rather than vocal-fold paralysis
No family history, although some congenital or syndromic causes can have associated family history

data.description: A congenital form of bilateral vocal-fold immobility presenting in the neonatal period with stridor and airway obstruction; it may be isolated or associated with central nervous system abnormalities or syndromes.
symptoms_in_common: Stridor beginning in the neonatal period
Endoscopic appearance of a markedly narrowed glottic airway with vocal folds near the midline
No prior laryngeal or thoracic surgery
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe birth asphyxia is not required for congenital vocal-fold paralysis
The onset after extubation can suggest an acquired or intubation-related process rather than a purely congenital disorder

data.diagnosis: Posterior glottic stenosis with vocal-fold fixation
data.description: Scar formation or fixation in the posterior glottis can prevent vocal-fold abduction and mimic bilateral vocal-fold paralysis. It is often acquired after airway trauma or prolonged endotracheal intubation.
symptoms_in_common: Narrow glottic airway on endoscopic examination
Recent endotracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation for 6 days
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior glottic stenosis is more often associated with longer or traumatic intubation than the described short neonatal intubation course
The immediate neonatal context and severe asphyxia may favor neurologic bilateral vocal-fold paralysis instead
No history of prior laryngeal surgery

data.diagnosis: Subglottic stenosis due to post-intubation airway injury
data.description: Narrowing below the vocal folds caused by congenital small airway caliber or acquired mucosal injury and scarring after intubation. It commonly causes biphasic or inspiratory stridor after extubation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent mechanical ventilation with endotracheal intubation
Prematurity or near-term birth, which can increase vulnerability to airway injury
symptoms_not_in_common: The endoscopic images primarily suggest a very narrow glottic opening rather than isolated narrowing below the vocal folds
Inspiratory stridor alone is more suggestive of glottic or supraglottic obstruction; subglottic stenosis often produces biphasic stridor
No reported repeated or prolonged intubation

data.description: The most common congenital cause of neonatal stridor, caused by dynamic collapse of immature supraglottic structures during inspiration. Symptoms are usually worse with feeding, crying, or supine positioning.
symptoms_not_in_common: The endoscopic appearance of a fixed, severely narrowed glottic opening is not typical of laryngomalacia
Symptoms became prominent after extubation rather than being clearly present from birth
No reported worsening with feeding, crying, or supine position
No described supraglottic collapse or omega-shaped epiglottis

diagnoses.name: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis
diagnoses.title: Paralysis of vocal cords or larynx[Bilateral]

data.description: 24-year-old man presented with a 2-day history of swelling on the left side of neck and fever. Past medical history included two similar neck abscesses 2 years and 6 years ago, which were treated with antibiotics and drainage. Physical examination showed a 2 cm diameter swelling at the level of thyroid cartilage.

data.diagnosis: Fourth branchial pouch anomaly with pyriform sinus fistula
data.description: A congenital tract arising from the pyriform sinus that commonly causes recurrent infected left-sided neck abscesses, often near the thyroid gland or thyroid cartilage.
symptoms_in_common: Swelling at the level of the thyroid cartilage
History of prior drainage and antibiotic treatment with recurrence

data.description: A rare congenital branchial apparatus anomaly that can form a sinus or fistula in the lower anterior neck and become repeatedly infected, sometimes communicating with the pyriform sinus.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion in the lower neck near the thyroid cartilage
symptoms_not_in_common: Third branchial anomalies are less commonly left-sided and less commonly associated with recurrent pyriform sinus-related infection than fourth branchial anomalies

data.description: A congenital epithelial cyst of the lateral neck that may enlarge or become infected, producing a painful neck mass and fever.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent swelling can occur if a congenital cyst remains untreated
symptoms_not_in_common: The swelling is at the level of the thyroid cartilage rather than the typical upper anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle
Repeated abscesses in the same left lower-neck location are more suggestive of a pyriform sinus fistula
Prior drainage without definitive excision is less characteristic for a typical second branchial cleft cyst

data.diagnosis: Acute suppurative cervical lymphadenitis or deep neck abscess
data.description: Bacterial infection of cervical lymph nodes or deep neck spaces causing a painful swollen neck mass, fever, and possible abscess formation.
symptoms_in_common: Clinical appearance of a neck abscess
Prior episodes treated with antibiotics and drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple recurrent episodes over several years in the same location suggest an underlying congenital fistula rather than isolated bacterial lymphadenitis
Left-sided lower-neck localization near the thyroid cartilage is particularly suggestive of a fourth branchial pouch anomaly

data.description: 35-year-old female with intermittent rhinitis presented with a 5-day history of urticaria, fever up to 39.5°C, severe headache, myalgia, and arthralgia. She developed pruritic, painful wheals and erythematous macules >1 cm on the limbs with burning sensation; lesions persisted >24 hours and left residual pigmentation. She also had nonpitting angioedema of the hands, fingers, ankles, and feet. Symptoms were severe enough to impair daily activities. She had taken over-the-counter diet pills starting 18 days before symptom onset and stopped them after a prior visit 6 days earlier for dehydration and violaceous hives on the palms. Exam showed large confluent wheals and macules on the limbs. Labs showed lymphopenia and elevated C-reactive protein; complement levels, liver and kidney function, electrolytes, glucose, thyroid studies, and ANA were normal/negative. Skin biopsy showed mild vacuolar interface change, papillary dermal edema, superficial and perivascular lymphocytic and eosinophilic infiltrate, focal fibrin in vessel walls, and erythrocyte extravasation.

A delayed hypersensitivity reaction to a medication, commonly occurring 1–3 weeks after exposure, characterized by urticarial rash, fever, joint symptoms, and edema. Unlike true serum sickness, complement levels are usually normal and significant immune-complex organ injury is absent.
symptoms_in_common: Onset approximately 18 days after starting over-the-counter diet pills
Nonpitting angioedema of hands, fingers, ankles, and feet
Lymphocytic and eosinophilic perivascular inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheals persisting for approximately 24 hours with residual pigmentation
Focal fibrin in vessel walls and erythrocyte extravasation on biopsy, which can suggest associated urticarial vasculitis

data.description: A small-vessel cutaneous vasculitis that presents with urticarial-appearing lesions that are often painful or burning, persist longer than ordinary hives, and may leave bruising or hyperpigmentation. Complement levels may be normal or low.
symptoms_in_common: Painful and burning wheals rather than itch alone
Fever, myalgia, arthralgia, and severe headache
Biopsy showing focal fibrin in vessel walls
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent pruritus, which is more typical of ordinary urticaria than vasculitis
Only mild vasculitic histologic changes without clear leukocytoclastic vasculitis
Normal complement does not exclude this diagnosis but makes hypocomplementemic disease less likely

data.description: An allergic or nonallergic medication-related mast-cell reaction causing transient pruritic wheals and swelling of deeper tissues, often after exposure to a new drug or supplement.
symptoms_in_common: New exposure to over-the-counter diet pills before onset
Angioedema of the hands, feet, fingers, and ankles
History of intermittent rhinitis suggesting an atopic tendency
Eosinophils in the skin inflammatory infiltrate
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever up to 39.5°C
Severe headache, myalgia, and arthralgia
Individual lesions persisting about 24 hours and leaving pigmentation
Focal fibrin in vessel walls and erythrocyte extravasation on biopsy
Elevated inflammatory markers and lymphopenia

data.diagnosis: DRESS syndrome (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms)
data.description: A severe delayed drug hypersensitivity reaction that usually develops 2–8 weeks after medication exposure and may cause fever, rash, facial edema, eosinophilia, lymphadenopathy, and internal-organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Delayed onset after starting a new medication or supplement
Systemic symptoms including headache, myalgia, and arthralgia
Eosinophilic inflammatory cells in the skin biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported peripheral eosinophilia
Lymphopenia rather than the more typical leukocytosis or atypical lymphocytosis
Normal liver and kidney function
No lymphadenopathy reported
Urticarial wheals are less typical than a persistent morbilliform eruption
Very short 5-day clinical course

data.description: A systemic autoinflammatory disorder characterized by recurrent high spiking fevers, inflammatory arthritis or arthralgia, and a transient salmon-pink rash, often with markedly elevated inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: Severe systemic illness impairing daily activities
symptoms_not_in_common: Pruritic, painful urticarial wheals with angioedema
Rash persisting for approximately 24 hours and leaving pigmentation
Temporal relationship to new diet pills
Lymphopenia rather than typical neutrophilic leukocytosis
No persistent inflammatory arthritis reported
Skin biopsy with eosinophils and vascular fibrin, which is not typical of Still disease

data.description:
16-year-old girl with 4 weeks of intermittent sharp abdominal pain, worsening over 2 weeks from every few days to twice daily, later lasting up to 15 minutes. Pain was worst in the epigastrium and upper quadrants, sometimes woke her from sleep, and was associated with nausea and recurrent vomiting; symptoms worsened with ibuprofen and improved after vomiting. She also had decreased appetite, fatigue, dizziness, weakness, and worsening constipation with last bowel movement 3 days before admission. She was unable to attend school.  

At outside evaluation, she was afebrile with tachycardia, dry mucous membranes, diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding in the epigastrium and upper quadrants, leukocytosis, and mild anemia; urinalysis and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound were normal. Over the following week, abdominal pain and nausea persisted, with increasing vomiting on admission day. Past history included iron-deficiency anemia and anxiety disorder; medications were iron, oral contraception, and famotidine.

A large gastric trichobezoar (mass of swallowed hair) that extends from the stomach into the small intestine, potentially causing gastric outlet or intestinal obstruction. The imaging and endoscopic images are characteristic of a hair-containing bezoar with intestinal extension.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent epigastric and upper abdominal pain
Palpable or imaging-visible upper abdominal gastric mass
Symptoms severe enough to impair school attendance
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of hair pulling or hair swallowing
Pain worsening with ibuprofen is not specific for Rapunzel syndrome
Dizziness is nonspecific
Leukocytosis is not typical unless there is inflammation or an obstruction-related complication

data.description: A compact mass of ingested hair retained in the stomach. It may produce chronic abdominal pain, vomiting, poor intake, anemia, and gastric outlet obstruction; it is the gastric component of Rapunzel syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Weight or functional impact suggested by inability to attend school
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported trichophagia or other hair-ingestion behavior
Tachycardia and dry mucous membranes reflect dehydration rather than being primary features
Leukocytosis is not a usual uncomplicated finding
Sharp brief episodes of pain are less characteristic than persistent fullness or discomfort

data.diagnosis: Gastric outlet obstruction due to bezoar
data.description: Mechanical obstruction at the stomach outlet caused by a large bezoar, leading to retained gastric contents, postprandial abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dehydration, and poor oral intake.
symptoms_in_common: Dizziness and weakness from poor intake or dehydration
Constipation due to reduced intake and downstream obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Iron-deficiency anemia is not a typical direct feature of acute gastric outlet obstruction
A four-week intermittent course is more gradual than many acute obstruction presentations
Leukocytosis is not typical without ischemia, inflammation, or another complication
Ibuprofen-associated worsening is not specific for mechanical obstruction

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease or NSAID-associated gastritis
data.description: Inflammation or ulceration of the stomach or duodenal lining, which can be worsened by ibuprofen and can cause epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and anemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked constipation is not typical
Relief specifically after vomiting is more suggestive of obstruction
The large hair-containing gastric mass seen on endoscopy and CT is not explained by peptic ulcer disease
Progressive obstructive symptoms and bowel extension are not typical
Tachycardia and dry mucous membranes are more consistent with vomiting-related dehydration

data.description: A 45-year-old white man was found dead at home and underwent autopsy as the cause of death was not apparent. He had recently been under review by the respiratory team for poor respiratory function and patchy fibronodular lung changes. His medical history included osteomyelitis of the elbow, congenital kyphoscoliosis, and testicular seminoma, which had been treated with orchidectomy and chemotherapy. At postmortem examination, the abdominal cavity contained copious pus covering the serosal aspect of the small bowel. There was an obvious perforation at the level of the mid-ileum, as well as three ulcers on the mucosal aspect of the ileum, one of which had perforated. Widespread pale nodules measuring up to 5 mm each were noted throughout the parenchyma of both lungs and a small pale lesion was present in the left kidney. No abnormalities were seen in the cardiovascular, endocrine, or central nervous systems.

Systemic infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis involving multiple organs. It can produce pulmonary nodules, granulomatous lesions in the kidney, and ulcerative intestinal disease that may perforate and cause fatal peritonitis.
symptoms_in_common: Patchy fibronodular lung changes and poor respiratory function
Widespread small pale nodules throughout both lungs, compatible with miliary/disseminated tuberculosis
Ileal ulcers with one ulcer perforating
Purulent peritonitis secondary to bowel perforation
Small pale renal lesion, compatible with extrapulmonary dissemination
History of osteomyelitis, which can occur with skeletal tuberculosis
Histology showing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented fever, night sweats, weight loss, or chronic cough
No described lymph-node enlargement
The prior seminoma is not a typical manifestation of tuberculosis

data.description: A disseminated infection caused by nontuberculous mycobacteria, most often M. avium or M. intracellulare, typically occurring in patients with significant immune impairment. It may involve the lungs, gastrointestinal tract, bone marrow, liver, spleen, and lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: History of chemotherapy for seminoma, which may have contributed to immune impairment
Diffuse pulmonary nodules and impaired respiratory function
Possible renal involvement represented by a pale kidney lesion
Prior osteomyelitis, which may occur in disseminated nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
Numerous acid-fast bacilli within granulomatous or histiocytic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No known HIV infection or other severe chronic immunodeficiency is reported
No documented constitutional symptoms such as persistent fever, severe weight loss, or drenching night sweats
Fibronodular pulmonary disease is more classically associated with tuberculosis or some other nontuberculous mycobacteria than disseminated MAC

data.description: A nontuberculous mycobacterial infection that commonly causes chronic pulmonary disease resembling tuberculosis; disseminated disease can occur in immunocompromised individuals and may involve extrapulmonary organs.
symptoms_in_common: Poor respiratory function with fibronodular pulmonary abnormalities
Past chemotherapy, which may predispose to opportunistic infection
Possible extrapulmonary disease involving bowel, kidney, and bone
symptoms_not_in_common: Small-bowel ulceration and perforation are uncommon manifestations
Disseminated disease is less common than isolated pulmonary disease
No known chronic lung disease, HIV infection, or other profound immunosuppression is described

data.diagnosis: Intestinal tuberculosis causing ileal perforation and generalized peritonitis
data.description: Tuberculosis involving the gastrointestinal tract, usually affecting the ileocecal region but potentially involving the ileum. Ulceration can progress through the bowel wall, producing perforation and severe purulent peritonitis.
symptoms_in_common: Mid-ileal perforation arising from an ulcer
Copious intraperitoneal pus consistent with peritonitis
Pulmonary fibronodular disease supporting a tuberculous source
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is in the mid-ileum rather than the more typical ileocecal region
No reported preceding abdominal pain, diarrhea, fever, or weight loss
Diffuse lung nodules and renal lesion indicate disease beyond isolated intestinal tuberculosis

data.description: 33-year-old man admitted with chest pain that began 2 hours earlier as epigastric pain and progressed to central chest pain, associated with one episode of vomiting, dizziness, dyspnea, sweating, and distal paresthesias; pain had resolved on admission. Later the same day, he developed nausea, diaphoresis, pallor, blurred vision, muffled hearing, and tingling in both hands, with systolic blood pressure dropping to 89 mm Hg and cardiac monitoring showing a 3–4 second pause without P wave activity. Past history included syncope during phlebotomy. He had recent flu-like symptoms and a daughter with gastroenteritis. Physical examinations were normal, including after the hypotensive episode.

data.diagnosis: Cardioinhibitory vasovagal syncope (vasovagal reflex with sinus pause)
data.description: A neurally mediated reflex causing increased vagal tone, leading to hypotension, bradycardia, or transient sinus arrest. It is commonly triggered by pain, nausea, emotional stress, medical procedures, or gastrointestinal illness.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotension with systolic blood pressure of 89 mm Hg
3-4 second pause without P waves consistent with transient sinus arrest
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial central chest pain
Epigastric pain preceding chest pain
Dyspnea

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome (including unstable angina or myocardial infarction)
data.description: Acute coronary syndrome results from reduced blood flow to the heart, typically due to coronary artery plaque rupture or spasm, and can cause chest pain with autonomic symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age of 33 years
Pain had resolved by admission
History of phlebotomy-associated syncope
Prodromal blurred vision and muffled hearing
Bilateral hand tingling
Sinus pause without P waves, which is more suggestive of vagal cardioinhibition than typical ischemic arrhythmia
Normal examinations after the event

data.description: Brugada syndrome is an inherited cardiac sodium-channel disorder associated with characteristic right-precordial ECG abnormalities and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias, syncope, and sudden cardiac death. Fever or viral illness can unmask ECG changes.
symptoms_in_common: Recent flu-like illness, which can precipitate or unmask Brugada ECG findings
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent nausea, pallor, diaphoresis, blurred vision, and muffled hearing suggest a vasovagal prodrome
Hypotension associated with a sinus pause rather than documented ventricular tachyarrhythmia
History of syncope specifically during phlebotomy
Epigastric pain and vomiting
Bilateral distal paresthesias

data.description: Myopericarditis is inflammation of the myocardium and/or pericardium, often occurring after a viral illness. It can cause chest pain, ECG changes, arrhythmias, and occasionally impaired cardiac function.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain began as epigastric pain and resolved rapidly
Marked vasovagal-type prodrome with nausea, pallor, muffled hearing, and visual blurring
Syncope history during phlebotomy
Transient sinus arrest associated with hypotension as the main documented rhythm event
Normal physical examinations after the episode
No reported persistent chest pain, fever, or signs of heart failure

data.diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis or viral illness triggering a vagal episode
data.description: A viral gastrointestinal illness can cause nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, and dehydration; pain, vomiting, and nausea may trigger a strong vagal reflex resulting in hypotension and bradycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Vagal-mediated sinus pause may be triggered by nausea or vomiting
symptoms_not_in_common: Central chest pain
Dyspnea
Blurred vision and muffled hearing are more characteristic of presyncope than primary gastroenteritis
No reported diarrhea
No reported fever
Prior syncope during phlebotomy suggests an underlying vasovagal susceptibility rather than gastroenteritis alone

data.description: A 21-year-old man presented to his general practitioner with intermittent left-sided pain in the anterior chest wall associated with neck discomfort. The pain was described as 'stabbing' in nature and had arisen suddenly while watching television, with no history of trauma before onset. The pain was not exacerbated by inspiration or effort. His medical history and physical examination were initially unremarkable. Several days later, he attended the emergency department with worsening chest pain and dyspnea. On examination, chest expansion was equal and breath sounds were normal, although there was crepitus on auscultation of the precordium. Palpation of the neck and supraclavicular fossae detected subcutaneous emphysema. His respiratory rate was 25 breaths per minute and oxygen saturations were 100%. His full blood count and inflammatory markers were within normal limits.

Free air within the mediastinum occurring without trauma or an obvious precipitating event, often due to rupture of small alveoli with air tracking along bronchovascular structures. It can cause subcutaneous emphysema and Hamman sign (precordial crepitus).
symptoms_in_common: Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and supraclavicular fossae

data.description: A full-thickness tear of the esophagus that can permit air and gastrointestinal contents to enter the mediastinum, causing pneumomediastinum, severe chest pain, systemic inflammation, and potentially mediastinitis.
symptoms_in_common: Precordial crepitus due to mediastinal air
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of vomiting or retching before symptom onset
No fever or elevated inflammatory markers
Initially well appearance and unremarkable examination
Pain began while watching television without an obvious trigger

data.description: Air in the pleural space causing partial or complete lung collapse, commonly presenting in young men with sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. It may occasionally coexist with pneumomediastinum and subcutaneous emphysema.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain was not worsened by inspiration
Equal chest expansion
Normal breath sounds
Precordial crepitus and neck subcutaneous emphysema are more characteristic of pneumomediastinum
Oxygen saturation was 100%

data.description: Inflammation of the pericardium that typically causes sharp chest pain, often worse with inspiration or lying flat and relieved by sitting forward. A pericardial friction rub may be heard.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp or stabbing anterior chest pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain was not exacerbated by inspiration
Precordial crepitus rather than a pericardial friction rub
Subcutaneous emphysema in the neck and supraclavicular fossae
Radiologic evidence of mediastinal air
No inflammatory marker elevation

data.description: 34-year-old man in Scotland presented with an expanding itchy rash on the right flank that persisted for three months. He did not recall any insect bite or foreign travel history, but regularly visits the Scottish highlands. Initial Borrelia serology performed at 4 weeks after rash onset was negative.

data.diagnosis: Erythema migrans due to Lyme disease
data.description: The characteristic expanding skin lesion of early Lyme borreliosis, caused by Borrelia infection transmitted by Ixodes ticks. A recalled tick bite is often absent, and early serology may be negative.
symptoms_in_common: Expanding annular red rash with central clearing
Regular exposure to the Scottish Highlands, where tick exposure is possible
No recalled insect bite does not exclude tick exposure
Negative Borrelia serology early after rash onset can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistence for three months is longer than the usual untreated duration of a single erythema migrans lesion

data.description: A superficial dermatophyte fungal infection that commonly produces an itchy, enlarging ring-shaped rash with a more active red border and relative central clearing.
symptoms_in_common: Persistence for several months can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible scale or raised scaly edge is described
The lesion appears unusually large and relatively smooth for typical tinea corporis
Highland tick exposure is not relevant to fungal infection

data.description: A reactive inflammatory skin eruption characterized by slowly enlarging annular red plaques, often with central clearing; it may be itchy and can persist for weeks to months.
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion lacks a clearly described trailing scale, which is often present
The apparent exposure risk from visits to the Scottish Highlands may suggest an alternative tick-associated cause

data.description: Inflammation of the skin after exposure to an allergen or irritant, often causing an itchy red patch or plaque. It may persist if exposure continues.
symptoms_in_common: Persistence over several months is possible with ongoing exposure
Location on the flank could correspond to contact from clothing, adhesives, or topical products
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive annular expansion with central clearing is not typical
No exposure to a new product, adhesive, clothing material, or irritant is reported

data.description: A benign inflammatory dermatosis that causes annular plaques, usually with a smooth raised border and central clearing. Localized lesions commonly occur on hands and feet but can occur elsewhere.
symptoms_not_in_common: Granuloma annulare is usually not itchy
It generally does not rapidly expand as an erythematous patch
The flank is less typical than the hands, feet, wrists, or ankles
The lesion appears more erythematous and diffuse than typical granuloma annulare

data.description: A 39-year-old man with a history of current smoking and no other medical history presented with left-sided squeezing chest pain that was worse in the early morning after drinking alcohol and lasted 30 minutes. Initial vital signs showed blood pressure of 132/89 mmHg and pulse rate of 98 beats/minute. Initial laboratory findings revealed creatine kinase 118 U/L (normal 58-348), CK-MB 1.7 ug/L (normal 0-5.0), elevated highly sensitive troponin-T 0.027 ng/mL (normal 0-0.014), and microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL. Echocardiography showed normal-sized cardiac chambers with good left ventricular systolic function (ejection fraction of 61%) and no regional wall motion abnormality.
Transient coronary artery spasm causing episodic myocardial ischemia, often occurring at rest in the early morning and triggered by smoking or alcohol.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided squeezing chest pain at rest
Normal left ventricular systolic function and no regional wall-motion abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.description: Acute myocardial infarction with myocardial injury indicated by elevated troponin but without persistent ST-segment elevation; it may result from plaque disruption, coronary spasm, or another ischemic mechanism.
symptoms_in_common: Squeezing left-sided chest pain lasting approximately 30 minutes
ECG repolarization abnormalities consistent with ischemia
Smoking as a cardiovascular risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal CK and CK-MB
No regional wall-motion abnormality on echocardiography
Young age for typical atherosclerotic NSTEMI
Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.description: Acute coronary syndrome characterized by new, worsening, or rest angina due to transient myocardial ischemia, traditionally without a significant rise in cardiac biomarkers.
symptoms_in_common: New squeezing chest pain at rest
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated high-sensitivity troponin-T, which favors NSTEMI rather than unstable angina
Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.diagnosis: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA)
data.description: Myocardial infarction with elevated cardiac troponin and ischemic symptoms despite no major obstructive epicardial coronary lesion; possible mechanisms include coronary spasm, plaque erosion, embolism, or spontaneous coronary artery dissection.
symptoms_in_common: Normal left ventricular function without regional wall-motion abnormality
Possible absence of a clearly obstructive coronary lesion on angiographic images
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic hypochromic anemia

data.diagnosis: Type 2 myocardial infarction due to oxygen supply-demand mismatch from anemia
data.description: Myocardial injury caused by inadequate oxygen supply relative to myocardial demand rather than acute coronary thrombosis; significant anemia can contribute to ischemia, especially in the presence of coronary spasm or underlying coronary disease.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoglobin of 9.8 g/dL with microcytic hypochromic anemia
Mild tachycardia with pulse rate of 98 beats per minute
symptoms_not_in_common: Early-morning pain after alcohol consumption is more characteristic of vasospastic angina
Smoking-related coronary vasospasm is a more specific explanation
No documented severe hypotension, hypoxemia, arrhythmia, or marked tachycardia

data.description: 12-year-old Saudi boy presented with severe spontaneous dental pain for 3 days. He was the fourth of five siblings. Parents were not related. His mother had 5 previous spontaneous abortions in first trimester. Mother took acetazolamide 1000mg/day for idiopathic intracranial hypertension before and throughout pregnancy. Patient was born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery, weighing 2,270g (below 5th percentile). He presented without major dysmorphic features, was intelligent with good behavior, and had normal skin, hair and nails. Intraoral exam showed mixed dentition with retained primary lower central incisors, hypocalcified permanent upper incisors, and multiple carious teeth. Tongue, floor of mouth, upper lip, hard and soft palate were normal.
A TP63-related disorder characterized by split-hand/split-foot malformations (ectrodactyly), variable tooth-development defects, ectodermal abnormalities, and sometimes cleft lip or palate.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral split-hand/split-foot or ectrodactyly-like limb abnormalities
Multiple missing or developmentally abnormal teeth on panoramic radiograph
Retained primary lower central incisors, compatible with delayed eruption or absent successors
Multiple carious teeth, which can occur with enamel defects and tooth malformations
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal skin, hair, and nails
No cleft lip or cleft palate
No major dysmorphic facial features
Normal intelligence and behavior
Low birth weight is not a defining feature
Severe spontaneous dental pain is more likely due to caries than the syndrome itself

data.diagnosis: Nonsyndromic split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) with tooth agenesis
data.description: A congenital limb-malformation disorder featuring central absence or hypoplasia of digits, producing split hands and/or feet; some genetic forms are associated with hypodontia or oligodontia without prominent ectodermal or craniofacial findings.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital bilateral hand abnormalities consistent with split-hand malformation
Congenital bilateral foot abnormalities consistent with split-foot malformation
Multiple absent teeth or tooth buds on panoramic radiography
Retained primary incisors, potentially due to absent permanent successor teeth
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypocalcified enamel is not a universal feature of isolated SHFM
Multiple carious teeth are not intrinsic to the limb-malformation disorder
Low birth weight is not typical
Severe dental pain is not a primary feature and is likely caused by dental caries
Maternal acetazolamide exposure is not a typical genetic cause of SHFM

data.diagnosis: Acetazolamide-associated fetal limb and dental developmental anomaly (teratogenic embryopathy)
data.description: Prenatal exposure to acetazolamide has been suspected, though not conclusively proven in humans, to contribute to congenital malformations including limb defects and growth restriction; exposure during organogenesis could potentially contribute to the observed abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal acetazolamide use before and throughout pregnancy
Low birth weight below the 5th percentile
Congenital limb abnormalities affecting both hands and feet
Dental developmental abnormalities, including hypocalcified incisors and apparent missing teeth
symptoms_not_in_common: A characteristic split-hand/split-foot pattern more strongly suggests an underlying genetic ectrodactyly disorder
Normal skin, hair, and nails do not specifically support a teratogenic syndrome
Severe dental pain is attributable to caries rather than fetal drug exposure itself
Retained primary teeth and extensive tooth agenesis are not established hallmark effects of acetazolamide exposure
The mother's recurrent first-trimester spontaneous abortions are not a typical manifestation in the affected child

data.description: 62-year-old man with palpitations occurring four times in the past week, associated with episodes of rapid heartbeat and shortness of breath; two episodes followed alcohol intake. He denied chest pain or syncope. History of hypertension treated with amlodipine. On examination, blood pressure was 160/90 mm Hg, heart rate 82 bpm, with normal heart and respiratory exam. Holter monitoring showed frequent supraventricular ectopy and two episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
An intermittent supraventricular arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial electrical activity and an irregular, often rapid ventricular rhythm that terminates spontaneously.
symptoms_in_common: Hypertension, a risk factor for atrial fibrillation
Holter monitoring documented two episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
Frequent supraventricular ectopy, which can trigger atrial fibrillation
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain
No syncope
Normal resting heart rate between episodes

data.description: Early atrial beats arising outside the sinus node that may cause skipped beats, fluttering, palpitations, and may precipitate atrial tachyarrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Frequent supraventricular ectopic beats on Holter monitoring
Supraventricular couplets and runs on Holter monitoring
Alcohol exposure, which can increase atrial ectopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Shortness of breath is less typical with isolated premature atrial contractions
Documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation indicates an additional sustained arrhythmia
No report of skipped beats or single forceful beats

data.description: An episodic rapid heart rhythm originating above the ventricles, usually causing sudden palpitations and a regular rapid heartbeat; atrial tachycardia may occur in association with frequent atrial ectopy.
symptoms_in_common: Supraventricular ectopic runs on Holter monitoring
symptoms_not_in_common: Holter specifically documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation rather than a sustained regular supraventricular tachycardia
Atrial fibrillation is typically irregular rather than the regular rhythm expected in many supraventricular tachycardias
No description of abrupt onset and abrupt termination of a sustained regular tachycardia
No chest discomfort, lightheadedness, or syncope

data.description: Atrial arrhythmias, most commonly atrial fibrillation, precipitated by acute alcohol intake, often in people without severe structural heart disease but more likely in those with cardiovascular risk factors.
symptoms_in_common: Two symptomatic episodes followed alcohol intake
symptoms_not_in_common: The amount and pattern of alcohol consumption are not provided
Not all episodes were reported to follow alcohol intake
Hypertension may independently contribute to atrial fibrillation
No nausea, tremor, or other alcohol-related symptoms were reported

data.description: A 58-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He also experienced urinary symptoms including frequency, urgency, and dysuria. Initial colonoscopy revealed prominent congestion and edema, loss of vascular pattern, and multiple moth-eaten ulcers with purulent exudates involving the entire colon. A repeat colonoscopy showed scattered irregular ulcers with with granular background mucosa and 'fuzzy' vasculature. The ileum appeared normal.

A chronic inflammatory bowel disease causing continuous mucosal inflammation of the colon, typically beginning in the rectum and extending proximally; severe disease can produce diffuse ulceration and purulent exudate.
symptoms_in_common: Normal terminal ileum can occur in ulcerative colitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria
Scattered irregular rather than clearly continuous ulcers on repeat colonoscopy

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can involve any part of the gastrointestinal tract and often causes patchy, deep, irregular ulcers with intervening granular or relatively normal mucosa.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal ileum, although isolated colonic Crohn disease is possible
Diffuse involvement of the entire colon is less characteristic than patchy disease
Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria without evidence of a fistula or urinary infection

data.diagnosis: Intestinal tuberculosis with possible genitourinary tuberculosis
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can involve the gastrointestinal tract, producing chronic abdominal symptoms, weight loss, ulceration, and granulomatous colitis. Genitourinary involvement may cause dysuria, frequency, and urgency.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse whole-colon involvement is less typical than ileocecal disease
Normal ileum is less typical for intestinal tuberculosis
Purulent exudates are not specific for tuberculosis

data.description: Colonic infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica that may cause abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, and discrete flask-shaped or irregular ulcers covered by exudate.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcers with purulent or necrotic-appearing exudate
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria
Diffuse involvement of the entire colon is less typical than cecal or right-sided colonic involvement

data.description: Lymphoma involving the colon, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma or other lymphoproliferative disorders, may cause weight loss, abdominal pain, diarrhea, mucosal infiltration, ulceration, and abnormal vascular patterns.
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency
Urinary urgency
Dysuria
Diffuse inflammatory congestion with purulent exudate may more strongly suggest severe colitis or infection than lymphoma

data.description: A previously healthy 9-year-old boy presented to the emergency department with a 6-hour history of left chest pain and increasing respiratory distress. His vital signs showed a respiratory rate of 40/min and heart rate of 105/min. Physical examination revealed unremarkable cardiac auscultation, while auscultation of lung fields showed diminished breath sounds over the left side.
Accumulation of both air and fluid in the pleural space, producing an air-fluid level and partial collapse of the adjacent lung.
symptoms_in_common: Diminished breath sounds over the left hemithorax
Chest radiograph showing a left pleural air-fluid level
symptoms_not_in_common: No atypical symptoms reported

data.description: Air in the pleural cavity causes lung collapse and pleuritic pain; associated pleural fluid creates a hydropneumothorax appearance on radiography.

symptoms_not_in_common: Pleural fluid is not typical of an uncomplicated primary spontaneous pneumothorax
Previously healthy 9-year-old child is less typical than an adolescent or young adult

data.description: Infected pleural fluid together with pleural air, usually resulting from pneumonia, empyema, trauma, or communication between an airway and pleural space.
symptoms_in_common: Diminished breath sounds on the affected side
Pleural air-fluid level on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported

Very acute 6-hour onset is less typical for empyema

data.description: A pulmonary echinococcal cyst can rupture into a bronchus or pleural cavity, causing sudden chest pain, dyspnea, pneumothorax, hydropneumothorax, or an intrapulmonary air-fluid level.

data.diagnosis: Congenital pulmonary airway malformation with infection or rupture
data.description: A congenital cystic lung lesion may remain silent until childhood and can present with infection, air trapping, pneumothorax, or an air-fluid level if a cyst communicates with the airway.

symptoms_not_in_common: No history of recurrent respiratory infections

data.description: 63-year-old man with well-controlled hypertension and diabetes was referred from primary clinic due to hepatic mass found on ultrasonography. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed normal hematological indexes, liver function tests, and renal functions. Patient was negative for viral markers with normal α-fetoprotein levels. Bone marrow biopsy showed 30% marrow cellularity but was otherwise normal. Serum calcium, β-2 microglobulin, and serum/urine protein immunoelectrophoresis were normal. Skeletal radiography revealed no abnormalities.

data.diagnosis: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
data.description: A localized tumor of monoclonal plasma cells arising outside the bone marrow; hepatic involvement is rare. It is diagnosed when there is a solitary lesion without significant marrow plasmacytosis, myeloma-defining bone lesions, or a monoclonal protein.
symptoms_in_common: Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis
Normal bone marrow aside from age-compatible cellularity
No skeletal radiographic abnormalities or lytic lesions

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with extramedullary hepatic involvement

Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis

Normal calcium

Normal hematologic indexes without anemia

No bone pain or systemic symptoms

symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss, night sweats, or other B symptoms

Histologic appearance and plasma-cell immunophenotype would be less typical than for plasmacytoma

data.description: Young female European traveler presented to a clinic in central Australia with vaginal discharge. She reported new sexual contact with another European traveler 1 week earlier in Sydney.
A sexually transmitted bacterial infection that can infect the cervix and cause increased or abnormal vaginal discharge, often developing within days to a week after exposure.
A common sexually transmitted bacterial infection of the cervix that is frequently asymptomatic but can cause vaginal discharge and cervical inflammation.

data.description: A sexually transmitted infection caused by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis, which can cause vaginal discharge, irritation, odor, and discomfort with urination or intercourse.

data.description: A 44-year-old man with a 17-year history of tobacco and cannabis use presented with acute dyspnoea and left-sided pleuritic chest pain. He had no other medical conditions and took no regular medications. On examination, he was thin and hypoxic, with a silent, hyper-resonant left hemithorax. Laboratory results showed normal α-1 antitrypsin concentration (1.4 g/L), normal immunoglobulins, and specific IgE for Aspergillus. Spirometry revealed severe obstruction with FVC of 2.95 L (57% predicted), FEV1 of 1.37 L (34% predicted), and FEV1/FVC ratio of 59% predicted.

A severe form of bullous emphysema characterized by large air-filled bullae, often upper-lobe predominant, that compress adjacent functional lung tissue. It is strongly associated with cigarette smoking and cannabis use in younger patients.
symptoms_in_common: History of tobacco and cannabis use
Severe obstructive spirometry with reduced FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio

data.diagnosis: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax due to bullous emphysema
data.description: Collapse of the lung from air entering the pleural space, occurring in a patient with underlying lung disease such as emphysema or giant bullae. Rupture of a bulla can precipitate sudden pleuritic pain and breathlessness.

data.diagnosis: Smoking-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with emphysema
data.description: A chronic progressive airflow-limiting disorder caused most commonly by tobacco exposure. Emphysema involves destruction of alveolar walls and may lead to hyperinflation, bullae, and secondary pneumothorax.
