Age 44 is relatively young for severe smoking-related COPD
No chronic cough or sputum production was reported

data.diagnosis: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax associated with apical blebs or bullae
data.description: A spontaneous pneumothorax usually occurring in thin individuals, often from rupture of subpleural blebs or bullae. Smoking substantially increases risk, and large bullae may complicate interpretation of chest imaging.

Age is older than the usual demographic for primary spontaneous pneumothorax

data.description: 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented with 3 months of progressive fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and vague upper abdominal pain. He had a 40-pack-year smoking history (quit 2 years earlier). On presentation, he had renal insufficiency (creatinine 3.2), severe anemia (hemoglobin 7), thrombocytopenia (platelets 77,000/μL), hypercalcemia (12.7), elevated total protein (>10), biochemical evidence of tumor lysis syndrome (LDH 1,157; uric acid 20.8), and coagulopathy consistent with disseminated intravascular clotting, with prolonged PT and aPTT, low fibrinogen, and elevated D-dimer and fibrin split products.

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with aggressive extramedullary plasmacytoma
data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder characterized by monoclonal protein production, marrow infiltration, renal injury, anemia, hypercalcemia, and sometimes bulky extramedullary soft-tissue masses.

Bulky abdominal/retroperitoneal mass compatible with extramedullary plasmacytoma
Elevated LDH and uric acid consistent with high tumor burden and tumor lysis

Vague upper abdominal pain is not a classic presenting symptom

data.description: An aggressive plasma-cell neoplasm in which malignant plasma cells circulate in peripheral blood, often causing severe marrow failure, renal dysfunction, hypercalcemia, high LDH, and extramedullary disease.

Upper abdominal pain is nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.diagnosis: High-grade non-Hodgkin lymphoma, such as diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive lymphoid malignancy that can present with bulky abdominal or retroperitoneal masses, constitutional symptoms, marrow involvement, tumor lysis syndrome, and occasionally hypercalcemia.
symptoms_in_common: Upper abdominal pain with an abdominal mass
Hyperuricemia and biochemical tumor lysis syndrome
Anemia and thrombocytopenia from marrow involvement
Disseminated intravascular coagulation can occur in advanced aggressive lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated total protein is less typical than in plasma-cell disorders
The combined pattern of hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, and high total protein is more characteristic of myeloma
No lymphadenopathy or B-cell immunophenotyping is provided

data.diagnosis: Burkitt lymphoma or other highly proliferative B-cell lymphoma
data.description: A rapidly growing high-grade B-cell lymphoma associated with very high tumor burden, markedly elevated LDH, spontaneous tumor lysis syndrome, abdominal masses, and possible marrow involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and apparent bulky abdominal disease
Anemia and thrombocytopenia if bone marrow is involved
Possible disseminated intravascular coagulation in advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 62 is less typical for classic Burkitt lymphoma
Hypercalcemia is not a usual presentation
Elevated total protein is not typical
The clinical combination strongly suggestive of plasma-cell dyscrasia is less characteristic

data.description: A 26-year-old woman presented with a one-year history of rash on her lower legs, abdomen, and arms, accompanied by a six-month history of paraesthesia in her right hand and left foot. She had no history of fatigue, weight loss, fever, or arthralgia. Neurological examination showed reduced sensation to light touch in the right ring and little fingers, the lateral palmar and dorsal hand, the left lateral calf, and the dorsum of the left foot. She experienced clumsiness in her right hand causing difficulty with writing, but no weakness was noted. Blood tests, including a full autoimmune screen, were normal. Electromyography demonstrated sensory damage in the right ulnar nerve and asymmetrical superficial sensory damage in the peroneal nerve, with greater involvement on the left side.

data.diagnosis: Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa (cutaneous PAN) with mononeuritis multiplex
data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of small- to medium-sized arteries primarily affecting the skin, sometimes associated with peripheral nerve involvement. It commonly produces livedo racemosa, nodules, purpura, ulcers, and asymmetric peripheral neuropathy without major internal-organ disease.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic mottled violaceous rash consistent with livedo racemosa on the legs, abdomen, and arms
Asymmetric sensory neuropathy involving the right ulnar and left peroneal nerve distributions
Paraesthesia in the right hand and left foot
Reduced sensation in multiple peripheral nerve territories
Hand clumsiness due to sensory nerve dysfunction
Electromyography showing asymmetric peripheral sensory nerve damage
Absence of constitutional symptoms and normal autoimmune blood tests, which can occur in skin-limited PAN
symptoms_not_in_common: No painful subcutaneous nodules, skin ulceration, or digital ischemia were reported
No motor weakness was found

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause livedo reticularis or racemosa, mononeuritis multiplex, hypertension, renal ischemia, abdominal pain, and systemic inflammatory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Asymmetric peripheral neuropathy consistent with mononeuritis multiplex
Ulnar and peroneal sensory nerve involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, fatigue, weight loss, or arthralgia
No renal symptoms or hypertension were reported
No abdominal pain or gastrointestinal ischemic symptoms were reported
No weakness or painful motor neuropathy was noted
Normal blood tests and autoimmune screen

data.diagnosis: ANCA-associated vasculitic neuropathy, such as microscopic polyangiitis
data.description: Small-vessel systemic vasculitis may cause palpable purpura or other skin lesions and an asymmetric axonal neuropathy, often presenting as mononeuritis multiplex. It commonly has renal, pulmonary, constitutional, or inflammatory manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple noncontiguous peripheral nerve territories affected
Skin rash that could reflect cutaneous vasculitis
Electromyographic evidence of asymmetric nerve damage
symptoms_not_in_common: The rash appears livedo-like rather than typical palpable purpura
No fever, fatigue, weight loss, or arthralgia
No renal, pulmonary, ear-nose-throat, or gastrointestinal symptoms were reported
Normal autoimmune testing
No weakness was found

data.description: 17-year-old male with high myopia and craniofacial/skeletal abnormalities. Full-term vaginal birth, birth weight 4.3 kg. Height tracked at the 80th percentile until age 15, then plateaued at the 55th percentile. History includes pectus excavatum since birth, dental crowding and class III dentofacial growth pattern at age 12, retroclined lower teeth on exam, and a grade 3/6 systolic heart murmur noted at age 13. Current exam shows scoliosis with loss of normal thoracic kyphosis; weight 66.3 kg, height 177.5 cm, head circumference 58.5 cm. Laboratory testing showed marked hyperhomocysteinemia (237.0 µmol/L) with elevated methionine (240 nmol/mL); vitamin B12, folate, methylmalonic acid, and hemoglobin/hematocrit were normal.

data.diagnosis: Classic homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency
data.description: An autosomal recessive disorder of methionine metabolism causing markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine. It commonly produces a marfanoid skeletal habitus, ectopia lentis, myopia, osteoporosis, and thromboembolic risk.
symptoms_in_common: Likely lens subluxation/ectopia lentis on eye examination
Scoliosis and loss of normal thoracic kyphosis
Dental crowding and class III malocclusion
Growth pattern with relatively tall stature before adolescent plateau
Vertebral bone changes/low bone mineral density suggested by imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No thromboembolic event has been reported
No developmental delay, intellectual disability, or psychiatric symptoms have been described

data.description: An autosomal dominant connective-tissue disorder, usually caused by FBN1 variants, characterized by skeletal overgrowth, pectus deformity, scoliosis, ocular abnormalities including myopia and ectopia lentis, and aortic-root disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hyperhomocysteinemia is not typical
Elevated methionine is not typical
No documented aortic-root dilatation, aortic aneurysm, or mitral valve prolapse
Vertebral osteopenia/compression changes are less characteristic than in homocystinuria

data.description: A hereditary connective-tissue disorder involving TGF-beta signaling, associated with arterial aneurysms and tortuosity, pectus deformity, scoliosis, craniofacial differences, and sometimes myopia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hyperhomocysteinemia is not typical
Elevated methionine is not typical
Ectopia lentis is not a typical defining feature
No arterial aneurysm, arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism, bifid uvula, or cleft palate has been reported

data.diagnosis: Cobalamin-remethylation defect (for example, cblC disease or severe methionine synthase deficiency)
data.description: An inherited disorder of intracellular cobalamin processing or homocysteine remethylation that can cause severe hyperhomocysteinemia, neurologic disease, eye disease, and hematologic abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Methionine is elevated, whereas remethylation disorders usually cause low or low-normal methionine
Methylmalonic acid is normal, arguing against cblC-type disease
Vitamin B12 is normal
No anemia, macrocytosis, neurologic dysfunction, developmental delay, or renal disease has been described
Pectus excavatum, scoliosis, and ectopia lentis are more characteristic of CBS deficiency

data.description: 29-year-old right-hand dominant male chef with a 4-day history of gradually worsening dull left-sided neck pain radiating to the head, associated with diplopia, right-sided numbness, dropping objects at work, and unsteadiness. He denied head injury, loss of consciousness, seizures, alcohol, or illicit drug use. Past history: hypothyroidism on thyroxine. On examination, he was alert and oriented with stable vital signs, right-sided weakness (MRC grade 4, mainly upper limb) with pronator drift, reduced right-sided pinprick/light touch/proprioception, resting and intention tremor with dysdiadochokinesia, broad-based ataxic gait, and an upgoing right plantar response. Pupils were equal and reactive; diplopia was present on extreme gaze without obvious ocular palsy, and no papilloedema was seen.

data.diagnosis: Pontine cavernous malformation with acute hemorrhage
data.description: A cavernous malformation is a cluster of fragile abnormal blood vessels that can bleed. Hemorrhage within a pontine cavernoma can cause focal brainstem and long-tract neurological deficits and may obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow, producing hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Gradually worsening neck and head pain
Right-sided numbness involving pinprick, light touch, and proprioception
Dropping objects due to upper-limb weakness and incoordination
Imaging appearance of a focal pontine hemorrhagic lesion with ventricular enlargement
symptoms_not_in_common: No obvious ocular motor palsy despite diplopia
No papilloedema despite ventriculomegaly

data.description: Pontine hemorrhage is bleeding into the pons, which can injure corticospinal, sensory, cerebellar, and ocular-motor pathways. In a young adult without hypertension, an underlying vascular lesion such as a cavernoma or arteriovenous malformation should be considered.
symptoms_in_common: Hyperdense pontine focus on CT consistent with acute blood
Ventricular dilatation compatible with obstructive hydrocephalus
symptoms_not_in_common: Four-day gradual progression rather than a sudden maximal-onset deficit
Young age and absence of known hypertension
Stable vital signs
Preserved consciousness and orientation

data.description: A brain arteriovenous malformation is an abnormal direct connection between arteries and veins. It can bleed into the pons and cause acute or subacute focal brainstem deficits, headache, and hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Ataxia and impaired rapid alternating movements
Upper motor neuron sign with an upgoing right plantar response
Ventricular enlargement from possible obstruction of cerebrospinal-fluid pathways
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported abrupt thunderclap headache
No seizure
No altered consciousness
No bruit or other reported vascular physical finding

data.diagnosis: Vertebral artery dissection with posterior-circulation ischemic stroke
data.description: Vertebral artery dissection is a tear in the arterial wall that can cause neck pain or headache and lead to ischemia in the brainstem or cerebellum. It is an important consideration in a young person with neck pain and posterior-circulation neurological deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral neck pain radiating to the head
symptoms_not_in_common: CT appearance suggests a focal pontine hemorrhage rather than a typical ischemic infarct
No history of neck trauma or manipulation
No clear sudden onset of symptoms
Ventricular enlargement is not typical of a small posterior-circulation ischemic stroke

data.diagnosis: Brainstem glioma or other hemorrhagic pontine tumor
data.description: A pontine tumor can produce progressive cranial-nerve, long-tract, and cerebellar signs. Some tumors may bleed, but a focal hyperdense lesion with acute neurological deterioration is more suggestive of a vascular hemorrhagic lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Gradually worsening symptoms over several days
Potential obstruction of cerebrospinal-fluid flow causing ventricular enlargement
symptoms_not_in_common: Very short four-day illness for most brainstem tumors
Hyperdense CT appearance more consistent with acute hemorrhage than uncomplicated tumor
No reported constitutional symptoms
No papilloedema despite ventricular enlargement

data.description: 18-year-old male with 4 days of fatigue, subjective fever, chills, headache, non-bilious nonbloody vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, low back pain, dysuria, and lower abdominal, groin, and scrotal pain. Past history includes exercise-induced asthma and childhood hospitalization for diarrhea. Born in Central America, moved to the US at age 15. On examination he appeared tired, febrile to 39.4°C, tachycardic, tachypneic, and had low back paraspinal muscle tenderness.

A systemic infection caused by Leishmania parasites, transmitted by sandflies; amastigotes may be seen within macrophages in bone marrow and other reticuloendothelial tissues. It is endemic in parts of Central America.
symptoms_in_common: Gastrointestinal symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea
Origin from Central America, an endemic region
Bone marrow findings with intracellular organisms in macrophages
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute 4-day presentation
Dysuria
Lower abdominal, groin, and scrotal pain
Prominent low back/paraspinal muscle tenderness
No reported hepatosplenomegaly or weight loss

data.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum. Small intracellular yeasts can resemble Leishmania in macrophages on bone marrow examination, and disease may cause fever, constitutional symptoms, and gastrointestinal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Possible intracellular organisms within macrophages on pathology
Residence in or origin from an area where Histoplasma may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute 4-day illness
Dysuria
Groin and scrotal pain
Localized lower abdominal pain
Low back paraspinal muscle tenderness
No reported respiratory symptoms, hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, or immunosuppression

data.description: A bacterial kidney infection, often ascending from the urinary tract, that can produce high fever, systemic inflammatory symptoms, vomiting, dysuria, and flank or back pain.
symptoms_in_common: Low back pain and paraspinal tenderness
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is less typical
Groin and scrotal pain are not typical unless there is associated epididymal or testicular involvement
Bone marrow intracellular organisms would not be expected

data.description: A deep bacterial infection of the iliopsoas or adjacent pelvic musculature that may cause fever, sepsis, lower back pain, abdominal pain, and pain radiating to the groin.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dysuria is not a defining feature
Scrotal pain is not typical unless pain is referred
Diarrhea is not typical
Bone marrow intracellular parasites would not be explained by a routine bacterial abscess

data.description: A genitourinary bacterial infection involving the prostate and possibly epididymis or testis. It commonly causes fever, dysuria, pelvic or lower abdominal pain, and scrotal or groin discomfort.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea is not typical
Prominent paraspinal muscle tenderness is less typical
Bone marrow intracellular organisms would not be expected
Headache is nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.description: This is a 56-year-old woman who underwent radical nephrectomy and lymph-node resection for clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma in February 2012. During subsequent follow-up, a single metastasis to the body of the left mandible was detected. She was referred in October 2012 for resection of the mandibular metastasis and fibular free-flap reconstruction. Two months later, bone scintigraphy revealed good vascularization of the flap, though additional bone metastases to the right humerus and pelvis were detected. In January 2014, the patient presented with visible bone exposure in the area of the graft with inflammation of surrounding tissues. Over days, there was an increase in bone exposure and necrosis without evidence of acute secondary infection.

data.diagnosis: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ), likely bisphosphonate- or denosumab-associated
data.description: Progressive exposed necrotic jaw bone in a patient receiving antiresorptive therapy, commonly used for skeletal metastases. It may occur after oral surgery or reconstruction and can affect vascularized bone grafts.
symptoms_in_common: Visible exposed bone in the mandibular graft region
Progressive increase in bone exposure over days
History of metastatic cancer with additional skeletal metastases, a setting in which antiresorptive therapy is commonly used
Prior mandibular surgery and fibular free-flap reconstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No antiresorptive medication use is explicitly provided in the case
No clear evidence of acute secondary infection

data.diagnosis: Chronic osteomyelitis of the mandibular fibular free flap
data.description: Persistent infection and inflammation of bone that can cause devitalized bone, sequestration, mucosal breakdown, and exposed bone after mandibular reconstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Exposed bone in the reconstructed mandible
History of major mandibular surgery and bone graft reconstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No evidence of acute secondary infection
No fever, purulent drainage, pain, or systemic infectious symptoms are reported
Rapidly progressive exposure without infectious findings is less typical

data.diagnosis: Recurrent or progressive metastatic clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma involving the mandibular reconstruction
data.description: Clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma can metastasize to bone, including the mandible, producing destructive osteolytic lesions and occasionally soft-tissue ulceration or pathologic bone exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Known history of clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma
Documented additional skeletal metastases in the humerus and pelvis
Progressive bony destruction/necrosis in the prior mandibular metastatic site
symptoms_not_in_common: Visible exposed devitalized bone is more characteristic of osteonecrosis or infection than uncomplicated metastatic disease
No reported enlarging soft-tissue mass, bleeding lesion, or biopsy evidence of recurrent tumor
No acute secondary infection is present

data.description: Radiation-induced hypovascular, hypocellular bone injury causing delayed bone exposure and necrosis, often after dental trauma or surgery in a previously irradiated jaw.
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of radiotherapy to the mandible or head and neck is provided
The affected bone is a fibular free flap with documented good vascularization after reconstruction
The clinical setting of metastatic cancer more strongly suggests medication-related osteonecrosis if antiresorptive treatment was given

data.description: 67-year-old man with 10 days of nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain unrelieved by omeprazole, followed on the day of presentation by substernal nonradiating chest heaviness on exertion progressing to rest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea. Past history includes mild asthma and prior hemicolectomy for dysplastic polyps with ventral abdominal hernia; remote 20 pack-year smoking history. On examination: tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnea, oxygen saturation 94% on 6 L oxygen, pallor, diaphoresis, accessory muscle use, elevated jugular venous pressure, grade 2/6 holosystolic apical murmur, left basilar rales, palpable liver edge 4 cm below the costal margin, and cool, clammy extremities with thready pulses.

A rare, rapidly progressive inflammatory myocarditis characterized histologically by myocyte necrosis, lymphocytic inflammation, and multinucleated giant cells. It often causes fulminant heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, conduction disease, and cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Apical holosystolic murmur consistent with functional mitral regurgitation
Left basilar rales consistent with pulmonary congestion
Hepatomegaly consistent with congestive heart failure
Cool clammy extremities and thready pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
Myocardial inflammatory infiltrate with giant cells and myocyte injury on biopsy image
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of prominent nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain before chest symptoms
History of mild asthma

data.description: An inflammatory myocardial disorder caused by eosinophil-rich infiltration of the heart, sometimes related to hypersensitivity, medications, infection, or systemic eosinophilic disease. It can present abruptly with chest pain, heart failure, and cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Signs of acute heart failure including elevated jugular venous pressure, rales, hepatomegaly, and a functional mitral regurgitation murmur
Cool extremities and weak pulses indicating low cardiac output
Gastrointestinal symptoms such as nausea and vomiting
History of asthma, which can coexist with eosinophilic disorders
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported peripheral eosinophilia
No reported rash, fever, allergic drug exposure, sinus disease, neuropathy, or other systemic eosinophilic manifestations
No reported history of new medication or toxin exposure

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock
data.description: Acute myocardial infarction results from coronary artery occlusion and can cause ischemic chest pain, pulmonary edema, papillary muscle dysfunction with mitral regurgitation, and cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional substernal chest heaviness progressing to pain at rest
Nausea and vomiting, which may be ischemic equivalents
New apical holosystolic murmur, potentially from ischemic mitral regurgitation
Cool clammy extremities and thready pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
Electrocardiographic abnormalities suggestive of myocardial injury or prior infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten-day prodrome dominated by bloating and epigastric pain preceding the acute chest symptoms
Myocardial biopsy showing prominent inflammatory infiltrates and giant cells would not be typical of uncomplicated infarction
No reported radiation of chest pain to the arm, jaw, neck, or back

data.description: Myocardial inflammation, commonly following a viral illness, that can cause chest pain resembling myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, impaired ventricular function, acute heart failure, and occasionally cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Recent systemic and gastrointestinal prodrome with nausea and vomiting
Signs of congestive heart failure including elevated jugular venous pressure, rales, hepatomegaly, and functional mitral regurgitation
Poor peripheral perfusion with cool clammy extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever, myalgias, sore throat, or respiratory viral syndrome
Multinucleated giant cells on biopsy would favor giant cell myocarditis rather than typical viral lymphocytic myocarditis
Severe rapidly progressive cardiogenic shock is less common in uncomplicated viral myocarditis

data.description: A 30-month-old boy presented with sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and nitric oxide before plastic surgery on June 7, 2004. The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.

A rare autosomal-dominant channelopathy caused most often by KCNJ2 variants. It is characterized by ventricular arrhythmias, prominent U waves/QU prolongation, episodic periodic paralysis, and distinctive craniofacial and skeletal features. The reported KCNJ2 p.Gly406Arg variant is a classic pathogenic ATS-associated variant.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction
Ventricular electrical abnormality with apparent QT/QU prolongation and prominent U waves on ECG
Distinctive facial appearance including round face, small upper jaw, small teeth, and sparse hair/nearly bald head
Hand skeletal abnormalities shown clinically and radiographically
Normal echocardiogram and normal ventricular function despite serious arrhythmia
Family member with paradoxical QT prolongation during epinephrine stress testing
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of episodic muscle weakness or periodic paralysis
Normal neurodevelopment
Normal toes, whereas toe syndactyly or other distal skeletal anomalies can occur

data.diagnosis: Congenital long QT syndrome type 1 (LQT1, KCNQ1-related)
data.description: An inherited cardiac repolarization disorder in which adrenergic stimulation can trigger marked QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, syncope, or cardiac arrest. Events are often provoked by exercise, emotional stress, or catecholamine exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest without structural heart disease
Paradoxical QT interval prolongation during epinephrine stress testing in the sister
Possible prolonged repolarization interval on ECG
Family pattern suggestive of an inherited arrhythmia syndrome
Normal electrolytes and normal cardiac structure
symptoms_not_in_common: Distinctive craniofacial abnormalities
Hand skeletal abnormalities
Sparse hair/nearly bald head
KCNJ2 p.Gly406Arg variant rather than a KCNQ1 variant
Cardiac arrest occurring during anesthetic induction rather than a classic exercise- or swimming-associated trigger

data.description: An inherited arrhythmia disorder, usually related to RYR2 or CASQ2, causing bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia during catecholamine stimulation, exercise, emotional stress, or anesthesia. The resting ECG and cardiac structure are often normal.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest in a young child
Potential catecholamine-sensitive repolarization/arrhythmic response in the family
No electrolyte abnormality or structural heart disease to explain the arrest
Absence of prior symptoms can occur before a first severe arrhythmic event
symptoms_not_in_common: QT/QU prolongation and prominent U-wave findings are not typical primary CPVT findings
Distinctive facial abnormalities
Hand skeletal abnormalities
Sparse hair/nearly bald head
KCNJ2 p.Gly406Arg variant, which supports Andersen-Tawil syndrome rather than CPVT

data.description: A severe syndromic long QT syndrome caused by CACNA1C variants. It can produce marked QT prolongation, ventricular arrhythmias, syndactyly, characteristic facial features, developmental abnormalities, and cardiac arrest in infancy or childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Normal intracardiac anatomy can be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal neurodevelopment, whereas developmental delay or autism-spectrum features are common
No reported syndactyly of fingers or toes
No reported congenital heart defect
No reported immune dysfunction, hypoglycemia, or severe dental abnormalities typical of many cases
KCNJ2 p.Gly406Arg variant rather than a CACNA1C variant

data.description: 27-year-old man with a history of ulcerative colitis presented with 2 weeks of fatigue and recent onset of bloating and persistent nonbloody loose stools after moving to the United States 11 days earlier. He also reported decreased exercise tolerance and about 4.5 kg weight loss over recent weeks. He had traveled to rural India in the prior month. Examination showed normal vital signs, a palpable spleen tip, and an erythematous papular rash on the anterior thorax. Laboratory studies showed marked leukocytosis with severe eosinophilia.

Infection with Strongyloides stercoralis, a soil-transmitted intestinal nematode acquired in tropical and subtropical regions. It can cause chronic gastrointestinal symptoms, skin manifestations, and eosinophilia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Palpable splenomegaly
Marked leukocytosis with very severe eosinophilia may be more pronounced than in uncomplicated infection

data.description: Intestinal infection with Ancylostoma or Necator species, usually acquired through skin exposure to contaminated soil. It may cause transient rash, gastrointestinal symptoms, eosinophilia, and chronic blood-loss anemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported anemia or overt iron-deficiency symptoms
Splenomegaly is not typical
Extreme leukocytosis and severe eosinophilia are less typical in uncomplicated hookworm infection

data.description: A helminthic infection caused by Toxocara larvae, often acquired from contaminated soil or food. Larval migration can produce marked eosinophilia, rash, constitutional symptoms, and hepatosplenomegaly.
symptoms_in_common: Recent rural travel with potential soil exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent loose stools are not a prominent typical manifestation
Bloating is not typical
No reported fever, hepatomegaly, cough, wheezing, or visual symptoms

data.description: A disorder characterized by persistent, marked eosinophilia with eosinophil-mediated organ involvement after secondary causes such as parasites, medications, and malignancy are excluded. It can affect the gastrointestinal tract, skin, spleen, and bone marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Bloating and loose stools consistent with gastrointestinal eosinophilic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent rural travel to India suggests a secondary parasitic cause rather than primary hypereosinophilic syndrome
Abrupt onset over approximately 2 weeks is less typical than persistent eosinophilia
No reported cardiac, pulmonary, neurologic, or thrombotic manifestations

data.description: A clonal myeloid neoplasm with sustained eosinophilia, often associated with constitutional symptoms, splenomegaly, marrow eosinophilic proliferation, and possible skin or gastrointestinal organ infiltration.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recent travel to rural India strongly supports an infectious or parasitic alternative
Acute gastrointestinal onset is less characteristic
No reported anemia, thrombocytopenia, blasts, or other evidence of a myeloid neoplasm

data.description: 28-year-old male who suddenly went into coma for 9 hours preceded by tonic-clonic seizures lasting 10 minutes. No fever, vomiting or micturition. No focal neurological signs. Past medical history was unremarkable. Neurological examination revealed normal cranial nerves, normal power and reflexes. Routine laboratory tests were normal.

A highly malignant diffuse astrocytic brain tumor that can show necrosis, ring enhancement, extensive edema, and intratumoral hemorrhage. The imaging and immunohistochemical profile shown, including GFAP and Olig2 positivity with absent IDH1 staining and retained ATRX, are most consistent with glioblastoma.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden deterioration due to intratumoral hemorrhage
Frontal lobe mass with surrounding edema and ring enhancement
Absence of fever or systemic infectious symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal neurological deficits despite a sizable frontal mass
No preceding headache, vomiting, or progressive cognitive/personality symptoms reported
Very abrupt presentation without a known prior period of progressive symptoms

data.description: A malignant astrocytic glioma that may cause seizures, cerebral edema, necrosis, contrast enhancement, and bleeding within the tumor. Glioblastoma is the highest-grade and most likely form in this setting.
symptoms_in_common: No fever or laboratory evidence of systemic infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal weakness, aphasia, or frontal-lobe behavioral symptoms
No chronic headache or vomiting reported
No prior progressive neurological complaints

data.description: A diffuse glioma that commonly affects younger adults and often presents with seizures. Higher-grade tumors can enhance, become necrotic, and occasionally bleed, although molecular testing for IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion would be required for diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Potential for a mass lesion with edema and altered consciousness
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked intratumoral hemorrhage is less typical
Rapid coma as the initial presentation is less typical
The reported IDH1-negative immunostaining is not typical for oligodendroglioma
No history of chronic seizure disorder or slowly progressive symptoms

data.description: A focal collection of infection within brain tissue that may appear as a ring-enhancing lesion with surrounding vasogenic edema and can cause seizures or impaired consciousness.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No vomiting or constitutional infectious symptoms
Normal routine laboratory tests
Prominent hemorrhagic appearance is atypical
No reported source of infection, immunosuppression, or leukocytosis

data.description: Metastatic tumors in the brain may bleed and present abruptly with seizures, coma, edema, and a contrast-enhancing mass. Melanoma, renal-cell carcinoma, choriocarcinoma, and thyroid carcinoma are classic hemorrhagic metastases.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden neurological decline related to intracerebral hemorrhage
Possible absence of focal deficits early in the presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: No known prior malignancy
Young age without a reported cancer history
Solitary infiltrative-appearing frontal lesion favors a primary glial tumor
Histology and glial-marker positivity favor glioblastoma rather than metastasis

data.description: 82-year-old man with 6 months of worsening back and left hip pain, worse with activity and sometimes waking him from sleep, without leg radiation, morning stiffness, fever, chills, night sweats, or bowel/bladder incontinence. He reported 9 kg weight loss over the past few months; symptoms began after recovery from pneumonia treated with levofloxacin. Past history includes sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary fibrosis, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, gout, postherpetic neuralgia, and basal-cell carcinoma. Exam showed no acute distress, afebrile, no spinal or sacroiliac tenderness, normal hip exam, no neurologic deficits, slightly diminished patellar reflexes bilaterally, intact sensation, normal rectal tone, and negative straight-leg raise.

data.diagnosis: Histoplasma capsulatum vertebral osteomyelitis (disseminated histoplasmosis involving the lumbar spine)
data.description: A fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum that can disseminate from the lungs to bone, rarely causing destructive vertebral osteomyelitis and paravertebral inflammatory masses. Calcified thoracic lymph nodes/granulomas can reflect prior pulmonary histoplasmosis.
symptoms_in_common: Pain that sometimes wakes him from sleep
Lumbar vertebral/disc destructive changes with adjacent soft-tissue inflammatory mass on CT
Prior pulmonary illness and thoracic imaging showing calcified hilar/mediastinal granulomatous changes
Advanced age and chronic cardiopulmonary disease, which may increase susceptibility to disseminated infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No chills
No night sweats
No focal neurologic deficits
No bowel or bladder incontinence
No spinal tenderness on examination

data.description: Usually bacterial infection of an intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral endplates, commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus. It can produce progressive pain, vertebral destruction, and paravertebral or epidural inflammatory collections.
symptoms_in_common: Six months of worsening back pain
Pain worsened by activity and occurring at night
CT appearance of disc-space/endplate destruction and adjacent paravertebral soft-tissue abnormality
Recent preceding infection treated as pneumonia
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No chills
No spinal tenderness
No neurologic deficit or radicular leg pain
Very indolent six-month course is less typical for untreated acute pyogenic infection
No reported bacteremia or systemic toxic appearance

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine causing slowly progressive vertebral destruction, disc involvement, paraspinal abscesses, chronic pain, and constitutional symptoms. It may occur without prominent pulmonary symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Vertebral destruction with adjacent paravertebral soft-tissue mass/collection
Absence of prominent neurologic findings can occur early
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No night sweats
No chills
No reported tuberculosis exposure or known active pulmonary tuberculosis
No spinal tenderness
No lower-extremity weakness, sensory loss, or bowel/bladder dysfunction

data.diagnosis: Spinal malignancy or metastatic vertebral disease
data.description: Cancer metastatic to the spine, or less commonly a primary spinal tumor, can cause progressive mechanical and nocturnal back pain, weight loss, vertebral destruction, and soft-tissue mass effect.
symptoms_in_common: Pain that sometimes wakes him from sleep
Destructive lumbar vertebral abnormality with soft-tissue component
History of malignancy, although prior basal-cell carcinoma is rarely metastatic
symptoms_not_in_common: No known visceral malignancy with a high tendency for bone metastasis
Disc-space and adjacent endplate involvement is more characteristic of infection than most metastases
No neurologic deficits
No focal spinal tenderness
No reported anemia, hypercalcemia, or other cancer-related systemic findings

data.description: A 47-year-old woman presented with intermittent cough, shortness of breath, fever (body temperature up to 38.5°C), accompanied by right eyelid swelling around June 17, 2017, which worsened day by day. Weight loss was about 9 kg. Physical examination included high body temperature of 39°C, right eyelid swelling, and a painless enlarged lymph node about 2 cm × 2 cm in size in the left axilla. Auscultation of lungs revealed coarse respiratory sounds with moist rale. No hepatosplenomegaly and edema in lower limbs.
A systemic fungal infection that can involve the lungs, lymph nodes, skin, soft tissues, and other organs, particularly in patients with impaired cellular immunity.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary nodular and infiltrative lesions on CT
Histologic appearance compatible with fungal organisms in inflamed tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of hepatosplenomegaly
No lower-extremity edema

data.description: An invasive infection caused by Cryptococcus species that commonly affects the lungs and central nervous system but may disseminate to lymph nodes, skin, soft tissue, and the orbit.
symptoms_in_common: Eyelid swelling suggesting possible orbital or cutaneous involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, neck stiffness, or other reported neurologic symptoms
No reported skin papules or umbilicated lesions
No hepatosplenomegaly

data.description: A severe mold infection, usually occurring in immunocompromised patients, that begins in the lungs and can spread hematogenously to the skin, orbit, lymph nodes, and other tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral lung nodules and infiltrates
Eyelid swelling, which can occur with orbital fungal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No hemoptysis reported
No pleuritic chest pain reported
Painless axillary lymph-node enlargement is less characteristic than pulmonary disease

data.description: A rapidly progressive invasive fungal infection caused by Mucorales molds that may involve the lungs, orbit, skin, and soft tissue, often producing tissue necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive eyelid swelling, which can indicate rhino-orbital involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported facial pain, nasal discharge, or black nasal eschar
No reported diabetes mellitus or ketoacidosis
Painless axillary lymphadenopathy is not a classic presentation

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can involve the lungs, lymph nodes, and extrapulmonary tissues, causing constitutional symptoms and diffuse pulmonary abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapidly progressive eyelid swelling is less typical
Histology described by the images appears more suggestive of fungal organisms than acid-fast bacilli
No night sweats reported
No hepatosplenomegaly

data.description: A 19-year-old previously healthy gravida 3 para 2002 female presented at 28 weeks' gestation after emigrating to the U.S. at 25 weeks of gestation. During the 20th week of gestation, she experienced a maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache. She and her spouse had unprotected intercourse through the first and second trimester. The patient's initial fetal ultrasound with neurosonography revealed cerebral ventriculomegaly (20-25 mm) with dangling choroid, prominent 3rd ventricle, and a widened cavum septum pellucidum. Amniocentesis showed negative NAT for ZIKV with no evidence of chromosomal variations by CMA; TORCH panel was negative.

Fetal neurologic injury caused by maternal Zika virus infection during pregnancy, which may include microcephaly, ventriculomegaly, cortical malformations, intracranial calcifications, and other brain abnormalities. Fetal infection can occur despite a negative amniotic-fluid NAT result.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in or recent emigration from a Zika-endemic area
Unprotected sexual intercourse with spouse during pregnancy, allowing possible sexual transmission
symptoms_not_in_common: No fetal microcephaly reported
Negative amniotic-fluid Zika NAT

data.description: A transplacentally acquired CMV infection that can cause fetal ventriculomegaly, microcephaly, intracranial calcifications, growth restriction, hearing loss, and neurodevelopmental impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Possible fetal central nervous system abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache are more suggestive of Zika than CMV
TORCH panel was negative
No intracranial calcifications reported
No fetal growth restriction reported
No microcephaly reported
No hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, or hydrops reported

data.diagnosis: Fetal cerebral aqueductal stenosis causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct impairs cerebrospinal-fluid flow from the third to fourth ventricle, typically causing enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles.
symptoms_in_common: Dangling choroid plexus, consistent with hydrocephalus
No chromosomal variation detected by chromosomal microarray
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash
Maternal conjunctivitis
Maternal fever
Maternal headache
Exposure risk for Zika virus infection
Abnormal/widened cavum septum pellucidum may suggest a broader cerebral developmental abnormality rather than isolated aqueductal stenosis

data.description: 26-year-old Chinese female with a 2-year history of progressive lower-limb weakness and scissor gait սկսing at age 24, followed by dysphagia and severe cognitive impairment (MMSE 16/30). Exam showed severe spasticity in the lower extremities, mild spasticity in the upper extremities, and left patellar clonus. Birth history and developmental milestones were normal. Genetic testing later showed compound heterozygous mutations consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

data.diagnosis: Spastic paraplegia type 11 (SPG11, spatacsin-related hereditary spastic paraplegia)
data.description: An autosomal-recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG11 mutations. It commonly causes progressive lower-limb spasticity, gait impairment, cognitive decline, dysphagia, white-matter abnormalities, and thinning of the corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive lower-limb weakness beginning in young adulthood
Normal early development followed by progressive neurologic decline
Autosomal-recessive inheritance with compound heterozygous mutations
MRI features suggestive of corpus callosum thinning and periventricular white-matter changes

data.diagnosis: Spastic paraplegia type 15 (SPG15, ZFYVE26-related hereditary spastic paraplegia)
data.description: A rare autosomal-recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia that resembles SPG11 and may produce progressive spastic paraparesis, intellectual/cognitive decline, dysphagia, white-matter disease, and a thin corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive spastic weakness of the lower limbs
Possible thin corpus callosum and white-matter MRI abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous mutations consistent with SPG11 rather than ZFYVE26
SPG15 more often has retinal abnormalities or pigmentary retinopathy, which were not reported

data.diagnosis: Spastic paraplegia type 21 (SPG21, Maspardin-related hereditary spastic paraplegia)
data.description: An autosomal-recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia characterized by slowly progressive lower-limb spasticity, gait dysfunction, cognitive impairment, and sometimes dysarthria or swallowing difficulty.
symptoms_not_in_common: SPG21 frequently begins in childhood or adolescence, whereas this patient developed symptoms at age 24
Thin corpus callosum and the characteristic MRI pattern are more strongly associated with SPG11/SPG15
The reported genetic findings support SPG11 rather than SPG21

data.diagnosis: Adult-onset leukodystrophy with hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotype
data.description: A group of inherited white-matter disorders that can present in adulthood with progressive pyramidal tract dysfunction, spastic gait, cognitive decline, and dysphagia. SPG11 itself may be considered within the broader complicated-HSP/leukodystrophy spectrum.
symptoms_not_in_common: Many leukodystrophies cause additional features such as peripheral neuropathy, adrenal dysfunction, seizures, ataxia, vision loss, or psychiatric symptoms, none of which were reported
The specific SPG11 compound heterozygous mutations make SPG11 a more precise diagnosis

diagnoses.name: Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
diagnoses.title: Autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.description: A 25-year-old female in her third trimester of pregnancy presented with paroxysmal headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension up to 230/130 for three weeks. Her medical history was negative for previous hypertension, and physical examination was unremarkable. Initial work-up excluded pre-eclampsia. Her urine catecholamines were markedly elevated: Dopamine 607 μg/24 hours (range 65-400), Norepinephrine 978 μg/24 hours (range 15-80), Metanephrine 108 μg/24 hours (range 24-96), Normetanephrine 4067 μg/24 hours (range 75-375), and Vanillyl mandelic acid 13.6 mg/24 hours (range 2-7). Epinephrine level was normal at 0.8 μg/24 hours (range 0.0-20.0). Initial abdominal MRI showed a 28×19 mm left juxta-adrenal mass that was later found to be brown fat.

A catecholamine-secreting extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumor arising from paraganglionic tissue in the mediastinum, often adjacent to the heart or great vessels. It commonly produces norepinephrine and can cause severe episodic hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Normal epinephrine level, consistent with many extra-adrenal paragangliomas
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms clearly atypical for this diagnosis

data.description: A catecholamine-producing neuroendocrine tumor of the adrenal medulla that causes episodic or sustained hypertension, headache, palpitations, and diaphoresis. It is an important consideration during pregnancy because of major maternal and fetal risk.
symptoms_not_in_common: No adrenal mass was identified
The initially suspected left juxta-adrenal lesion was brown fat rather than a tumor
Imaging demonstrates a mediastinal/cardiac-region lesion rather than an adrenal lesion
Normal epinephrine level is less typical for many adrenal pheochromocytomas

data.description: A pregnancy-specific hypertensive disorder occurring after 20 weeks of gestation, usually associated with proteinuria and/or maternal organ dysfunction. Severe disease can cause headache and marked hypertension.
symptoms_not_in_common: Paroxysmal palpitations and sweating
Marked elevation of urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Elevated vanillylmandelic acid
Evidence of a catecholamine-secreting mediastinal mass
Preeclampsia was excluded during the initial work-up

data.description: Excess thyroid hormone production can produce sympathetic-like symptoms, including palpitations, sweating, anxiety, and systolic hypertension, but it does not usually cause marked catecholamine metabolite elevation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely high urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Paroxysmal hypertensive crises up to 230/130
Mediastinal/cardiac-region mass consistent with a neuroendocrine tumor
No reported weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance, goiter, or ophthalmopathy

data.description: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 3-day history of headache and fatigue, followed by sudden onset of confusion and language production difficulties while typing at work. The confusion resolved briefly but recurred later that evening. She had a history of myasthenia gravis (diagnosed 18 years prior, treated with mycophenolate mofetil for 7 years), vitamin B12 deficiency, and hypertension. Past surgical history included supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (31 years prior), transsternal thymectomy and wedge resection of right upper lobe for cortical thymoma (22 years prior), and sigmoid colectomy for recurrent diverticulitis (7 years prior). On examination at the current hospital, she had severe expressive aphasia, followed commands intermittently, disconjugate gaze at rest, motor strength 5/5 in left extremities and 4/5 in right extremities. Blood phosphorus was 2.2 mg/dL (reference range 2.6-4.5); other routine labs were normal.

A focal bacterial brain infection caused by Nocardia species, an opportunistic branching filamentous bacterium that commonly affects patients receiving chronic immunosuppression and can form ring-enhancing cerebral abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Immunosuppression from long-term mycophenolate mofetil use
Focal brain lesion with surrounding edema and ring-like enhancement
Histology consistent with a suppurative inflammatory process
symptoms_not_in_common: Brief spontaneous resolution and recurrence of confusion
Disconjugate gaze at rest
Mild hypophosphatemia

data.description: A localized collection of pus within the brain caused by bacteria, typically producing headache, altered mental status, focal neurologic deficits, edema, and a ring-enhancing lesion on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Focal lesion with edema and ring enhancement
Suppurative inflammatory cells on tissue examination
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever
No reported leukocytosis or other routine laboratory abnormalities
No described contiguous ear, sinus, dental, cardiac, or pulmonary source of infection
Disconjugate gaze at rest
Brief fluctuation of symptoms before persistent aphasia

data.description: An opportunistic infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii that produces focal encephalitis and often multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions in severely immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Focal neurologic deficits including aphasia and right-sided weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: No known advanced HIV infection or profound T-cell immunodeficiency
Solitary dominant lesion rather than multiple classic basal-ganglia lesions
Histology appears suppurative rather than typical necrotizing toxoplasma encephalitis
No reported fever
Disconjugate gaze at rest

data.description: A fungal infection of the central nervous system caused by Aspergillus species, usually occurring in markedly immunocompromised patients and causing hemorrhagic infarcts, abscesses, or ring-enhancing lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing brain lesion with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pulmonary or sinus aspergillosis
No reported fever or systemic fungal infection signs
No prominent hemorrhagic infarction described
Histology is more suggestive of bacterial suppuration than fungal hyphae
Brief fluctuation of confusion

data.description: An aggressive primary glial brain tumor in older adults that can present with rapidly progressive focal neurologic deficits, cognitive changes, headache, edema, necrosis, and irregular ring enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing left hemispheric brain mass with edema and central necrotic appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset and fluctuating confusion over hours
Only a 3-day prodrome before major neurologic deficits
Suppurative inflammatory histology rather than malignant glial cells
Chronic immunosuppression more strongly favors opportunistic infection
Disconjugate gaze at rest

data.description: 36-year-old obese woman with type 2 diabetes for 5 years, positive Mantoux test, and a smoking history presented with 5 days of fever, chills, productive cough with yellow sputum, and sharp right lower chest pain worsened by deep breathing. Symptoms began about 1 week after a stay at a lakeside cottage. On return for persistent symptoms, she was febrile to 39°C with mild tachycardia (104 bpm), and chest examination showed decreased air entry with bronchial breath sounds in the right lower chest.

A severe atypical bacterial pneumonia acquired by inhalation of aerosolized freshwater, often from lakes, plumbing, hot tubs, or air-conditioning systems. It can progress from focal to multilobar or bilateral infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Recent stay at a lakeside cottage with possible freshwater aerosol exposure
Diabetes and smoking history, which increase pneumonia risk
Right lower lobe consolidation progressing to bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: Yellow sputum is less typical than a dry or minimally productive cough, although it can occur
No reported gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea or abdominal pain
No reported confusion, headache, hyponatremia, or elevated liver enzymes

data.diagnosis: Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia due to Streptococcus pneumoniae
data.description: Pneumococcal pneumonia is a common cause of acute community-acquired lobar pneumonia, producing fever, productive cough, pleuritic pain, and focal bronchial breathing.
symptoms_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest pain worsened by deep inspiration
Bronchial breath sounds and decreased air entry over the right lower chest
Right lower lobe air-space consolidation on chest imaging
Diabetes and smoking as risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Freshwater/lakeside exposure is not specifically associated with pneumococcal pneumonia
Rapid evolution to multifocal bilateral infiltrates is less classic for uncomplicated focal pneumococcal lobar pneumonia
No mention of rust-colored sputum

data.diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia due to Klebsiella pneumoniae
data.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae can cause severe necrotizing or multilobar bacterial pneumonia, particularly in people with diabetes, chronic alcohol use, or impaired host defenses.
symptoms_in_common: Productive cough with purulent yellow sputum
Diabetes mellitus as a major risk factor
Focal right lower lobe consolidation with subsequent more extensive bilateral air-space disease
symptoms_not_in_common: She is young for typical severe Klebsiella pneumonia
No reported alcohol-use disorder or chronic debilitating illness
No described currant-jelly sputum
Lakeside freshwater exposure is not a characteristic source

data.description: Melioidosis is an environmental infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, acquired through contact with contaminated soil or surface water. Pneumonia may be acute, severe, multifocal, and more likely in patients with diabetes.
symptoms_in_common: Diabetes mellitus, a major risk factor for melioidosis
Possible exposure to environmental freshwater during a lakeside stay
Progression from focal to bilateral patchy pulmonary infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: No stated travel or residence in a melioidosis-endemic region
No reported direct exposure to muddy soil, floodwater, or skin inoculation
The very short illness after a brief cottage stay is less specific for melioidosis

data.description: Pulmonary tuberculosis is a chronic infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. A positive Mantoux test indicates prior sensitization but does not by itself establish active disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute onset over 5 days is atypical for pulmonary tuberculosis
Prominent chills and high acute fever are more consistent with bacterial pneumonia
Purulent yellow sputum and pleuritic chest pain are less characteristic
Right lower lobe consolidation followed by rapid bilateral air-space progression is not the typical upper-lobe cavitary pattern
No reported chronic cough, weight loss, night sweats, hemoptysis, or known tuberculosis exposure

data.description: 19-year-old female with hypotonia, weak breathing and cry at birth. During the first month of life she developed respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation. She had patent ductus arteriosus repaired at age 2, recurrent respiratory infections, and scoliosis surgery at age 12. At age 4, nerve stimulation showed a 36% decrement in compound muscle action potential area; no repetitive CMAPs were seen after single nerve stimulation. AChR and MuSK antibodies were negative. Recent examination showed normal cognition, bilateral ptosis, mild limitation of upgaze, and facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness with preserved deep tendon reflexes.

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to RAPSN deficiency
data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by impaired clustering of acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction. It commonly presents in infancy with severe generalized and respiratory weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Weak cry and weak breathing at birth
Early respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a typical feature
Mild limitation of upgaze can occur but is not universal
Severe scoliosis requiring surgery is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to CHRNE or other acetylcholine-receptor subunit deficiency
data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by reduced expression or abnormal function of the muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. Severe forms can cause neonatal respiratory insufficiency and persistent ocular-bulbar weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Significant decrement on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not usually related to acetylcholine-receptor deficiency
Scoliosis is not a core manifestation, although it may develop secondarily from chronic weakness
Recurrent respiratory infections are secondary complications rather than a primary diagnostic feature

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to MUSK deficiency
data.description: A congenital neuromuscular-junction disorder caused by biallelic MUSK variants, disrupting formation and maintenance of the postsynaptic motor endplate. It may cause severe neonatal respiratory weakness, ptosis, and bulbar dysfunction despite negative serum MuSK antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Weak respiratory effort and cry at birth
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not typical
Scoliosis requiring surgery is not a characteristic primary feature
Preserved deep tendon reflexes may occur but are not specifically characteristic

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to LRP4 deficiency
data.description: A rare postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by impaired agrin-LRP4-MuSK signaling, leading to defective neuromuscular-junction development. Clinical severity ranges from neonatal respiratory failure to ocular, bulbar, and limb weakness.
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a usual manifestation
Marked scoliosis is not a defining feature
The long-term need for tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation is possible but represents a particularly severe course

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to DOK7 deficiency
data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by abnormal Dok-7 signaling at the neuromuscular junction. It usually produces limb-girdle, neck, and respiratory weakness, often with preserved reflexes and negative autoimmune antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Respiratory insufficiency and recurrent respiratory infections
Scoliosis related to chronic axial weakness
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe weakness at birth and respiratory failure in the first month are less typical than in RAPSN or acetylcholine-receptor deficiency
Ptosis and limitation of upgaze are less typical because ocular muscles are often relatively spared
Patent ductus arteriosus is not a typical feature
Prominent facial and bulbar weakness is less characteristic

data.description: A 52-year-old man was brought to the emergency department with acute onset shortness of breath and confusion. On physical examination, he was agitated and taking deep breaths at a rate of 28/min. Initial venous blood gas on ambient air showed pH 7.02, partial pressure of carbon dioxide 3.4 kPa, and partial pressure of oxygen 4.1 kPa. Laboratory studies revealed blood glucose 7.1 mmol/L (reference range 4.4-6.1), lactic acid 6.6 mmol/L (0.5-2.2), serum anion gap 19 mmol/L (8-16), serum osmolality 318 mmol/kg (275-295), serum osmolal gap 20 mmol/kg (<10), and acute kidney injury with creatinine 141 μmol/L (70-120). Blood ethanol was undetectable and urine drug screen was negative. Urinalysis showed haematuria and no ketones.
Toxic alcohol ingestion causing severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, elevated osmolal gap, acute kidney injury, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition in urine.
symptoms_in_common: Deep rapid breathing consistent with respiratory compensation for severe metabolic acidosis
Urine microscopy consistent with calcium oxalate crystals
Elevated lactate or apparent lactate elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical symptom is strongly inconsistent; ethanol may be absent in isolated ethylene glycol ingestion

data.description: Toxic alcohol ingestion metabolized to formic acid, producing a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and often an elevated osmolal gap; it classically causes visual toxicity.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute kidney injury is less characteristic than in ethylene glycol poisoning
Haematuria is not typical
Calcium oxalate crystals in urine are not typical
No visual symptoms are reported

data.description: A diabetic metabolic emergency caused by insulin deficiency, leading to hyperglycaemia, ketone production, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, dehydration, and Kussmaul respirations.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney injury can occur with dehydration
symptoms_not_in_common: Blood glucose is only mildly elevated rather than markedly elevated
Urine ketones are absent
Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
Haematuria is not typical
Calcium oxalate crystals are not typical

data.description: Aspirin or salicylate toxicity can cause agitation, tachypnoea, respiratory alkalosis followed by high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and elevated lactate in severe poisoning.
symptoms_in_common: Acute kidney injury may occur in severe poisoning
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated osmolal gap is not typical
Calcium oxalate crystals in urine are not typical
Haematuria is not typical
The very low carbon dioxide level could fit respiratory alkalosis, but the overall toxic alcohol pattern is more suggestive

data.description: 36-year-old man with 18 days of fever up to 39.5°C, preceded by throat swelling sensation. Symptoms began with throat swelling, then fever 3 days later, with persistent fevers despite amoxicillin-clavulanic acid for presumed pharyngitis, along with headache and fatigue. He also reported lower neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement, without dysphagia, odynophagia, rhinorrhea, or rash. Past history includes seasonal allergies. He traveled to the southwestern United States 2 weeks before symptom onset; his wife had a self-limited febrile sore throat during the trip. On examination, he was afebrile but tachycardic, with a normal oropharynx, no lymphadenopathy, and a firm, nontender palpable thyroid in the anterior neck.

A self-limited inflammatory thyroid disorder, often occurring after a viral upper-respiratory illness. It causes thyroid enlargement, neck discomfort, fever, elevated inflammatory markers, and sometimes transient thyrotoxicosis.
symptoms_in_common: Lack of response to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid
symptoms_not_in_common: Thyroid tenderness is often present, whereas the thyroid was nontender
Radiating jaw or ear pain was not reported
Symptoms of thyrotoxicosis such as tremor, palpitations, heat intolerance, or weight loss were not reported

data.description: A rare bacterial infection of the thyroid gland that can cause fever, neck swelling, thyroid pain, cellulitis, and sometimes formation of a thyroid abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Possible onset after an upper-respiratory or pharyngeal infection
symptoms_not_in_common: The thyroid was nontender, while bacterial thyroid infection is usually painful and tender
No dysphagia or odynophagia
No overlying skin erythema or fluctuance was described
No lymphadenopathy was present
Lack of improvement with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid is less typical for a susceptible bacterial infection

data.diagnosis: Viral thyroiditis associated with an acute viral upper-respiratory infection
data.description: Inflammation of the thyroid occurring during or shortly after a viral illness; common triggers include enteroviruses, influenza-like viruses, adenovirus, and other respiratory viruses.
symptoms_in_common: Recent exposure to a wife with a self-limited febrile sore throat
Initial throat swelling sensation followed by fever
Diffuse anterior neck or thyroid swelling
Normal oropharyngeal examination after the initial illness
symptoms_not_in_common: No rhinorrhea, cough, or other prominent respiratory symptoms
No rash
The duration and severity of fever are more prolonged than many uncomplicated viral upper-respiratory infections

data.diagnosis: Coccidioidomycosis (primary pulmonary or disseminated Valley fever)
data.description: A fungal infection caused by Coccidioides species, acquired through inhalation of spores in the southwestern United States. It commonly causes fever, fatigue, headache, and respiratory symptoms; extrapulmonary dissemination is uncommon but can involve many organs.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to the southwestern United States
Symptoms beginning about 2 weeks after travel, compatible with the usual incubation period
Failure to improve with antibacterial therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, or other pulmonary symptoms
No rash, including erythema nodosum
Thyroid enlargement or thyroiditis is an unusual manifestation
The wife having a brief sore throat illness is more suggestive of a contagious viral infection than coccidioidomycosis

data.diagnosis: Lemierre syndrome (internal jugular septic thrombophlebitis after pharyngitis)
data.description: A potentially severe complication of pharyngitis, usually due to Fusobacterium necrophorum, characterized by persistent fever, unilateral neck pain or swelling, internal jugular vein thrombosis, and possible septic emboli.
symptoms_in_common: Limited response to initial oral antibiotic therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No unilateral neck tenderness was reported
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No pulmonary symptoms or evidence of septic emboli
The palpable abnormality was a firm thyroid rather than a painful lateral neck mass
No odynophagia or active pharyngitis on examination

data.description: 42-year-old man with coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia presented with 2 days of sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back in a bandlike pattern, worsening with movement, associated with nausea and early satiety. He also had substernal chest pressure similar to his usual angina but not relieved by nitroglycerin. He denied trauma, vomiting, or GI bleeding. History notable for chronic diarrhea since coronary bypass surgery, worsened after a lipid-lowering medication dose increase 6 months earlier, with 16 kg unintentional weight loss over 6 months, intermittent early satiety, daily headaches, nocturia, and feeling warm at night without fever or night sweats. Exam showed mild left upper quadrant tenderness without peritoneal signs; vital signs were stable. Labs showed mildly elevated amylase, lipase, AST, and ALT with otherwise normal blood counts, renal function, electrolytes, bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and triglycerides. ECG and chest radiograph were normal.

A rare systemic infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei, classically producing malabsorption, chronic diarrhea, weight loss, abdominal pain, and mesenteric lymph-node involvement. It can also involve the heart, nervous system, joints, and pancreas.
symptoms_in_common: Nighttime warmth/constitutional symptoms without documented fever
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden severe left upper quadrant pain radiating to the back
Substernal chest pressure resembling angina
Mild elevation of amylase and lipase
Nocturia

data.description: Acute inflammation of the pancreas, usually causing abrupt upper abdominal pain radiating to the back with nausea and elevated pancreatic enzymes. Causes include gallstones, alcohol, hypertriglyceridemia, medications, ischemia, and systemic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden left upper quadrant abdominal pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Six months of chronic diarrhea
16 kg unintentional weight loss
Chronic early satiety
Mesenteric lymph-node enlargement
Daily headaches
Nocturia
Nighttime warmth
Substernal chest pressure similar to angina

data.description: Some medications, including certain lipid-lowering agents and other cardiovascular drugs, can cause diarrhea, liver-enzyme abnormalities, pancreatitis, or pancreatic enzyme elevation. Drug-related gastrointestinal toxicity may worsen after a dose increase.
symptoms_in_common: Diarrhea worsened after a lipid-lowering medication dose increase
Weight loss associated with prolonged diarrhea
Mild elevation of amylase and lipase
Mild elevation of AST and ALT
symptoms_not_in_common: Mesenteric lymph-node enlargement on CT
Intermittent early satiety predating or persisting beyond acute symptoms
Daily headaches
Nocturia
Nighttime warmth
Substernal chest pressure not relieved by nitroglycerin

data.description: Lymphoma involving the small bowel or mesenteric lymph nodes can cause abdominal pain, diarrhea, early satiety, weight loss, constitutional symptoms, and abdominal lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden bandlike pain radiating to the back
Mildly elevated amylase and lipase
Substernal chest pressure resembling angina
Nocturia
Normal blood counts
Absence of fever or drenching night sweats

data.diagnosis: Chronic mesenteric ischemia with possible acute exacerbation
data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of mesenteric arteries can cause intestinal ischemia, typically with postprandial abdominal pain, food avoidance, diarrhea, and weight loss. Severe acute ischemia can cause abrupt abdominal pain.
symptoms_in_common: Coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia indicating significant atherosclerotic risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain not clearly described as postprandial
Mesenteric lymph-node enlargement
Mildly elevated amylase and lipase suggesting pancreatic involvement
Daily headaches
Nocturia
Nighttime warmth
Stable vital signs and lack of peritoneal signs despite acute pain

data.description: A 59-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of stiffness, swelling, and severe pain beginning in the metacarpophalangeal joint of the right thumb, followed by bilateral ankle involvement 3 days later. She had a history of stroke, glaucoma, and total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 7 years prior. The patient lived in New England, worked in health care, and reported unprotected vaginal intercourse 2 weeks before presentation. Physical examination showed the right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint was erythematous, warm, and painful with movement. Both ankles showed effusion and warmth without erythema, with pain on all range of motion. No fever, chills, night sweats, or systemic symptoms were reported. Joint stiffness was not worse in the morning and did not improve throughout the day. Symptoms had not improved despite 4 days of methylprednisolone therapy.
Systemic spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae that can cause migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, dermatitis, and/or septic arthritis, often after asymptomatic genital infection.
symptoms_in_common: Acute onset of severe joint pain and swelling
Sequential or migratory involvement of multiple joints
Absence of genital symptoms does not exclude infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported rash or pustular skin lesions
No reported tenosynovitis
Marked erythema of a thumb metacarpophalangeal joint is less typical than distal migratory arthralgias
No fever or systemic symptoms

data.diagnosis: Staphylococcus aureus septic arthritis with polyarticular involvement
data.description: Bacterial infection of one or more joints, commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, producing acute painful warmth, effusion, and restricted motion; polyarticular disease can occur with bacteremia.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous and painful thumb metacarpophalangeal joint
Pain with all ankle range of motion
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, or systemic illness
Bilateral ankle involvement developing after a thumb joint presentation is less typical than single-joint disease
No reported bacteremia symptoms or obvious skin/wound source

data.diagnosis: Reactive arthritis following sexually transmitted infection
data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis that develops after genitourinary or gastrointestinal infection, commonly associated with Chlamydia trachomatis and sometimes gonococcal infection.
symptoms_in_common: Acute asymmetric lower-extremity arthritis involving the ankles
Joint symptoms occurring shortly after possible genitourinary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe inflammatory thumb metacarpophalangeal arthritis is less typical
No reported urethritis, cervicitis, dysuria, or vaginal discharge
No conjunctivitis or uveitis
No enthesitis, heel pain, mucosal lesions, or characteristic rash
Symptoms began only about 2 weeks after intercourse, which is relatively early for classic reactive arthritis

data.description: A late manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi infection causing intermittent or persistent inflammatory arthritis, usually affecting large joints such as the knee.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in New England, an endemic region for Lyme disease
Absence of fever or major systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt severe onset over days
Thumb metacarpophalangeal joint involvement
Bilateral ankle arthritis rather than predominant knee involvement
No reported tick bite, erythema migrans rash, or preceding flu-like illness
Prominent joint erythema and severe pain with all motion are less typical

data.description: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis that typically causes symmetric small-joint synovitis, prolonged morning stiffness, and progressive joint damage if untreated.
symptoms_not_in_common: Very abrupt onset over 9 days
Initial involvement of only the right thumb followed by ankles
Stiffness was not worse in the morning
Stiffness did not improve during the day
Severe erythema and acute effusions suggest an infectious process more than rheumatoid arthritis
No improvement after corticosteroid therapy

data.description: A 29-year-old man presented to the hospital after several weeks of lumbar pain and fever up to 38°C. He had no significant past medical history. Physical examination revealed vital signs of blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 121/min, and body temperature 38.2°C. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected on examination. Laboratory tests showed anemia with hematocrit 31.8% and hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, white blood cell count 3.92 × 10³/μL, elevated liver enzymes with AST 78 IU/L and ALT 71 IU/L, and markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase 1,591 IU/L. Serum cortisol level was 17.47 μg/dL at 8 AM and ACTH level was 12.1 pg/mL (normal range: 10-90). Ten days after admission, the patient developed pancytopenia with WBC 2.88 × 10³/μL, Hb 10.7 g/dL, and platelets 129 × 10³/μL. Bone marrow biopsy was negative for specific hematologic or malignant disorder.

data.diagnosis: Primary bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: A rare extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma involving one or both adrenal glands, most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. It commonly presents with fever, adrenal-region or back pain, elevated LDH, cytopenias, and bilateral adrenal masses without prominent peripheral lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral adrenal enlargement/masses on abdominal imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal morning cortisol and ACTH without overt adrenal insufficiency
