data.description: An aggressive lymphoma in which malignant B cells proliferate mainly within small blood vessels rather than forming obvious lymph nodes or masses. It can cause persistent fever, high LDH, cytopenias, liver abnormalities, pulmonary findings, and adrenal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Negative or nondiagnostic bone marrow biopsy can occur
Possible bilateral adrenal involvement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent lumbar pain is less characteristic
Discrete bulky bilateral adrenal masses are less typical than diffuse organ involvement

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with bilateral adrenal tuberculosis
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can disseminate and involve the adrenal glands, causing bilateral adrenal enlargement, fever, constitutional symptoms, anemia, abnormal liver tests, and eventually adrenal insufficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia can occur in disseminated disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase is less typical
No reported pulmonary tuberculosis symptoms such as chronic cough or weight loss
Normal cortisol and ACTH without adrenal insufficiency
Rapid progression to pancytopenia is less typical

data.description: Disseminated infection with Histoplasma can involve the reticuloendothelial system and adrenal glands, producing fever, cytopenias, liver enzyme elevation, bilateral adrenal masses, and adrenal insufficiency, especially in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known immunosuppression or relevant exposure history
Marked LDH elevation is more suggestive of aggressive lymphoma
No hepatosplenomegaly
Normal adrenal hormone testing without adrenal insufficiency

data.diagnosis: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis secondary to occult lymphoma or infection
data.description: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is a severe hyperinflammatory syndrome, often triggered by lymphoma or infection, causing persistent fever, rapidly progressive cytopenias, liver dysfunction, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers including LDH.
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly
No reported hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, or hemophagocytosis on bone marrow examination
Bilateral adrenal masses are not a primary feature of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

diagnoses.name: Non-Hodgkin T-cell lymphoma, natural killer (NK)/T-cell, nasal type

data.description: A 23-year-old female presented with a complaint of intermittent dyspnea (New York Heart Association NYHA grade, II), which aggravates on exertion and mild chest pain. No past significant medical and surgical history was given by the patient. On clinical examination, bruit was heard on auscultation in the left mid-zone.

A congenital or acquired abnormal direct communication between a pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein, creating a right-to-left shunt. Large lesions may produce a pulmonary bruit and exertional breathlessness.
symptoms_in_common: Bruit heard over the left mid-lung zone
Young age with no significant prior medical history

data.description: A large or complex subtype of pulmonary arteriovenous malformation involving multiple feeding pulmonary arteries and/or draining pulmonary veins, often appearing as prominent tortuous vascular structures on contrast CT.
symptoms_in_common: Localized pulmonary bruit in the left mid-zone
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported cyanosis
No reported hemoptysis
No reported neurologic complications such as stroke or brain abscess

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary artery aneurysm with arteriovenous communication
data.description: An abnormal focal enlargement of a pulmonary arterial segment, sometimes associated with a congenital arteriovenous fistulous connection and turbulent blood flow.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary bruit due to turbulent vascular flow
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hemoptysis
No reported syncope
No reported severe pulmonary hypertension symptoms
No reported signs of right-sided heart failure

data.description: A localized dilatation of a pulmonary vein that can mimic a pulmonary vascular malformation on imaging; it is often congenital and may occasionally cause chest symptoms or a vascular murmur when associated with abnormal vascular flow.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional worsening of shortness of breath
symptoms_not_in_common: A pulmonary bruit is less typical
No reported palpitations or arrhythmia
No reported hemoptysis
No history of mitral valve disease or pulmonary venous hypertension

data.description: A 65-year-old man presented with bilateral leg swelling that had worsened over six weeks. He reported vague abdominal discomfort and tiredness. Physical examination revealed bilateral pitting edema up to the groin, without erythema, tenderness, or warmth. The patient was systemically well with normal heart sounds and clear chest examination. No palpable masses or lymphadenopathy were found in the abdomen. Laboratory testing showed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 95 g/L; normal range 130-180), elevated C-reactive protein of 33.0 mg/L (normal range 0-5.0), and raised IgG4 level (3.55 g/L; normal range 0.08-1.4). Doppler ultrasound showed no deep vein thrombosis.

A fibroinflammatory manifestation of IgG4-related disease in which inflammatory tissue develops in the retroperitoneum, often around the aorta, ureters, and iliac vessels. Venous or lymphatic compression can cause severe bilateral leg edema.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilateral pitting leg edema extending to the groin
CT appearance consistent with retroperitoneal soft-tissue inflammation/fibrosis
No deep vein thrombosis on Doppler ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly reported urinary obstruction, flank pain, or renal impairment
No other overt organ manifestations of IgG4-related disease, such as pancreatitis or salivary gland enlargement

data.description: A rare inflammatory condition causing fibrotic tissue to form around retroperitoneal structures, particularly the abdominal aorta, iliac vessels, and ureters. Compression of pelvic veins or lymphatic vessels may produce bilateral lower-limb edema.
symptoms_in_common: Normocytic anemia consistent with chronic inflammation
No evidence of deep vein thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised IgG4 level, which favors an IgG4-related cause rather than purely idiopathic disease
No reported ureteric obstruction, hydronephrosis, flank pain, or reduced renal function

data.description: Lymphoma can present as retroperitoneal soft-tissue masses or lymph node enlargement that compress the inferior vena cava, iliac veins, or lymphatic drainage, causing bilateral leg swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral leg edema from possible venous or lymphatic compression
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable lymphadenopathy
No fever, drenching night sweats, or unintentional weight loss reported
Elevated IgG4 is not a typical primary feature of lymphoma
No discrete abdominal mass was palpable

data.diagnosis: Inferior vena cava or bilateral iliac venous obstruction due to retroperitoneal mass effect
data.description: Obstruction or compression of the inferior vena cava or common iliac veins can cause marked, symmetrical lower-limb edema. In this case, retroperitoneal fibrosis or another retroperitoneal process could be the underlying cause.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pitting edema up to the groin
Absence of erythema, warmth, and tenderness
Negative Doppler ultrasound for peripheral deep vein thrombosis
CT evidence of a retroperitoneal process capable of causing venous compression
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported prominent abdominal wall collateral veins
No reported scrotal edema
Anemia, elevated C-reactive protein, and raised IgG4 suggest an underlying inflammatory disorder rather than isolated venous obstruction

data.description: A 19-year-old man with no previous medical problems presented with a six-day history of breathlessness and left-sided chest pain that had started acutely. On examination, his respiratory rate was 22 breaths per minute with oxygen saturations of 95% on room air. The patient had no significant past medical history and no other baseline characteristics were reported.
Air in the pleural space causing partial or complete collapse of a lung, occurring without known underlying lung disease; common in young otherwise healthy men.
symptoms_in_common: Tachypnea with respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute
Chest radiograph appearance of a large left pneumothorax with absent peripheral lung markings and a collapsed left lung

data.diagnosis: Large left pneumothorax without tension physiology
data.description: A substantial collection of pleural air causing lung collapse but without clear clinical or radiographic evidence of hemodynamic compromise or major mediastinal shift.
symptoms_in_common: Relatively preserved oxygen saturation of 95% on room air
Large left-sided pneumothorax on chest radiograph

data.description: A life-threatening pneumothorax in which trapped pleural air increases intrathoracic pressure, potentially causing mediastinal displacement, impaired venous return, hypoxia, and shock.
symptoms_in_common: Large left pneumothorax on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Oxygen saturation is relatively preserved at 95% on room air
No reported hypotension, shock, severe hypoxia, or altered mental status
No clearly reported mediastinal shift or other radiographic signs of tension physiology

data.description: 28-year-old woman with no significant prior medical history presented with fatigue and migratory joint pain. Symptoms began with several days of painful swelling of the right foot and ankle causing difficulty walking, then resolved and were followed by pain in the knees and hips and swelling/pain of the right elbow. She reported intermittent low-grade fevers and, on initial exam, had fever to 38.3°C, diffuse joint tenderness without swelling or erythema, normal joint range of motion, and tachycardia; chest radiograph was normal. Five days later, she returned with progressive dyspnea worse when supine, persistent right knee pain and stiffness, fever 37.5°C, tachycardia, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral crackles, a holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla, and a warm left knee with limited range of motion and severe pain on flexion. She was born in Brazil and recalled childhood exertional dyspnea.

data.diagnosis: Acute rheumatic fever with rheumatic carditis causing mitral regurgitation
data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory complication of prior group A streptococcal streptococcal infection, characterized by migratory polyarthritis and carditis. Rheumatic valvulitis commonly affects the mitral valve and can cause acute mitral regurgitation and heart failure.
symptoms_in_common: Migratory joint pain affecting ankles/feet, knees, hips, and elbow
Painful swelling of the foot and ankle that resolved before other joints became involved
New holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla, consistent with mitral regurgitation
Elevated jugular venous pressure and bilateral crackles, consistent with congestive heart failure from carditis
History of childhood exertional dyspnea and birth in an area where rheumatic heart disease is more prevalent
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe persistent monoarthritis of the left knee with marked limitation of flexion is less typical than the usual rapidly migratory arthritis
No preceding sore throat or documented recent streptococcal pharyngitis was reported

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with mitral valve regurgitation and inflammatory arthritis
data.description: Infection of the endocardial surface of the heart, usually involving a valve, which can cause fever, a new or worsening regurgitant murmur, heart failure, and immune-mediated musculoskeletal manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: New holosystolic murmur compatible with mitral regurgitation
Dyspnea, orthopnea, elevated jugular venous pressure, and crackles suggesting heart failure
Joint pain and possible inflammatory arthritis
symptoms_not_in_common: Classic migratory arthritis beginning in the foot/ankle and moving among large joints is more characteristic of acute rheumatic fever
No reported intravenous drug use, prosthetic valve, known bacteremia, recent invasive procedure, or other clear endocarditis risk factor
No reported peripheral stigmata such as petechiae, splinter hemorrhages, Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, or embolic findings
Young age with childhood exertional dyspnea suggests a possible pre-existing rheumatic valve disorder rather than new infective disease

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with inflammatory arthritis and cardiac involvement
data.description: A systemic autoimmune disease that can cause constitutional symptoms, inflammatory joint pain, serositis, myocarditis, or valvular abnormalities. It occurs most often in young women.
symptoms_in_common: Warm painful knee with restricted movement
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly migratory large-joint arthritis with sequential resolution and recurrence is more typical of acute rheumatic fever
New severe holosystolic murmur with apparent acute mitral regurgitation is not a typical presenting feature of lupus
No rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, alopecia, Raynaud phenomenon, renal symptoms, cytopenias, or serositis were reported
Elevated jugular venous pressure and pulmonary crackles are more directly explained by acute rheumatic valvulitis with mitral regurgitation

data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis that develops after gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection, usually affecting the lower extremities asymmetrically and sometimes accompanied by enthesitis, conjunctivitis, urethritis, or mucocutaneous lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Acute lower-extremity joint involvement including foot/ankle and knee
Painful swollen joint with reduced range of motion
symptoms_not_in_common: Migratory involvement of multiple large joints with resolution in one joint before another develops is more characteristic of acute rheumatic fever
No preceding diarrhea, urethritis, cervicitis, or sexually transmitted infection symptoms were reported
No conjunctivitis, uveitis, enthesitis, dactylitis, oral ulcers, or characteristic skin lesions were reported
Mitral regurgitation murmur and signs of acute congestive heart failure are not typical features of reactive arthritis

data.description: A 56-year-old female patient presented with low-back and hip pain radiating down to her left leg for 12 months. She did not respond to initial management with conservative therapy of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications.

data.diagnosis: Aggressive vertebral hemangioma with epidural extension
data.description: A benign vascular lesion of a vertebral body that can enlarge into the epidural space or posterior elements, causing spinal canal narrowing and nerve-root compression.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating down the left leg consistent with radiculopathy
Poor response to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medication

data.description: A vascular malformation in the epidural space that may compress the thecal sac or lumbar nerve roots and mimic a disc herniation or nerve-sheath tumor.
symptoms_not_in_common: Hip pain is less specifically characteristic, although it may occur as referred radicular pain

data.description: A fluid-filled degenerative cyst arising from a lumbar facet joint, often causing lateral recess or foraminal nerve-root compression and sciatica.
symptoms_not_in_common: A 12-month progressive course is possible but is not specific

data.description: Displacement of lumbar disc material that compresses a nerve root, producing low-back pain and sciatica, commonly affecting one leg.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating into the left leg
Hip-region pain that may represent referred radicular pain
Limited or absent response to NSAIDs
symptoms_not_in_common: A slowly progressive 12-month course without improvement is less typical of an uncomplicated acute disc herniation

data.diagnosis: Lumbar spinal stenosis due to degenerative disease
data.description: Narrowing of the central spinal canal, lateral recesses, or neural foramina from degenerative disc, facet, and ligament changes, leading to nerve-root compression.
symptoms_in_common: Age in the typical degenerative range
Chronic symptoms and incomplete response to NSAIDs
symptoms_not_in_common: Only unilateral left-leg symptoms are described; lumbar stenosis often causes bilateral symptoms or neurogenic claudication

data.description: A 57-year-old male patient presented with a three-month history of fatigue, recurrent sore throats, and a persistent 'cold sore.' The patient had no relevant medical history, drank little alcohol, and was a non-smoker.
A hematologic malignancy causing bone-marrow failure, often leading to fatigue from anemia and recurrent infections from neutropenia; persistent oral or perioral infections may occur.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent crusted lip ulcer or 'cold sore'
Possible cervical lymph node enlargement shown in the image
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported bruising or bleeding
No reported fever
No reported weight loss
No relevant prior medical history

data.description: HIV progressively impairs immune function and can cause persistent or recurrent herpes simplex infection, recurrent throat infections, fatigue, and lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent lesion clinically resembling herpes labialis
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever or night sweats
No reported weight loss
No reported generalized lymph node enlargement
No reported oral thrush, diarrhea, or recurrent opportunistic infections

data.description: A chronic B-cell leukemia that may cause fatigue, painless lymphadenopathy, and increased susceptibility to recurrent bacterial or viral infections because of impaired immune function.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported widespread painless lymphadenopathy
No reported splenomegaly or abdominal fullness
No reported weight loss or drenching night sweats
Persistent lip ulcer is not a classic primary feature

data.description: A group of lymphoid cancers that can present with cervical lymph node enlargement, constitutional symptoms, and immune dysfunction causing recurrent infections.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent lip lesion that could occur with immune suppression
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported progressive generalized lymphadenopathy
No reported fever, night sweats, or weight loss
A persistent cold-sore-like lesion is not typical as the main presenting feature
No reported pruritus or abdominal symptoms

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lip/oral cavity
data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor that may present as a persistent nonhealing ulcer or crusted lesion of the lip and can spread to cervical lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent nonhealing crusted ulcer at the lip commissure
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent sore throats are not a typical main feature
Fatigue alone is nonspecific
The patient is a non-smoker and drinks little alcohol, reducing but not eliminating risk
The lesion resembles a cold sore, whereas cancer often presents as a more indurated persistent ulcer

diagnoses.name: Perioral lesion with plasma cell rich infiltrate
diagnoses.title: Plasma cell neoplasms

data.description: 28-year-old male patient admitted on November 27, 2013, complaining of diarrhea (loose stool, three to five times per day) for over 10 years and hematochezia for about 1 month. Had been diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia 5 months after birth, with hemoglobin level remaining 70-80 g/L (normal range 110-150 g/L) for most of the time. On admission, albumin level was 26 g/L (normal range 35-52 g/L). Liver and renal function were otherwise normal. Patient reported recurrent arthralgia in the knee and ankle joints.

data.diagnosis: Chronic enteropathy associated with SLCO2A1 (CEAS), also called cryptogenic multifocal ulcerous stenosing enteritis
data.description: A rare inherited small-intestinal disorder characterized by chronic superficial ulcers, multiple intestinal strictures, protein loss, gastrointestinal bleeding, and severe iron-deficiency anemia, often beginning in childhood.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chronic iron-deficiency anemia beginning in infancy
Small-bowel ulceration and stenotic/stricturing lesions on imaging and endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: No major symptoms are clearly atypical; hematochezia may be less prominent than occult bleeding in some cases

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract and may cause diarrhea, intestinal ulceration, strictures, bleeding, malnutrition, anemia, and joint manifestations.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe anemia diagnosed in infancy is unusual for typical Crohn disease
More than 10 years of relatively stable diarrhea without reported abdominal pain is less typical
No reported weight loss, fever, perianal disease, fistula, or abdominal pain

data.description: A systemic inflammatory vasculitic disorder that can produce deep intestinal ulceration, gastrointestinal bleeding, abdominal symptoms, anemia, and inflammatory arthritis; it is usually associated with recurrent oral or genital ulcers.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent oral aphthous ulcers reported
No genital ulcers reported
No eye inflammation or skin lesions reported
Very early onset iron-deficiency anemia in infancy is not typical
Chronic diarrhea for over 10 years is less characteristic than episodic abdominal pain and ulcer-related bleeding

data.description: Tuberculosis involving the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly the ileocecal region, which can cause chronic diarrhea, ulceration, strictures, intestinal obstruction, bleeding, anemia, and low albumin.
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia beginning at 5 months of age is highly atypical
A disease course lasting more than 10 years without reported fever, night sweats, weight loss, or tuberculosis exposure is less typical
Recurrent knee and ankle arthralgia is not a typical dominant feature
No pulmonary or systemic tuberculosis findings reported

data.diagnosis: NSAID-induced enteropathy with diaphragm-like small-bowel strictures
data.description: Chronic use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can cause small-bowel erosions, ulcers, occult or overt bleeding, iron-deficiency anemia, protein loss, and multiple short strictures known as diaphragm disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of long-term NSAID exposure is provided
Anemia beginning in infancy strongly argues against NSAID-induced disease
Recurrent arthralgia may lead to NSAID use but does not itself establish NSAID enteropathy
The long childhood-onset course is atypical

data.description: A 65-year-old male retired farmer presented with an inability to fully straighten the ring finger and little finger of his right hand, which had progressed over the past two years. He had recently noticed a 'rope like' swelling in his palm with no history of trauma. His medical history was unremarkable except for smoking cessation 10 years earlier with a 90 pack-year history. His father had a similar deformity. On examination, he had palpable cords to his middle, ring, and little fingers with palpable nodules on the volar aspect of all proximal phalanges, causing flexion contractures of the proximal interphalangeal joints. The cord and nodules in the ring finger were adherent to the overlying skin.
A benign fibroproliferative disorder of the palmar fascia causing nodules and fibrous cords that progressively pull the fingers into flexion, most commonly affecting the ring and little fingers.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive inability to fully straighten the ring and little fingers
Palpable palmar cords extending to the middle, ring, and little fingers
Palpable volar nodules over the proximal phalanges
Flexion contractures of the proximal interphalangeal joints
Cord and nodules adherent to overlying skin
Positive family history in his father
symptoms_not_in_common: No major atypical symptoms are described

data.description: Inflammation and thickening around the flexor tendon and A1 pulley that can cause painful catching, locking, or inability to extend an affected finger.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable palmar thickening or nodule may occur near the base of a finger
symptoms_not_in_common: Gradual formation of rope-like cords across the palm
Multiple palpable cords extending to several fingers
Fixed proximal interphalangeal joint flexion contractures
Nodules along the volar proximal phalanges rather than mainly at the A1 pulley
Skin adherence of the cord and nodules
No reported painful clicking, catching, or locking during finger motion
Family history of a similar deformity

data.description: A condition characterized by flexion contracture of the proximal interphalangeal joint, usually affecting the little finger and often beginning in childhood or adolescence.
symptoms_in_common: Flexion contractures of proximal interphalangeal joints
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset at age 63 years
Progressive rope-like palmar swelling
Palpable palmar cords
Palmar and volar proximal phalanx nodules
Skin adherence of the ring-finger cord and nodules
Prominent ring finger involvement with palmar fascial changes

data.diagnosis: Flexor tendon contracture due to prior trauma or scarring
data.description: Scarring of the flexor tendons, tendon sheath, or surrounding soft tissues can restrict tendon glide and result in finger flexion contractures.
symptoms_in_common: Flexion contractures involving multiple finger joints
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of trauma, hand surgery, infection, or laceration
Rope-like palmar cords
Palpable fascial nodules
Skin adherence over the ring-finger lesion
Family history of a similar deformity
Typical ring and little finger distribution of Dupuytren disease

data.description: 57-year-old man with HIV infection for 8 years and a 10-year history of bilateral inguinal hernias, left larger than right, previously intermittently reducible. Over 3 months he developed increasing pain with the hernia, and over the 3 weeks before presentation had worsening left inguinal pain and enlargement, intermittent subjective fevers, night sweats, and hard, tender lumps near the hernia. He also had a fever to 38.1°C the night before presentation. Past history included Kaposi sarcoma, molluscum contagiosum, anal dysplasia, pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex infection, pneumocystis pneumonia, thrush, preseptal cellulitis, and cryptosporidium-related diarrhea. On examination, he was afebrile with stable vital signs and had easily reducible bilateral inguinal hernias with bulky, slightly tender left inguinal lymphadenopathy, including three nodes up to 3 cm.

data.diagnosis: Syphilitic lymphadenitis due to Treponema pallidum
data.description: Lymph-node involvement by syphilis, often producing prominent regional or generalized lymphadenopathy with follicular hyperplasia and plasmacytosis. Inguinal nodes are commonly involved, particularly with genital or anorectal infection; fever and other systemic symptoms may occur in secondary syphilis. The histologic appearance and spirochete staining are supportive.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection, which increases risk for sexually transmitted infections and can alter presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Long-standing bilateral reducible inguinal hernias
Progressive hernia-related pain over 3 months
Marked enlargement of a pre-existing hernia

data.description: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, is more common in people with advanced HIV and may present with rapidly enlarging lymph nodes and constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarged inguinal lymph nodes up to 3 cm
symptoms_not_in_common: Tender lymph nodes, as lymphoma nodes are often painless
Easily reducible bilateral inguinal hernias
Pain clearly associated with a chronic hernia

data.description: A lymphoproliferative disorder associated with HHV-8 and HIV that causes systemic inflammatory symptoms and generalized or regional lymphadenopathy. It can coexist with Kaposi sarcoma.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparently localized predominant left inguinal node involvement rather than clearly multicentric lymphadenopathy
Tender nodes, which are not a defining feature
Long-standing reducible bilateral inguinal hernias

data.description: Reactive or suppurative inflammation of inguinal lymph nodes caused by infection draining from the lower extremities, genital region, perineum, or anorectal area. In people with HIV, atypical and opportunistic bacterial infections are also possible.
symptoms_not_in_common: Night sweats over a prolonged period
No reported skin, genital, perineal, or lower-extremity infectious source
Long-standing bilateral reducible inguinal hernias

data.description: A complication of an inguinal hernia in which herniated bowel or tissue becomes trapped, potentially causing ischemia, obstruction, severe pain, and systemic illness.
symptoms_in_common: Increasing pain in the left groin
Perceived enlargement of the left hernia
symptoms_not_in_common: Hernias were easily reducible on examination
Bulky discrete inguinal lymphadenopathy is not typical of uncomplicated incarceration or strangulation
Night sweats
No reported vomiting, abdominal distension, bowel obstruction, or peritoneal signs

diagnoses.name: Necrotizing lymphadenitis
diagnoses.title: Histiocytic necrotising lymphadenitis of Kikuchi and Fujimoto

data.description: A 16-year-old girl presented with acute left shoulder pain, left-sided chest pain, and shortness of breath. She had a 4-month history of intermittent left shoulder and left-sided chest pain following a dance recital, which had been treated with analgesia and physiotherapy. She denied fever, cough, orthopnea, weight loss, and appetite change. Physical examination revealed tenderness at the location of the left fifth rib and reduced left chest expansion.

data.diagnosis: Ewing sarcoma of the rib / Askin tumor
data.description: A malignant small-round-cell tumor arising from bone or the chest wall, most often affecting children and adolescents. Rib involvement may cause pleural effusion, chest-wall pain, dyspnea, and referred shoulder pain.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent localized left chest and shoulder pain
Tenderness over the left fifth rib
Acute worsening with shortness of breath
Reduced expansion of the left chest
Pleural fluid or pleural-based abnormality on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No weight loss
No appetite change

data.diagnosis: Primary chest-wall Ewing sarcoma (peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor)
data.description: A subtype of the Ewing sarcoma family arising in the soft tissues of the thoracopulmonary region, historically called an Askin tumor. It commonly presents with chest-wall pain, a pleural mass or effusion, and respiratory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Shoulder pain referred from the chest wall
Reduced chest expansion on the affected side
Imaging compatible with a left pleural/chest-wall process
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough
No fever
No constitutional symptoms such as weight loss

data.diagnosis: Osteomyelitis of the rib with parapneumonic pleural effusion or empyema
data.description: Infection of a rib can cause focal bony pain and tenderness and may extend into adjacent pleura, producing pleural fluid and breathing difficulty.
symptoms_in_common: Focal tenderness at the fifth rib
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No cough
No reported systemic illness
Four-month intermittent course without infectious symptoms

data.diagnosis: Stress fracture or pathological fracture of the fifth rib
data.description: A rib stress fracture may occur after repetitive physical activity, including dancing, and causes focal pain and tenderness. A pathological fracture can occur when an underlying bone lesion weakens the rib.
symptoms_in_common: Pain beginning after a dance recital
Intermittent chest and shoulder pain over several months
Reduced chest expansion due to pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute shortness of breath is less typical unless there is associated pleural complication
Pleural effusion or chest-wall mass on imaging is not typical for an uncomplicated stress fracture

data.diagnosis: Langerhans cell histiocytosis of the rib (eosinophilic granuloma)
data.description: A focal lytic bone lesion caused by proliferation of Langerhans cells, often affecting children and adolescents. It can involve ribs and produce persistent localized pain, tenderness, and occasionally a pathological fracture or pleural reaction.
symptoms_in_common: Tenderness over the affected fifth rib
Possible preceding minor trauma or activity drawing attention to the lesion
Potential chest discomfort and restricted chest expansion
symptoms_not_in_common: Shortness of breath is not a usual early feature
Large pleural effusion would be uncommon
Shoulder pain is less characteristic

diagnoses.name: Rib osteosarcoma
diagnoses.title: Osteosarcoma of bone or articular cartilage of ribs, sternum or clavicle

data.description: A 66-year-old man presented with a 4 to 5-month history of fever, chills, drenching night sweats, and unintentional 35-kg weight loss. He had previously undergone work-up for fever of unknown origin including evaluation for infectious causes such as tuberculosis, typhoid, and brucellosis, but these were not revealing. On physical examination, his spleen was palpable but no adenopathy was detected. Blood tests revealed anemia with hemoglobin of 9.0 g/dL (normal 13.0-18.0 g/dL), microcytosis with mean corpuscular volume of 75 fl (normal 80.0-94.0 fl), normal platelet count of 354,000/μL, and elevated international normalized ratio of 1.30 (normal 0.85-1.20). His serum ferritin level was significantly elevated at 1,796.0 ng/mL (normal 25-310 ng/mL).

A rare form of classical Hodgkin lymphoma initially confined to or predominantly involving the spleen, often producing constitutional symptoms and splenomegaly. The cytology images are suggestive of Reed-Sternberg-type cells with CD30-positive staining.
symptoms_in_common: No peripheral adenopathy can occur in primary splenic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic anemia is not the most typical anemia pattern
Normal platelet count despite splenomegaly is less characteristic in advanced splenic involvement
Mildly elevated INR is not a typical defining feature

data.diagnosis: Primary splenic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma that may present as an isolated splenic mass or diffuse splenic enlargement with systemic inflammatory symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of palpable lymphadenopathy may occur with primary splenic lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: The illustrated Reed-Sternberg-like morphology and CD30-pattern staining would be less typical than for classical Hodgkin lymphoma
Microcytosis is not specifically characteristic
Normal platelet count is less expected if there is substantial hypersplenism

data.description: A severe hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by excessive immune activation, often triggered by lymphoma or infection; it commonly causes fever, splenomegaly, cytopenias, and very high ferritin levels.
symptoms_not_in_common: Only one cytopenia is reported; HLH commonly causes bicytopenia or pancytopenia
Platelet count is normal rather than low
Ferritin is elevated but not extremely high compared with many HLH cases
Night sweats and a focal splenic mass are more suggestive of lymphoma itself

data.description: A systemic protozoal infection that can cause prolonged fever, weight loss, massive splenomegaly, anemia, and hyperferritinemia, particularly in endemic regions.
symptoms_not_in_common: No pancytopenia is reported
Platelet count is normal
A discrete splenic mass is less typical than diffuse splenic enlargement
The cytology images are more suggestive of malignant large cells than intracellular Leishmania organisms

data.description: Extrapulmonary tuberculosis involving the spleen can present with prolonged fever of unknown origin, weight loss, night sweats, anemia, splenomegaly, and splenic lesions.
symptoms_not_in_common: Tuberculosis testing and evaluation were reportedly unrevealing
No pulmonary symptoms or known tuberculosis exposure are described
The cytology images do not show typical granulomatous inflammation or acid-fast bacilli
Marked ferritin elevation is nonspecific and not a defining finding of splenic tuberculosis

diagnoses.name: Splenic involvement
diagnoses.title: Fibrosis of spleen[Schistosomiasis involving the skin]

data.description: 52-year-old man with hypertension, benign prostatic hypertrophy with obstructive nephropathy, chronic renal insufficiency requiring dialysis until a living-related renal transplant 1 year prior, and hyperparathyroidism with bilateral cataract surgery presented with acute palpitations and chest pressure. Two days earlier, he developed epigastric burning, fatigue, weakness, and vomiting, partially relieved by antacids. He denied fever, chills, or other localizing symptoms. On arrival, heart rate was 200 bpm with atrial fibrillation and rapid ventricular response; after cardioversion, pulse was 53 bpm and blood pressure 128/90 mmHg. Exam showed a diffuse, laterally displaced apical impulse, prominent S2, and an S4, without murmurs or JVD. Labs showed creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, troponin T 1.04 ng/mL, normal electrolytes and thyroid function, mild proteinuria, and markedly reduced leukocyte α-galactosidase activity.

data.diagnosis: Fabry disease (Anderson-Fabry disease) with cardiac involvement
data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A activity, resulting in globotriaosylceramide accumulation in the kidneys, heart, nervous system, skin, and eyes. Cardiac involvement commonly causes concentric left-ventricular hypertrophy, conduction abnormalities, atrial arrhythmias, and myocardial injury.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal insufficiency progressing to dialysis and renal transplantation
Left-ventricular hypertrophy suggested by diffuse displaced apical impulse, prominent S2, S4, ECG voltage, and echocardiographic appearance
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and palpitations
Chest pressure with elevated troponin, consistent with Fabry-related myocardial injury or microvascular ischemia
Epigastric burning, vomiting, fatigue, and weakness, which may reflect gastrointestinal involvement
History of cataract surgery, compatible with ocular manifestations of Fabry disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Obstructive nephropathy attributed to benign prostatic hypertrophy
Hypertension, which may coexist but is not a defining Fabry manifestation

data.diagnosis: Hypertensive heart disease with left-ventricular hypertrophy
data.description: Long-standing hypertension can cause pressure-overload left-ventricular hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, left-atrial enlargement, atrial fibrillation, and demand-related myocardial injury.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent S2 and S4, which can occur with left-ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Elevated troponin, potentially from tachyarrhythmia-related demand ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Severe renal disease requiring dialysis and transplant at a relatively young age
Proteinuria suggestive of a systemic renal disorder
Cataract history potentially associated with lysosomal storage disease
Epigastric burning, vomiting, and fatigue as systemic manifestations

data.description: A genetic myocardial disorder characterized by otherwise unexplained ventricular hypertrophy, impaired diastolic filling, arrhythmias, chest discomfort, and possible elevated cardiac biomarkers.
symptoms_in_common: Clinical and ECG/echocardiographic evidence suggestive of left-ventricular hypertrophy
Elevated troponin, which can occur with myocardial stress or microvascular ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity
Chronic proteinuric renal failure requiring dialysis and transplantation
History of obstructive nephropathy
Gastrointestinal symptoms such as epigastric burning and vomiting are not typical primary manifestations
Cataract surgery is not a typical feature

data.description: Male infant, 22 hours old, admitted for repeated right-sided limb clonic seizures for 16 hours. Born at 40+6 weeks by cesarean section after fetal heart monitoring showed frequent variable decelerations 1 hour before delivery; amniotic fluid was reduced and grade I turbid, with no premature rupture of membranes. Apgar scores were 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes, and birth weight was 3380 g. Seizures began 6 hours after birth, occurred 4 times, were not associated with loss of consciousness or cyanosis, and resolved spontaneously. On admission, the infant was alert and responsive, with normal skin color, flat anterior fontanelle, equal pupils with normal light reflexes, coarse breath sounds without rales, normal heart sounds without murmurs, soft abdomen without masses, normal limb activity and muscle tone, and normal primitive reflexes.

data.diagnosis: Neonatal arterial ischemic stroke (left middle cerebral artery territory infarction)
data.description: An acute focal cerebral infarction caused by interruption of arterial blood flow, often involving the middle cerebral artery in term newborns. It commonly presents in the first days of life with focal clonic seizures. The diffusion-restricted left cerebral lesion on MRI is consistent with acute ischemic infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Seizure onset within the first 24 hours of life
Repeated focal right-sided limb clonic seizures
Term infant with otherwise relatively normal initial neurologic examination
Imaging showing a focal acute ischemic-appearing cerebral lesion, likely in the left cerebral hemisphere, corresponding to right-sided seizures
Possible intrapartum fetal distress with variable decelerations and reduced amniotic fluid
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal limb activity and muscle tone on admission; some infants later develop contralateral weakness, although this may be absent initially
No persistent focal neurologic deficit documented at 22 hours of life

data.description: Brain injury caused by impaired oxygen delivery and/or cerebral perfusion around the time of birth. Neonatal seizures can occur during the first day of life, but HIE more often produces diffuse neurologic abnormalities and bilateral or widespread MRI injury rather than a single arterial-territory lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal seizures beginning shortly after birth
Reduced amniotic fluid and turbid amniotic fluid, which may accompany fetal stress
Acute diffusion abnormalities on brain MRI can occur with hypoxic-ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Apgar scores of 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
No need for reported resuscitation
Alert and responsive mental status
Normal muscle tone, primitive reflexes, and limb activity
No respiratory depression or cyanosis
Focal unilateral right-sided clonic seizures rather than more generalized or multifocal seizures
Focal unilateral imaging lesion rather than a typical diffuse or bilateral hypoxic-ischemic pattern

data.diagnosis: Neonatal intracranial hemorrhage, including hemorrhagic stroke
data.description: Bleeding into brain tissue, ventricles, or surrounding spaces can cause neonatal seizures. In term infants, focal parenchymal hemorrhage or hemorrhagic transformation of an infarct may present with seizures, although MRI characteristics would need to demonstrate blood products to confirm this.
symptoms_in_common: Focal right-sided clonic movements can occur with a left hemispheric hemorrhagic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No depressed consciousness, lethargy, apnea, or cyanosis
Flat anterior fontanelle without signs of raised intracranial pressure
No anemia, pallor, shock, or hemodynamic instability reported
No reported traumatic delivery or instrument-assisted vaginal delivery
MRI description appears more suggestive of focal diffusion-restricted ischemia than primary hemorrhage

data.description: 19-year-old woman with 3 weeks of right shoulder and right flank pain, followed 2 weeks later by exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough that progressively worsened over 8 days, progressing to severe dyspnea with walking and need for a wheelchair. On presentation she was ill-appearing with increased work of breathing, tachycardia, tachypnea >40/min, hypoxemia (88% on room air), and a cardiac murmur. She had intermittent back pain for 6 months, visible chest pulsations and labored breathing during sleep for 2 weeks, and two episodes of diarrhea during the cruise. History included asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection 2 months earlier, dental cleaning 5 weeks earlier, anxiety, and anemia; she took iron supplements. Labs showed anemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, low albumin, elevated ESR and CRP, and arterial blood gas with alkalemia and low CO2 on supplemental oxygen.

data.diagnosis: Native aortic valve infective endocarditis with severe aortic regurgitation and acute heart failure
data.description: Infection of the aortic valve, often bacterial, causing valve destruction or vegetation, severe aortic regurgitation, systemic inflammation, and decompensated heart failure. Dental manipulation can precede bacteremia and endocarditis.
symptoms_in_common: Shoulder, flank, and back pain that may reflect embolic complications
symptoms_not_in_common: Two isolated episodes of diarrhea during a cruise
History of asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection

data.description: Endocarditis in which routine blood cultures may be negative, often due to prior antibiotics or difficult-to-culture organisms such as Bartonella, Coxiella burnetii, fungi, or HACEK organisms. It can still cause severe valvular regurgitation, emboli, and heart failure.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammatory laboratory abnormalities including leukocytosis and elevated ESR and CRP
Shoulder, flank, and back pain potentially caused by embolic infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported persistent fever or chills
Two brief episodes of diarrhea
Anxiety history

data.diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure due to severe aortic regurgitation
data.description: Failure of the heart to maintain adequate circulation because of major leakage through the aortic valve. Severe acute or subacute aortic regurgitation can produce pulmonary congestion, hypoxemia, tachycardia, and rapidly progressive exercise intolerance.
symptoms_in_common: Dyspnea severe enough to require a wheelchair
symptoms_not_in_common: Leukocytosis
Markedly elevated ESR and CRP
Thrombocytosis
Shoulder and flank pain
Recent dental cleaning

data.diagnosis: Septic systemic embolization from infective endocarditis
data.description: Fragments of infected valve vegetation can embolize to systemic organs, causing painful infarcts or abscesses in the kidneys, spleen, spine, brain, or peripheral arteries. This is a complication of left-sided infective endocarditis.
symptoms_in_common: Right flank pain, which may indicate renal embolism or renal infarction
Right shoulder pain, which can occur as referred pain from splenic or diaphragmatic involvement
Intermittent back pain, which may reflect vertebral osteomyelitis or embolic complications
Cardiac murmur suggestive of a valvular source
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive severe dyspnea is not explained by systemic embolization alone
Hypoxemia is not typical unless heart failure or pulmonary involvement is also present
Two episodes of diarrhea

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus, usually from venous thrombosis, causing acute or subacute dyspnea, tachycardia, hypoxemia, and respiratory alkalosis. It is an important alternative cause of severe dyspnea in a young traveler, although it does not fully explain the murmur and inflammatory syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Respiratory alkalosis with low carbon dioxide
symptoms_not_in_common: Cardiac murmur
Visible chest pulsations
Six months of intermittent back pain
Marked inflammatory marker elevation
Leukocytosis with thrombocytosis
Recent dental cleaning as a relevant trigger
Right shoulder and flank pain occurring weeks before respiratory symptoms

data.description: 56-year-old man with 7 days of worsening epigastric pain with nausea and belching. Past history included splenectomy after trauma, hyperlipidaemia, obesity, and Bell’s palsy. He had started orlistat about 10 days before symptom onset. On examination, he was haemodynamically stable and afebrile to low-grade fever (37.5°C), with soft abdomen but epigastric and left iliac fossa tenderness; rectal examination was negative. Labs showed mild neutrophilia and elevated CRP, with normal liver, renal, amylase, and lipase results. His pain persisted and inflammatory markers worsened despite analgesia and high-dose proton pump inhibitor therapy.

data.diagnosis: Superior mesenteric vein thrombosis with portal venous thrombosis
data.description: Occlusion of the superior mesenteric and/or portal venous system can cause mesenteric venous congestion, bowel-wall edema, abdominal pain, and inflammatory-marker elevation; it may progress to intestinal ischemia if untreated.
symptoms_in_common: Worsening abdominal pain, particularly epigastric pain
Persistent pain despite proton pump inhibitor treatment
History of splenectomy, which can be associated with thrombotic risk
symptoms_not_in_common: Belching
Left iliac fossa tenderness
Soft abdomen without peritonism
Normal amylase and lipase

data.description: Mesenteric panniculitis is an inflammatory disorder of mesenteric fat that causes abdominal pain and CT findings of increased mesenteric fat density, sometimes with a pseudocapsule or small mesenteric nodes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent belching
Left iliac fossa tenderness
Recent orlistat initiation
History of splenectomy as a thrombosis-related risk factor

data.description: Acute pancreatic inflammation usually presents with acute epigastric pain, nausea, and elevated serum lipase or amylase; severe cases can produce systemic inflammation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal amylase
Normal lipase
Left iliac fossa tenderness
Belching as a prominent symptom
Persistent symptoms without typical biochemical evidence of pancreatitis

data.description: A 12-year-old female presented to the Emergency Department with a 48-hour history of abdominal pain localised in the hypogastrium, which had progressively worsened in the last few hours. The patient mentioned previous episodes of less intense abdominal pain. Considering the clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, an abdominal ultrasound was requested.

Accumulation of retained menstrual blood in the vagina and uterus caused by congenital obstruction at the hymen. It commonly presents around puberty with pelvic pain and a midline pelvic fluid-filled mass containing internal echoes.
symptoms_in_common: Previous episodes of less intense abdominal pain, compatible with recurrent cyclic pain
Ultrasound appearance of a large midline fluid-filled pelvic structure with internal echogenic material, compatible with blood products
symptoms_not_in_common: No report of primary amenorrhea
No report of cyclic timing of pain
No report of a bulging bluish hymenal membrane or vaginal mass
No urinary retention or constipation reported

data.diagnosis: Hematometrocolpos due to a transverse vaginal septum
data.description: A congenital transverse vaginal septum can obstruct menstrual outflow, producing retained blood within the vagina and uterus (hematometrocolpos) and causing recurrent pelvic pain after menarche.
symptoms_in_common: Pain that has recurred previously and recently worsened
Pelvic ultrasound showing a distended fluid-containing genital tract structure with internal echoes suggestive of retained blood
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported primary amenorrhea
No reported cyclic association with menses
No reported difficulty with vaginal examination or abnormal vaginal anatomy
No urinary or bowel compression symptoms reported

data.diagnosis: Obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA syndrome)
data.description: A Müllerian anomaly, typically uterus didelphys with an obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal agenesis, that may cause hematocolpos or hematometrocolpos and recurrent pelvic pain after menarche.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent pelvic/hypogastric pain with acute worsening
Possible ultrasound evidence of retained hemorrhagic fluid in the genital tract
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported duplicated uterus or separate uterine cavities
No reported unilateral pelvic collection
No reported renal agenesis or other urinary tract anomaly
No report of menstrual irregularity or persistent postmenstrual pain

data.description: Inflammation of the appendix, usually causing progressive abdominal pain that often migrates to the right lower quadrant and may be associated with fever, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia.
symptoms_in_common: Presentation prompted clinical concern for appendicitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is localized to the hypogastrium rather than the typical right lower quadrant
Previous recurrent episodes of similar pain are less typical
No fever reported
No nausea, vomiting, anorexia, or bowel symptoms reported
Pelvic cystic/fluid-filled ultrasound appearance is not typical of uncomplicated appendicitis

data.diagnosis: Ovarian torsion associated with an ovarian cyst
data.description: Twisting of the ovary around its vascular pedicle, often in the presence of an ovarian cyst or enlarged ovary. It produces acute pelvic pain and requires urgent evaluation.
symptoms_in_common: Possible pelvic mass or fluid-containing structure on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain developed over 48 hours with prior recurrent episodes rather than classically abrupt severe unilateral pain
No nausea or vomiting reported
Pain is described as midline hypogastric rather than unilateral
The ultrasound appearance is more suggestive of a midline distended genital tract than an adnexal mass

data.description: 8-year-old Korean boy with severe global developmental delay, hypotonia, microcephaly, ptosis, and nystagmus. Developmental delay was first noted at 3 months due to poor eye contact and head control. He had marked growth retardation and severe intellectual disability (FSIQ <30 at age 5). Physical findings included sparse eyebrows, prominent nasal bridge, hypoplastic nare, down-turned mouth, high-arched palate, and inability to sit or walk independently. Multiple exostoses were first noted at age 6 as protrusions of the right wrist and knee. Karyotype was normal (46,XY).

A contiguous-gene deletion syndrome caused by deletions of chromosome 11p11.2, commonly involving EXT2, ALX4, and PHF21A. It is characterized by multiple osteochondromas/exostoses, enlarged parietal foramina, developmental delay/intellectual disability, hypotonia, craniofacial differences, and growth impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Inability to sit or walk independently
Multiple exostoses involving the wrist and knee
Skull imaging suggestive of enlarged parietal foramina
Normal conventional karyotype despite a pathogenic submicroscopic deletion
symptoms_not_in_common: No major atypical symptoms reported

data.diagnosis: Hereditary multiple exostoses (multiple osteochondromas), especially EXT2-related
data.description: An autosomal dominant skeletal disorder caused mainly by pathogenic variants in EXT1 or EXT2, producing multiple cartilage-capped bony outgrowths near the metaphyses of long bones. EXT2 loss is also a major feature of Potocki-Shaffer syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic bony protrusions compatible with osteochondromas
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe global developmental delay
Severe intellectual disability
Hypotonia
Microcephaly
Ptosis
Nystagmus
Marked growth retardation
Characteristic craniofacial differences
High-arched palate
Inability to sit or walk independently
Parietal skull defects/enlarged parietal foramina

data.description: A chromosomal microdeletion disorder of 11p11.2. Deletion of PHF21A contributes to neurodevelopmental impairment and craniofacial features, ALX4 deletion is associated with enlarged parietal foramina, and EXT2 deletion causes multiple exostoses; this combination is generally termed Potocki-Shaffer syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Severe developmental delay beginning in infancy
Poor eye contact and poor head control
Normal 46,XY karyotype, consistent with a microdeletion not detectable by standard karyotyping
symptoms_not_in_common: No major atypical symptoms reported

data.description: 15-year-old boy with congenital neutropenia due to an ELA2 gene mutation and refractory anemia with excess blasts 2, with a history of chronic low absolute neutrophil counts (200–1,000/μL) and recurrent bacterial skin and lung infections since infancy requiring granulocyte colony-stimulating factor and antimicrobials. He was referred for bone marrow transplantation. On examination, he had multiple nonpruritic skin ulcerations on the right abdomen, scalp, and left ankle, present for several weeks. Laboratory studies while on granulocyte colony-stimulating factor showed normal absolute neutrophil, lymphocyte, and eosinophil counts, elevated IgG, and normal IgE.

A severe, highly contagious Sarcoptes scabiei infestation with a large mite burden, typically occurring in immunocompromised patients. It may present atypically with little or no itching and can cause widespread crusted, erosive, or ulcerated lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple persistent skin lesions on the scalp, abdomen, and ankle
Nonpruritic presentation, which can occur in immunocompromised patients with crusted scabies
Immunocompromised state from congenital neutropenia, refractory anemia with excess blasts, and chronic treatment
Skin biopsy demonstrating a mite within the stratum corneum
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are described primarily as ulcerations rather than thick diffuse hyperkeratotic crusts
No generalized scaling or extensive crusting is specifically reported
Normal eosinophil count and normal IgE level

data.description: A superficial infestation of the skin by Sarcoptes scabiei mites, usually causing intensely pruritic papules, burrows, and excoriations, often involving the hands, wrists, axillae, waist, and genital region.
symptoms_in_common: Cutaneous lesions present for several weeks
Mite identified in the superficial epidermis/stratum corneum on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of pruritus
Ulcerative and erosive morphology rather than typical papules and burrows
Scalp involvement, which is uncommon in immunocompetent adolescents with classic scabies
No reported involvement of finger webs, wrists, genital area, or other typical sites
Severe underlying immunocompromise favors crusted rather than classic scabies

data.description: A necrotic ulcerative skin infection classically associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia in neutropenic or otherwise immunocompromised patients. Lesions may evolve into painful necrotic ulcers with dark eschars.
symptoms_in_common: Immunocompromised state related to marrow disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Absolute neutrophil count was normal while receiving granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
No fever, sepsis, bacteremia, or systemic toxicity is reported
Lesions had been present for several weeks rather than rapidly progressing
No characteristic hemorrhagic bullae, necrotic eschars, or black central necrosis is described
Skin biopsy identifies a mite, supporting scabies rather than bacterial vasculitic infection

data.description: 16-year-old male with a 4-week history of weakness, malaise, anorexia, nausea, fever, and vomiting. No history of rash, joint pains, oral ulcers, or herbal medicine use. Exam showed pallor, bilateral pitting pedal edema, and hypertension (160/90 mmHg); otherwise unremarkable. Labs revealed anemia (Hb 9.0 g/dL), hematuria with RBC casts, proteinuria (3+; 24-hour urine protein 2.4 g), and rapidly worsening renal dysfunction (urea 130 mg/dL, creatinine 3 mg/dL rising to 10 mg/dL in 7 days). ANA, ANCA, HBsAg, anti-HCV, and HIV were negative; complement levels were normal. Ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys, and chest/abdominal CT and fundus examination were normal.

A rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis caused by necrotizing and crescent-forming inflammation of glomeruli, often with little or no immune-complex deposition. It may occur despite negative ANCA testing and can be limited to the kidneys.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly worsening renal function over days
Hematuria with red blood cell casts
Malaise, weakness, fever, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting
symptoms_not_in_common: No systemic vasculitic features such as rash, joint pains, respiratory symptoms, or neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (anti-GBM disease, renal-limited form)
data.description: An autoimmune disorder in which antibodies target the glomerular basement membrane, producing severe crescentic glomerulonephritis. Some patients have kidney-only disease without pulmonary hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria with red blood cell casts
Constitutional symptoms including weakness, malaise, fever, nausea, and vomiting
symptoms_not_in_common: No hemoptysis, cough, dyspnea, or radiologic evidence of pulmonary hemorrhage
Anti-GBM antibody result is not provided

data.description: A severe form of glomerulonephritis in which immune-complex deposition causes glomerular inflammation and crescents, leading to rapidly progressive kidney failure. It may occur with lupus, infection-related glomerulonephritis, IgA nephropathy, or other immune disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria with red blood cell casts
Systemic symptoms including fever, malaise, anorexia, nausea, and vomiting
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal complement levels, which are less typical for many immune-complex disorders
Negative ANA and absence of rash, arthritis, or oral ulcers make lupus nephritis less likely
No preceding infection history is reported

data.diagnosis: IgA nephropathy with rapidly progressive crescentic glomerulonephritis
data.description: IgA nephropathy is an immune-complex glomerular disease that commonly causes hematuria; rarely, extensive crescent formation causes rapidly progressive renal failure.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria with red blood cell casts
Rapidly progressive renal dysfunction can occur in crescentic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported episodic gross hematuria associated with upper respiratory or gastrointestinal infection
Severe constitutional symptoms and very rapid creatinine rise are less typical of uncomplicated IgA nephropathy

data.description: Glomerular inflammation following a bacterial infection, often streptococcal, that can produce hematuria, proteinuria, edema, hypertension, and occasionally rapidly progressive renal failure due to crescents.
symptoms_in_common: Hematuria with red blood cell casts
symptoms_not_in_common: No preceding skin, throat, or other infection is reported
Normal complement levels are less typical
The marked and rapidly progressive renal failure is less common in routine postinfectious glomerulonephritis

data.description: A 44-year-old man was hospitalized because of jaundice. Physical examination revealed normal findings except jaundice, and his past medical history was unremarkable. Complete blood count showed hemoglobin of 15 g/dL, white blood cell count of 8,200/μL with differential of 79% segmented neutrophils, 15% lymphocytes, 5% monocytes, and 1% eosinophils, and platelet count of 248,000/μL. Liver function test showed elevation of total bilirubin (15.3 mg/dL), direct bilirubin (9.4 mg/dL), and alkaline phosphatase (298 IU/L). Immunohistochemical stains showed tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen (CD 45) and negative for CD 3,4,5,8,10,21,23,56 and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy showed neither significant abnormalities nor evidence of myelodysplasia or leukemic infiltration.

data.diagnosis: Myeloid sarcoma (granulocytic sarcoma/chloroma) involving the extrahepatic bile duct
data.description: A localized tumor of immature myeloid cells that can occur outside the bone marrow, sometimes preceding or occurring without detectable acute myeloid leukemia. Rare involvement of the bile ducts can cause obstructive jaundice.
symptoms_in_common: Marked elevation of total and direct bilirubin
Elevated alkaline phosphatase indicating cholestatic biliary obstruction
Imaging appearance of an obstructing hilar/extrahepatic biliary lesion with biliary dilatation
Tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen (CD45)
Absence of bone marrow leukemic infiltration, which can occur in isolated myeloid sarcoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats were reported
No anemia, thrombocytopenia, or circulating blasts were present
No prior history of acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma of the bile duct
data.description: A lymphoma arising in or infiltrating the extrahepatic biliary tract can form a mass and produce obstructive jaundice. Most biliary lymphomas are B-cell lymphomas, although other hematolymphoid subtypes are possible.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Biliary hilar or extrahepatic duct mass on imaging
CD45 positivity supporting a hematolymphoid neoplasm
Normal blood counts and uninvolved bone marrow can occur in localized extranodal lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable lymphadenopathy was described
No fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss were reported
The reported tumor immunophenotype lacks typical T-cell markers and does not document a typical B-cell phenotype
No splenomegaly or other systemic lymphoma manifestations were reported

data.diagnosis: Cholangiocarcinoma (hilar or extrahepatic bile duct carcinoma)
data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the bile ducts that commonly presents with painless obstructive jaundice, cholestatic liver test abnormalities, and biliary ductal dilatation.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging evidence of biliary obstruction near the hepatic hilum/extrahepatic bile duct
symptoms_not_in_common: Tumor cells are CD45 positive, which is not typical of an epithelial cholangiocarcinoma
The tumor lacks the reported epithelial immunophenotypic characterization expected for cholangiocarcinoma
Histology appears to show infiltration by hematolymphoid-type cells rather than malignant biliary epithelial glands

data.diagnosis: Histiocytic sarcoma involving the biliary tract
data.description: A rare aggressive hematolymphoid malignancy composed of histiocytic cells. It is generally CD45 positive and often lacks B-cell, T-cell, and NK-cell markers; extranodal involvement can produce mass-related obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Negative reported T-cell markers including CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD8
Negative terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase, arguing against lymphoblastic neoplasia
Localized extranodal mass causing obstructive jaundice
Normal bone marrow can be seen with localized extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Biliary tract involvement is extremely uncommon
No systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats were reported
No hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, anemia, or thrombocytopenia was described

data.description: 65-year-old Haitian man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, bicuspid aortic valve with ascending and aortic-root aneurysm, prior positive tuberculin skin test with negative chest radiograph, treated secondary syphilis 11 years earlier, and recent HTLV-1 positivity. Presented with a leg injury and diffuse pruritic rash. He had 12 kg unintentional weight loss over 2 years. Exam showed bilateral wrinkled axillary plaques, multiple thin brown macules and patches with collarette of scale on the palms and some soles, and bilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy.

data.diagnosis: HTLV-1-associated adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL), cutaneous presentation
data.description: An aggressive mature CD4-positive T-cell neoplasm caused by HTLV-1 infection. It can present with pruritic papules, patches, plaques, erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, constitutional symptoms, and skin histology resembling cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Haitian/Caribbean origin, an endemic region for HTLV-1
symptoms_not_in_common: Palmar and plantar lesions with collarette scale are not the most classic ATLL morphology
Leg injury is unrelated
End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis is not a typical manifestation of ATLL
Aortic aneurysm and bicuspid aortic valve are unrelated

data.description: The most common primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, typically causing chronic pruritic patches and plaques that may progress to tumors, erythroderma, and lymph-node involvement. Histology often shows epidermotropism of atypical T lymphocytes.
symptoms_in_common: Plaques in flexural areas including the axillae
symptoms_not_in_common: HTLV-1 positivity more strongly raises concern for ATLL than classic mycosis fungoides
Palmar and plantar lesions with collarette scale are less typical
Leg injury is unrelated
End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis is not typical of mycosis fungoides

data.description: The disseminated stage of Treponema pallidum infection, classically producing a diffuse maculopapular or papulosquamous eruption involving the palms and soles, generalized lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Brown macules and patches with scale
Weight loss can occur with systemic infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior syphilis was reportedly treated 11 years earlier
Wrinkled axillary plaques are not classic for secondary syphilis
Long-standing diffuse pruritus is less typical because secondary syphilis lesions are often minimally pruritic or asymptomatic
HTLV-1 positivity does not specifically support syphilis
End-stage renal disease is unrelated

data.description: A severe infestation with Sarcoptes scabiei characterized by widespread hyperkeratotic, scaly, and often intensely pruritic plaques. It is more common in immunocompromised or chronically ill patients and may involve the palms, soles, and flexural regions.
symptoms_in_common: Scale on the palms and soles
Chronic severe medical illness with end-stage renal disease, which may predispose to severe infestation
symptoms_not_in_common: Brown macules and patches with collarette scale are not classic crusted-scabies lesions
Inguinal lymphadenopathy and marked weight loss are not typical primary manifestations
No burrows, widespread thick crusting, or household-contact symptoms are described
HTLV-1 positivity and the apparent lymphoproliferative histologic pattern would be unexplained

data.description: 80-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, coronary arteriosclerosis, congestive heart failure, hyperlipidemia, and gout was admitted with anorexia, weight loss, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. He had emigrated from Southeast Asia 22 years earlier. On examination, he appeared thin and chronically ill, with mild abdominal tenderness, posterior lower-lung crackles, and leg edema.

data.diagnosis: Intestinal tuberculosis with possible disseminated tuberculosis
data.description: Tuberculosis involving the gastrointestinal tract, most commonly the ileocecal region, sometimes accompanied by pulmonary or disseminated disease. It can cause chronic constitutional and abdominal symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Origin from Southeast Asia, an area with higher tuberculosis prevalence
Possible pulmonary findings with posterior lower-lung crackles
symptoms_not_in_common: Leg edema
Congestive heart failure
Peripheral arterial disease
Coronary arteriosclerosis

data.description: Cancer of the colon can produce progressive weight loss, anorexia, abdominal discomfort, altered bowel habits, and an obstructing or ulcerated lesion in the cecum or ascending colon.
symptoms_not_in_common: Southeast Asian origin
Posterior lower-lung crackles
Leg edema
Peripheral arterial disease
Gout

data.description: Insufficient intestinal blood flow due to severe atherosclerotic disease can cause postprandial abdominal pain, food avoidance, weight loss, diarrhea, and colonic ischemic injury.
symptoms_not_in_common: Southeast Asian origin
Posterior lower-lung crackles
Leg edema
Chronically ill appearance without stated postprandial pain

data.diagnosis: Abdominal aortic aneurysm with inflammatory involvement or impending complication
data.description: An abdominal aortic aneurysm is dilation of the abdominal aorta, usually caused by atherosclerosis. Large or inflammatory aneurysms may cause abdominal or back pain, constitutional symptoms, and may coexist with widespread vascular disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Diarrhea
Anorexia
Weight loss
Southeast Asian origin
Posterior lower-lung crackles
Leg edema

data.diagnosis: Gastrointestinal histoplasmosis or another disseminated fungal infection
data.description: Disseminated fungal infection can involve the lungs and gastrointestinal tract, producing chronic constitutional symptoms, abdominal pain, diarrhea, ulcerated intestinal lesions, and weight loss, especially in frail or immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Possible pulmonary findings with lower-lung crackles
Diabetes mellitus as a risk factor for severe infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Leg edema
Peripheral arterial disease
Coronary arteriosclerosis
Gout
Southeast Asian origin is less specifically associated than with tuberculosis
